`a0-implementation-dispatch` authorization. G2 failure leaves an active BTS but
no implementation authority and resumes idempotently. Ack loss observes the same
G1/G2 IDs. This post-admission rerun is a consistency predicate, not BTS
self-certification: BTS authority comes only from the external admission and the
operator decision remains independently signed. Product candidates may now be built and run in ordinary credentialless
development tests, but remain nonauthorizing, non-staging and non-installable
until their later exact scopes.

The round-ten signed decision predates G1 and therefore carries null
`bts_activation_id`, control generation and current program/run/lineage fields.
G2 never rewrites or “completes” it: the exact G1/G1b activation is attached as a
typed authorization evidence dependency while the decision's signed proposed
program/lineage IDs are preserved. A decision whose scope branch contains an
impossible post-created identity is invalid, even if that identity now exists.

The external registry has one mechanically enforced writer generation, not
merely a “sole authority” claim. Its stable lock inode is created on the private
local volume once and never unlinked/replaced; open uses no-follow semantics and
validates owner/mode/device/inode. The writer process itself retains the
exclusive kernel lock, each transaction includes exact admission/launch/writer
generation/fence/expected revision/root, and stale lock-file contents never
prove liveness:

| Registry-writer phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claimed` | exact BTS process/runtime/job is expected to hold stable lock; predecessor whole-job absence, admission, boot/host/volume and new generation/fence CAS are durable; endpoint unpublished | `reconcile-claimed-registry-writer-lifecycle` |
| `serving` | GO/endpoint receipt durable; ordinary fenced RPC servicing is enabled outside lifecycle recovery | `reconcile-serving-registry-writer-lifecycle` |
| `draining` | ingress/future privileged ops fenced; checkpoint/endpoint removal in progress while a live owner may still hold the lock | `reconcile-draining-registry-writer-lifecycle` |
| `exit-requested` | exact checkpoint and endpoint-absence receipts plus writer exit intent committed while the live writer still held the lock; actual exit/lock release not yet bound | `reconcile-exit-requested-registry-writer-lifecycle` |
| `exit-observed` | writer exited and endpoint absent; whole-job reap pending; a recovery-owned predecessor additionally requires its exact recovery attempt/generation settled before reap CAS | `reap-registry-writer-job` |
| `reaped` | whole job empty and lock released; immutable terminal launch | `claim-next-registry-writer-generation` |
| `quarantine-draining` | accepted compromise/invalidation fenced ingress/privilege; endpoint/checkpoint/exit cleanup owns the exact live job | `close-and-exit-quarantined-writer` |
| `quarantine-exit-observed` | endpoint absent and exit durable; whole-job reap pending | `reap-quarantined-registry-writer` |
| `quarantine-reaped` | whole job empty, lock released and authority epoch permanently quarantined | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | file/root/lock/boot/job/process/generation/fence identity diverged; ingress and guardian containment remain active | `contain-registry-writer-and-diagnose` |

Accepted compromise has a complete source-phase mapping in the same registry
sequence: `claimed`, `serving`, `draining`, `exit-requested` and any live/ambiguous
`manual-conflict` become `quarantine-draining`; `exit-observed` becomes
`quarantine-exit-observed`; `reaped` becomes `quarantine-reaped`. The transaction
also quarantines the registry head/authority epoch, increments the fence, denies
the endpoint and persists exact cleanup intent. A compromise racing
`claim-next-registry-writer-generation` is ordered by that transaction: compromise
first forbids the claim; claim first immediately quarantines the newly current
generation. No mapping reaches ordinary `reaped`, GO, serving or another claim.
External guardian kill/ingress containment is maintained even when identity is
ambiguous; failure to prove exit/reap preserves conflict evidence and never
restores authority.

Clients never receive filesystem write access. Every transaction holds that
lock, re-reads `(authorityEpoch, writerGeneration, revision, rootHash)`, validates
the exact caller capability, appends a transaction-chain entry and durably
commits database/WAL and directory before publishing the new head. Only one
current nonterminal writer launch is legal. Ordinary typed registry RPCs are
not RecoveryActions: they are admitted only while the row remains `serving` and
the exact writer holds the current lock/generation/fence. The four active-phase
reconcile actions have closed outcome-discriminated behavior. A live exact
`claimed` owner drives/observes only its existing G1b operation; an absent owner
dispatches the unique recovery attempt. A live exact `serving` owner/guardian/
endpoint leaves the phase unchanged; guardian loss with a live writer fences
ingress and enters `draining`; an absent owner dispatches the same recovery
protocol. A live exact `draining` owner drives/observes checkpoint/endpoint
removal and, while it still holds the lock, CASes the exact receipts plus exit
intent to `exit-requested`; it never claims that it has already exited. An absent
draining owner dispatches recovery. In `exit-requested`, a live exact owner is
allowed only to complete the committed exit intent; an absent owner dispatches
the unique recovery attempt, whose external observation binds actual exit.
Timeout/survivor or any process/job/endpoint/checkpoint/lock ambiguity enters
`manual-conflict`. None may jump directly to a successor generation.

For a dead source, `observe-and-bind-dead-writer-exit` in the effect-owning
recovery generation is the sole CAS owner from the exact intercepted
`claimed | serving | draining | exit-requested` phase to `exit-observed`. In one registry
transaction it validates the intercepted phase/revision, binds the source-phase,
process/job/endpoint/checkpoint observations, CASes the predecessor launch and
recovery attempt `observing -> exit-bound`, and records the effect-owning
generation/transaction. The active-phase reconcile actions only create, resume
or observe that attempt; they never execute a competing source-to-exit CAS.
Live G1b `claimed -> serving`, guardian-loss `serving -> draining`, and
checkpoint/endpoint/exit-intent `draining -> exit-requested` remain their
separate exact pre-exit transitions.

Before it is current, an exact admission-bound BTS process has only
`RegistryRecoveryAuthorityV1`. Each
`RegistryWriterRecoveryAttemptV1` binds predecessor launch, expected
head/generation/fence, intercepted writer phase/revision, intercepted GO/
endpoint and checkpoint-state hashes, source-phase observation, recovery
behavior/runtime policy, boot/host/volume,
current recovery generation, append-only generation count/root and one result
receipt. The predecessor launch has exactly one semantic recovery attempt for
all time; a conflict cannot be hidden with a new attempt. Each recovery generation separately binds its process/principal/job,
stable-lock acquisition, endpoint/whole-job observations and complete
reap/retirement proof. Lost acknowledgment resumes those rows.

If the disposable recovery owner dies, external supervision first reconciles
the exact registry transaction ID and whole job. An observed exit-bind is bound
once and that generation is reaped; a proven no-transaction/no-effect plus lock
release/job reap terminalizes it `no-effect-reaped` and permits one child
generation on the same semantic attempt. Ambiguity is sticky conflict. A child
cannot inherit a process, job or lock receipt. The attempt reaches `settled`
only after its effect-owning generation is fully reaped/retired; a writer launch
with a non-null recovery attempt cannot move `exit-observed -> reaped` before
that settlement. After a recovery-owned predecessor reaches
`exit-observed`, the existing `reap-registry-writer-job` then
`claim-next-registry-writer-generation` actions terminal-seal the predecessor
and CAS one higher generation/fence; recovery exposes no ordinary method.
Endpoint publication occurs only after the later claim commits. The writer
itself holds the lock; its independent guardian owns a kill-on-close job/control
pipe. Guardian loss closes ingress, fences privilege and forces a live writer
through `serving -> draining -> exit-requested`; after actual process exit, only
the recovery-owned observation transaction enters `exit-observed`, followed by
`reaped`. An already absent
writer uses the recovery-attempt transition above and then the same
`exit-observed -> reaped` suffix;
failure to prove drain/reap is conflict, never an unsupervised serving writer.
Old-generation requests fail their fence. A platform without the
stable local lock, blocked child, job-reap and boot/host/volume identity proof is
bootstrap unsupported/read-only. Hidden revocations have no observable order:
accepted registry sequence is authoritative, and a later-disclosed compromise
can quarantine the current epoch but cannot backdate or rewrite a final seal.

G1b publication, G2 import/authorization and every writer recovery claim CAS the
current revocation head and revalidate the program admission plus root admission/
materialization currentness. An accepted pre-seal compromise atomically marks the
activation/writer launch quarantined, fences endpoint/transactions and persists
the exact reap intent. Recovery may reap it but cannot claim or publish another
generation in that authority epoch; a quarantine-recovery authority exposes only
the same checkpoint/endpoint-close/exit/reap actions and cannot sign an ordinary
transaction, generation, GO or endpoint. A new offline admission is required.

Control-bundle distribution is an immutable packed artifact plus manifest. The
first bundle is built from the exact A0 implementation tree—not from the earlier
planning snapshot—and can be installed only through the predeclared
`a0-trust-control-install` bootstrap slot after external conformance succeeds
and the bootstrap plus independent human keys bind its exact tree, artifact,
manifest, reproducible-build provenance, component/runtime inventory,
conformance report and a fresh detached
four-perspective external code-review manifest produced by the frozen
round-ten governance rules with zero CRITICAL/P1. The plan-approval bundle
freezes the control coordinator, disposable install-executor and staging
contracts/threat profiles, not their future executable bytes. During A0
implementation the exact unprivileged permanent control coordinator, disposable
install executor and staging runner/oracle are built as separate bootstrap-TCB
candidates. Before any A0 target byte is executed, a
`bootstrap-tcb-authorization` review freezes only their exact source/artifact/
runtime closures, the exact candidate A0 tree/artifact identity, sandbox and
principal policies, and the already frozen inert escape/oracle plus disposable
install fixture definitions;
it requires no live candidate-produced observation, but does require the same
four perspectives, both auditors and a fresh operator
signature with scope `bootstrap-tcb-staging-execution`. The activated bootstrap
trust service's reviewed generic qualification adapter then launches those exact TCB
artifacts from a protected external bootstrap root under a credentialless
staging principal through the durable child-launch protocol below. External
instrumentation—not the under-review oracle—first runs and judges the inert
fixtures. It proves complete reap/destruction, then runs the exact control/
executor behavior against disposable fake registry/install roots under a
qualification-install principal with production-equivalent policy shape but
zero production access. After another complete reap/destruction, a third fresh
TCB process and namespace may run one exact A0 target. Only if all three stages
pass may the
external receipt sealer emit
a signed
`staging_launch_receipt` binding the TCB authorization/artifacts, sandbox/
principal, context execution root, scoped behavior-outcome root, target tree/artifact, all three raw
observation sets and verified absence of install/registry/pointer effects. The
TCB cannot reserve an install
slot, switch a pointer or activate a service because the staging principal lacks
those capabilities and registry ACLs reject it. A later
`a0-artifact-authorization` freezes the exact A0 tree/artifact plus the complete
staging history, raw reports and TCB hashes and requires four new reviews,
dual-auditor agreement and operator scope `a0-merge-install`. Every qualification
process set/namespace is already sealed and reaped and none is promoted.

Installation uses three disjoint OS principals. The permanent control
coordinator may sequence registry requests but has no install-root, pointer,
registry-writer or target-serving capability. A disposable install executor
receives only one installation/action/fence capability. The target service
principal becomes eligible only after the external final seal. A process that
ever held install capability can never become, replace or share an identity/job
with the permanent unprivileged control coordinator or target service. This is
mechanical: BTS allocates a random, epoch-bound `principal_instance_id`, exact
OS job/cgroup/SID/UID-token tuple and role before spawn, stores it in an
append-only principal ledger, and permanently retires it after reap. Process-start
identity plus capability audience—not a reusable numeric PID/UID alone—is the
identity. A retired install/qualification instance cannot be presented for
control or target launch even after reboot.

The exact merge/install authorization is consumed only in the external
transaction that reserves the two-key slot, creates the exact
`qualification-pending` installation and reserves one qualification launch; it
does not arm a production executor. Before every production executor generation,
BTS-0 drives that one-use qualification child under the same launcher, platform
cell and principal-policy template, but with closed equal-shape decoy handles;
production registry, roots, keys and pointer are unreachable. Its hidden/frozen
fault vector, continuous effect audit, no-production-effect proof, whole-job
reap and namespace destruction must PASS. Only then is a different fresh process
and principal instance armed with a policy attestation that is byte-identical
except for one closed resource-audience substitution from decoy IDs to the exact
installation IDs. The qualification terminal-bind transaction records PASS/reap,
retires its principal and moves the installation to `qualification-bound`.
Exactly one later expected-revision CAS creates a different executor principal/
launch and moves the installation to `prepared`; reusing or promoting the
qualification child is forbidden.

External observation begins before either namespace/job is created. For the
production executor it covers every process/descendant, registry call, file and
pointer effect including write-then-restore, network denial, capability/session
revocation, exit, whole-job reap and namespace destruction. No unsupported
ambient authority or audit gap can be repaired by a final snapshot. The stream
has append-only ordered events/checkpoints and phases `armed | recording |
gap-conflict | sealed`; observer restart must resume the same OS event source and
sequence or make the installation sticky conflict. The executor
must exit, be completely reaped, and have its effect-audit stream sealed before
the registry may bind the installation; a new executor generation repeats
qualification. No target-bundle component verifies, installs or activates
itself. The install executor sequences one capability-scoped broker action; only
the guard's broker principal opens the target path, extracts and independently
verifies artifact, manifest and every file hash into a new content-addressed
directory, fsyncs it, then the executor sequences the protected
current pointer. The protected install tree remains owned by the BTS install
broker, invisible to the target principal and mounted/non-executable outside a
launcher-created service job. A pointer is data, not an executable path. Partial
or pre-seal extraction therefore cannot be executed even by direct path lookup;
rollback selects a previously pinned directory by signed manifest. Platforms lacking external
gap-free effect/process audit, isolated capability injection or whole-job reap
are first-install unsupported/read-only.

| Install-effect audit phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `armed` | exact owner/backend/source/policy/start cursor frozen before namespace/child | `start-install-effect-audit-recording` |
| `recording` | continuous process/registry/effect events and checkpoints append under one source cursor | `resume-install-effect-audit` |
| `gap-conflict` | source/owner/event/checkpoint continuity diverged; containment remains active | `diagnose-only` |
| `sealed` | complete terminal event/checkpoint/raw inventory and cleanup receipts immutable | `noop` |

A separate target-denial observer reservation is created in the installation-
creation transaction. Its external `reserved -> recording` arm is then observed
and bound before any qualification, executor or materialization effect; the
installation cannot advance without that exact coverage-start receipt. It covers install-tree opens/execs,
target-principal allocations, executable mounts, target-launch rows and serving
endpoints until the final-seal transaction freezes its continuous root. Missing
coverage or any attempted target exec is terminal conflict; “target not running
now” is never accepted as proof of no earlier execution.

The observer is backed by qualified `TargetExecutionGuardV1`, not a file mode or
snapshot. It binds the target generation/inventory/future content-addressed path,
broker principal, OS backend/source/boot identity and blocks every non-broker
read/open, interpreter input, executable mapping/exec, target-principal grant,
mount, launch and serving endpoint. Its phases are `reserved | arming |
recording | freeze-barrier | seal-bound-guarding | released-to-launch |
cancellation-barrier | cancelled | gap-conflict`. Immediately before final
bind it enters `freeze-barrier`, prevents new accesses while draining the OS
source to an exact cursor and continues enforcement through the registry
transaction. Rollback resumes the same barrier/stream; commit freezes the
pre-seal prefix but keeps the guard enforcing and recording. Release occurs
exactly once, for launch generation one, only after its target-launch audit has
overlapping source coverage and binds an exact no-gap/no-attempt handoff receipt.
Later restarts inherit this immutable pre-seal proof and instead bind the
terminal parent launch's service-closure/audit seal before their own observer can
create a namespace. A platform that cannot enforce interpreter reads as
well as direct exec, or cannot prove continuous source order, is unsupported for
installation.

A failed installation cannot strand this observer. A terminalizing install
repair maps `reserved` directly to `cancelled` only with a proof that no observer,
broker or target principal was armed. It maps `arming | recording |
freeze-barrier` to `cancellation-barrier`, keeps all denial active, drains and
seals the exact source suffix, proves no target execution/mount/endpoint,
retires every observer/broker principal and then reaches `cancelled`.
The owned denial stream moves `reserved -> cancelled` with the same absence
proof or `recording -> cancellation-draining -> cancelled` with the same source
cursor/root; the two terminal receipts bind atomically.
`seal-bound-guarding | released-to-launch` are ineligible for pre-seal repair;
`gap-conflict` cannot be cancelled from a snapshot. A repair may not bind its
installation disposition until the owned guard and denial stream are terminal.
Repair creation, installation action fencing and this source-phase mapping are
one registry transaction; no persisted repair owner coexists with an old guard
phase. If ordinary arm/freeze wins its CAS first, repair remaps the newly
observed phase or rejects. Recovery therefore still has exactly the one action
shown for every persisted guard phase.

The guard freezes a closed access matrix. The broker principal alone may create,
write, reopen/hash and fsync the target tree for the exact materialize action;
the install executor may read the approved source artifact and call that one
broker action but cannot open the target tree; control/reviewer principals have
no target access; the target principal has none before seal and receives only the
seal/launch-scoped read/execute mount afterward. Each allowed broker access is
also an event in the guard stream and must match the materialization inventory;
an undeclared read/write is conflict.

| Target guard phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | guard ID, installation/generation/inventory/path, broker principal, access matrix, backend/source and stream IDs frozen; no coverage | `arm-target-execution-guard` |
| `arming` | external observer/backend arm intent durable | `observe-target-execution-guard-arm` |
| `recording` | continuous enforcement/source cursor bound; install may qualify/materialize through broker | `advance-install-until-guard-freeze` |
| `freeze-barrier` | new pre-seal accesses blocked and exact source cursor drained; enforcement continues | `bind-control-bundle-install-final-seal` |
| `seal-bound-guarding` | final seal binds the frozen pre-seal prefix; guard still denies and records every access | `arm-target-launch-audit-and-handoff-guard` |
| `released-to-launch` | launch-one audit overlaps the guard source and exact handoff cursor proves no suffix attempt; immutable one-use guard release is terminal | `noop` |
| `cancellation-barrier` | terminal repair owns the still-denying guard; exact source suffix, absence and principal cleanup remain | `drain-and-cancel-target-execution-guard` |
| `cancelled` | complete no-target-exec/audit/cleanup receipts bind the failed installation repair; no launch release exists | `noop` |
| `gap-conflict` | source, access matrix, broker, path or cursor diverged | `diagnose-only` |

Every target generation—not only the governance validator/coordinator—must
prove reviewed source equals executable behavior. It either executes the exact
reviewed source under a fully hashed interpreter/loader/dependency closure, or
two isolated builds produce a bit-for-bit identical packed artifact while
binding recipe, toolchain, flags, base image, SBOM and runtime closure. The fresh
implementation reviewers receive source, build provenance, artifact inventory
and runtime closure; BTS-0 independently revalidates all hashes before reserving
an install, while the unprivileged coordinator only requests sequencing. A
source/artifact pair with no such proof is ineligible for
first or successor authorization even if conformance is green.

Bundle activation is a durable saga in BTS-0's protected external trust registry,
not process memory. That registry remains sole authority for bundle generations,
installation phases, authorizations and the protected current pointer before and
after A0. The permanent control coordinator can request only closed sequencing
operations; the disposable executor can present only the exact per-action
capability; neither can write registry storage or invoke the other's method set.
BTS-0 owns launch/supervision, authorization predicates and final bind but never
executes target/install code. StateKernel stores only a hash-bound read-only
anchor/projection and fails closed on disagreement. The installation phases are:

| Install phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qualification-pending` | slot/materialization/installation, target-denial reservation and executor-generation one frozen; no production principal/launch | `resume-install-qualification-pending` |
| `qualification-bound` | current executor generation has sticky PASS, audit, whole-job reap/namespace seal and retired qualification principal bound | `arm-qualified-install-executor` |
| `prepared` | exact reserved slot/materialization, artifact/runtime closure, old pointer/generation, new generation and executor policy frozen | `resume-control-bundle-quiesce` |
| `quiesced` | old service generation denies new capabilities and every old service instance/operation is fenced, closed and reaped; the unprivileged coordinator remains; first install has none | `resume-control-bundle-materialize` |
| `materialized` | complete target inventory verified and directory-fsynced; pointer still exact old | `resume-control-bundle-pointer-cas` |
| `pointer-updated` | protected pointer equals exact target; target remains ineligible; current executor must stop and seal audit | `settle-install-executor` |
| `executor-reaped` | every executor generation is terminal, exact production executor and descendants are reaped, capability/session revoked, complete audit sealed; target still cannot serve | `bind-control-bundle-install-final-seal` |
| `bound` | one final seal atomically binds registry generation, slot, authorization lineage and all histories; only now may target launch | `noop` |
| `aborted` | repair permanently cancelled this successor installation and, when required, restored predecessor eligibility through a fresh launch | `noop` |
| `superseded` | failed installation is permanently linked to an independently authorized successor | `noop` |
| `tombstoned` | failed installation/materialization/authority is permanently ineligible with no successor bound here | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | pointer, inventory, generation, fence, qualification, audit or slot identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

The installation effect phase and executor lifecycle are orthogonal. Every
production generation first creates one durable `install_executor_generation`
with phases `qualification-reserved | qualifying | qualified | launch-armed |
running | settling | reaped | failed | manual-conflict`. It binds its predecessor,
generation number, exact executor behavior/runtime/policy/fault/context
equivalence, qualification and launch IDs, principal allocation, history
count/root and generation fence. A replacement generation can be claimed only
after the predecessor is terminal, its job/capability/session is proved empty,
and prior action effects are bound; the installation remains at its last durable
effect phase. A qualification FAIL is sticky for its equivalence hash and cannot
be resampled by changing nonce/generation. A prior PASS is not a reusable
qualification receipt: after the passed generation's production executor fully
terminates with work remaining, its child generation may run one fresh
qualification under the same equivalence. That is crash recovery, not verdict
selection. A sticky negative for the stable registry/project/checkout plus
equivalence key blocks every later generation and authorization; authority is
retained only as failure provenance. It cannot be invalidated back to eligible—a
compromise may only add a stronger quarantine. Only materially changed executor/
context bytes under a fresh applicable A0/update authority produce another
equivalence. Each qualification ID owns exactly one immutable launch row/child;
pre-execution infrastructure loss resumes that row and cannot allocate a second
launch generation or sample. A semantic qualification FAIL atomically records
the terminal generation/history and moves that installation to
`manual-conflict`; `resume-same-object` and `abort-to-old` may not re-enter
qualification. Only `supersede-with-new-authority` plus a materially changed,
freshly authorized successor may continue.

| Install-executor generation phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qualification-reserved` | generation/parent/equivalence and unique qualification ID frozen; no qualification child | `resume-generation-qualification-reservation` |
| `qualifying` | exact one-row qualification launch owns the generation | `resume-current-generation-qualification` |
| `qualified` | fresh PASS/audit/reap/retirement bound; no production launch | `arm-generation-production-launch` |
| `launch-armed` | exact production launch/principal/job/audit/GO identities frozen | `resume-generation-production-launch` |
| `running` | exact launch may execute only the current install action | `resume-generation-install-work` |
| `settling` | no new action; capability/session revoke, exit/reap and audit seal pending | `settle-generation-audit-and-reap` |
| `reaped` | whole generation terminal and immutable | `noop` |
| `failed` | sticky semantic qualification/launch failure terminal | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | generation/parent/qualification/launch/action/audit identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

Qualification and production execution are separate nested aggregates. The
qualification result is only a summary over one durable
`install_qualification_launch`:

| Qualification-launch phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | exact installation/generation, decoy policy, principal instance, job/namespace/observer/spawn/GO identities allocated; no child | `arm-install-qualification-observer` |
| `armed` | observer coverage predates namespace; blocked-child gate and decoy-only handle policy durable | `start-blocked-install-qualification` |
| `child-registered` | exact blocked child/job/runtime durable; no decoy handle/GO, production objects absent | `commit-install-qualification-go` |
| `running` | decoy grant/GO consumption durable; exact child executes fault vector | `observe-install-qualification` |
| `exit-observed` | complete effect/process stream and exit durable | `reap-install-qualification-job` |
| `reaped` | job empty, namespace destroyed, principal retired and audit sealed | `bind-install-qualification-outcome` |
| `passed` | immutable terminal PASS references full launch/audit root | `noop` |
| `failed` | immutable terminal FAIL references full launch/audit root and stable negative head | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | spawn/GO/job/process/effect/reap/audience identity ambiguous | `diagnose-only` |

Spawn-before-registration, GO and exit/reap lost acknowledgments recover only
this row; no terminal ambiguity can arm production. A production
`install_executor_launch` then moves as follows:

| Executor-launch phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `armed` | exact installation/materialization/A0 authorization, fresh passed qualification, executor bytes/runtime, production principal instance, launch generation/fences, job/namespace, observer, GO nonce and one-use start capability are allocated; no child effect | `start-fresh-install-executor` |
| `child-registered` | one exact blocked child is durably owned; observer coverage predates namespace; no production handle or GO is usable | `release-install-executor-go` |
| `running` | exact qualification-policy equivalence and resource-audience substitution are attested; GO/capability result binds the child/session | `drive-exact-install-action` |
| `exit-observed` | immutable exit plus effect/process/registry stream is complete; capability/session fenced | `reap-install-executor-job` |
| `reaped` | whole job empty, namespace destroyed and audit seal bound; process can never resume | `resume-installation-phase-after-executor-reap` |
| `manual-conflict` | child/job/policy/audience/capability/session/fence/audit identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

Each external install/repair effect is also one durable `install_action_intent`;
a running executor is not authority to choose a phase:

An action also has a monotonic `action_generation` and predecessor. Recovery
normally completes the same semantic intent. It may allocate a successor action
generation on that same intent only when
an externally sealed no-capability-consumption/no-effect proof terminalizes the
predecessor; otherwise the observed old effect is bound once or the installation
enters conflict. A partial unique index permits one nonterminal intent for an
installation/action/expected revision, so executor replacement cannot duplicate
an effect. A new semantic intent is legal only for a distinct installation/action/
expected-revision identity, never as recovery of the old action.

| Semantic install-intent phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | exact installation phase/revision, semantic action, resource audience and expected before/after identity frozen; one current generation | `drive-current-install-action-generation` |
| `executing` | current generation consumed capability or may have an effect | `settle-current-install-action-generation` |
| `effect-bound` | exact effect/no-effect and ordered audit range bound | `bind-install-phase-cas` |
| `phase-bound` | installation CAS and action result commit together | `settle-install-action` |
| `settled` | immutable action may share its still-running executor with the next preallocated action; later launch reap is a separate history event | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | phase/revision/audience/effect/audit cannot be uniquely reconciled | `diagnose-only` |

| Install action-generation phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | exact executor generation/launch, capability nonce and audit start frozen | `consume-install-action-capability` |
| `capability-consumed` | exact child/session/nonce result durable; effect may be absent or unacknowledged | `perform-or-observe-exact-install-effect` |
| `effect-observed` | exact effect/no-effect and audit end durable; semantic intent moves `effect-bound` | `bind-semantic-install-intent` |
| `transferred-no-effect` | sealed no-consume/no-effect/reap proof permits one child generation; semantic intent remains `prepared` | `noop` |
| `settled` | semantic intent/installation phase bound; generation immutable | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | capability/effect/audit/owner ambiguous | `diagnose-only` |

Action kinds are a closed union for quiesce, materialize, pointer CAS,
abort/restore and executor settle; qualification binding remains in its own
aggregate. Effect-before-phase-CAS recovery
reads the action's exact observer range; it never infers an action from the
current pointer alone.

The reviewed launcher/OS enforces the blocked boundary before executor user code.
Before GO it inherits no production handle, secret, ambient authority or
privileged IPC. BTS-0 persists GO and capability consumption before release; an
acknowledgment loss redelivers the same result to the same child. Each install
action receives a separate nonce-bound capability for the exact installation,
action, resource audience, generation and fence. The unprivileged control
coordinator cannot mint a launch/capability or widen a session, and the executor
cannot create another launch or write an unrelated registry object.

If an executor exits before the installation reaches `executor-reaped`, recovery
first seals the same external stream, revokes the session and proves the whole
job empty. A complete stream may bind an already durable filesystem/pointer
effect once. If another action remains, a higher production generation is legal
only through the orthogonal generation aggregate after a fresh qualification
launch and must observe prior durable effects;
it never blindly repeats them. Spawn-before-registration, GO lost-ack, effect-
before-phase-CAS and exit lost-ack remain distinguishable. PID reuse, executable/
job mismatch, audit gap, survivor or ambiguous reboot is `manual-conflict`.
Every qualification, action, executor generation/launch, audit checkpoint/outcome and
principal allocation/retirement appends by expected-count/root/revision CAS to one
installation execution-history count/root.
No “current launch” pointer can hide an older generation; final review, repair
and seal enumerate the entire root.

Every action revalidates materialization, expected old/target hashes, program/
run/behavior/context, current executor and qualification identities, complete
authorization lineage and the current registry revocation head. Registry
sequence—not wall clock or claimed issue time—orders revocation versus final
seal. Revoke-first blocks bind; seal-first preserves immutable history while a
later compromise fact quarantines future activity. The pointer never grants
authority by itself.

At `executor-reaped`, BTS-0 executes one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
`bind-control-bundle-install-final-seal` transaction using its protected
local epoch seal key; external HSM round trips are unsupported in v1. It
revalidates current writer admission/generation/fence/lock, pointer/inventory/
artifact/runtime, the exact seal-kind authorization branch and all of its
typed dependencies/consumers and retained raw evidence. First install additionally
revalidates program/run, complete candidate/budget history and frozen staging/
applicability/execution/outcome roots; successor update instead revalidates the
predecessor service closure, successor candidate policy/program/global-
equivalence/complete-history freeze, update/review/approval/source-build/conformance/
exact-cell qualification branch. Both revalidate the current qualification,
the complete installation generation/qualification/action/executor/audit and
principal-allocation/retirement roots plus every repair owner/approval/mode/
tombstone/successor-link/history root,
executor audit/reap/capability revocation, a gap-free frozen
`no-target-exec-before-seal` process/capability audit prefix plus the still-
enforcing guard/fence, an empty target-launch
ledger scoped to this exact `(installation,target generation)` (not prior
generations), and the exact revocation head. It
inserts one `ControlBundleInstallFinalSealV1` and atomically terminal-seals authorizations/consumers/
dependencies and exactly the predecessor-plus-final signing-operation manifest;
the later historical-anchor signing operation is not and cannot be an input to
that manifest. It terminal-binds materialization and installation;
for first install it also closes the selected run/program and staging receipt/
histories/slot, while successor closes the update authorization and predecessor
handoff; then it marks the target control
generation `launch-eligible` but not `serving`;
marks every executor reaped/terminal; for `first-install` only, it also seals the
bootstrap review-root admission/materialization, changes the BTS program
admission to `first-install-sealed`. For `first-install` only, after computing
the final-seal envelope inside the same transaction it creates the separate
historical anchor described immediately below; `successor-update` stops at its
generic final-seal envelope and creates no bootstrap historical anchor. Any
failed CAS rolls the entire transaction back at
`executor-reaped`; ack loss returns the same seal. Only a target launcher that
reads and verifies that seal may start the new bundle.

Final-seal signing is also acyclic. `ControlBundleInstallFinalSealStatementV1`
contains the complete content and every predecessor receipt-signing operation/
dependency root, plus the preallocated final signer/key dependency and operation
ID, but not its own object hash, result or signature. The synchronous registry
operation signs that statement hash. `ControlBundleInstallFinalSealEnvelopeV1`
then wraps the statement, final signing-operation receipt and signature. The
authoritative seal ID is the envelope hash; validators enumerate the predecessor
root plus the one final operation as the complete signing manifest. Neither the
statement nor final operation references the envelope hash it creates.

First-install historical anchoring is the next acyclic layer, not an input to
the final-seal statement. `BootstrapHistoricalAnchorStatementV1` references the
already computed final-seal envelope ID and enumerates the retained bootstrap
descriptor/admission/materialization, program admission, activation, review/
authorization and history facts; it contains no anchor envelope/result/signature.
A dedicated local signing operation produces
`BootstrapHistoricalAnchorEnvelopeV1`, whose hash is the historical anchor ID.
The one registry transaction computes final-seal statement → final-seal envelope
→ historical-anchor statement → historical-anchor envelope, then updates the
registry head with both IDs. Any step failure rolls back all rows. These records
are distinct from `sealed_bootstrap_anchors` used by bootstrap target sagas.

Target start is a separate durable `control_bundle_target_launch`, never an
implicit consequence of a pointer. The current seal-bound target launcher verifies the
seal, allocates a fresh target principal/job and blocked child while the install
tree is still broker-only, persists the exact read/execute mount grant and
seal-bound GO, then exposes the reviewed bundle through that job and releases
the same registered child. Phases are `reserved | observer-armed |
  coverage-handoff-bound |
child-registered | mount-authorized | go-committed | first-exec-observed |
  serving-endpoint-blocked | serving-release-committed |
  serving-activation-committed | serving | pre-serving-exit-observed | exit-observed |
access-revoked | endpoint-closed | unmounted | job-reaped | audit-sealed |
  reaped | manual-conflict`. First exec cannot open a serving endpoint. After
first-exec/runtime observation, the broker reserves an externally blocked
endpoint and BTS durably commits a broker-held, nondeliverable generation-scoped
serving release/capability while the generation remains `launch-eligible`. After
the broker's exact blocked-endpoint/readiness receipt, one registry transaction
creates the activation and changes the generation to `serving`; only then can the
broker's ingress/reply predicate consume the release. A final external visibility
observation moves the launch to `serving`. Every ingress and reply independently
requires the exact generation to be `serving`, the activation to be `current`
and both fences to match, so no service is possible in the release-ack window.
Pre-seal
there is no grant/row/mount and the external audit records/denies any direct exec;
post-seal ack loss resumes the same launch. Disk divergence requires
a dedicated two-key `control_bundle_install_repairs` authorization, never an
informal retry or another candidate.

| Target-launch phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | exact seal/generation/parent/artifact/runtime/command/env, fresh principal/job/namespace, audit stream, spawn/GO and revocation fence reserved; no child | `arm-target-launch-observer` |
| `observer-armed` | launch audit source coverage active before namespace/child; launch-one guard or restart parent closure remains authoritative | `bind-target-launch-coverage-handoff` |
| `coverage-handoff-bound` | launch one has guard overlap/no-attempt receipt; a restart has exact terminal parent service-closure/audit-seal/absence proof; no namespace yet | `start-blocked-target-child` |
| `child-registered` | exact blocked child/process/job durable; no mount or GO | `authorize-target-mount` |
| `mount-authorized` | exact seal-bound read/execute mount receipt durable; child blocked | `commit-target-launch-go` |
| `go-committed` | one-use GO result durable; delivery/first-exec may be unacknowledged | `observe-target-first-exec-or-exit` |
| `first-exec-observed` | exact runtime/process/mount observation bound; no endpoint | `reserve-blocked-serving-endpoint` |
| `serving-endpoint-blocked` | exact endpoint listener/identity exists but ingress/replies are kernel-blocked; no deliverable serving capability | `prepare-target-serving-release` |
| `serving-release-committed` | broker-held one-use release plus blocked-endpoint/readiness receipt durable; generation still launch-eligible and replies forbidden | `commit-target-serving-activation` |
| `serving-activation-committed` | generation serving and exact activation current; broker may consume the release, but visibility acknowledgment may be lost | `observe-target-serving-visibility-or-exit` |
| `serving` | activation/capability/endpoint current under exact revocation head | `observe-target-exit` |
| `pre-serving-exit-observed` | child exited before a current activation; exact never-served plus endpoint/session/mount presence-or-absence receipts bound | `revoke-target-access` |
| `exit-observed` | exit durable; cleanup has not been inferred | `revoke-target-access` |
| `access-revoked` | start/serving/session capabilities revoked and ingress fence durable | `close-target-serving-endpoint` |
| `endpoint-closed` | exact endpoint absence/close receipt durable | `unmount-target-install-tree` |
| `unmounted` | exact mount absence/unmount receipt durable | `reap-target-job` |
| `job-reaped` | whole job empty; namespace/audit seal pending | `seal-target-namespace-and-audit` |
| `audit-sealed` | namespace destroyed and complete audit root sealed | `retire-target-principal-and-terminalize-activation` |
| `reaped` | one transaction bound principal retirement/service closure/launch history, terminalized activation and reopened generation eligibility | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | source/process/job/mount/session/endpoint/revocation identity ambiguous | `start-or-resume-target-launch-invalidation` |

Every action from `child-registered` through `serving-release-committed` is an
outcome-discriminated observation: an externally observed exit atomically enters
`pre-serving-exit-observed`, records `never-served`, and skips activation
creation. Presence-or-absence receipts let the same cleanup phases close a mount,
session or endpoint that was never created. Exit after activation commit enters
`exit-observed` and marks the activation `draining`; process exit alone never
terminalizes it.

External target-launch observation begins before namespace creation and covers
process/job, mount, session/capability, endpoint, exec/exit and cleanup with the
same gap-conflict/checkpoint rules as install audit. Every phase transition and
GO/serving delivery revalidates current control generation, final seal,
revocation dependency/head and launch fence. A post-seal compromise transaction
atomically invalidates/fences every nonterminal launch/activation, revokes any
committed start/serving capability and persists its exact reap intent. Recovery
may only settle/reap that invalidated child; it cannot redeliver GO or reach
serving.

Invalidation owns an orthogonal durable cleanup aggregate, so it never dispatches
the ordinary action of the interrupted phase. Creation atomically sets
`active_invalidation_id`, increments generation/launch/activation fences, denies
endpoint ingress and future broker calls and persists the guardian kill/reap
intent. While it is non-null all ordinary launch actions are rejected:

| Target-launch invalidation phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fenced` | logical generation/activation/launch invalidation, capability revocation, ingress denial and exact kill/reap intent durable | `observe-invalidated-target-exit` |
| `child-exit-observed` | exact exit or never-created/absent-child receipt durable | `close-invalidated-target-endpoint` |
| `endpoint-closed` | endpoint/session absence and access-revocation receipts durable | `unmount-invalidated-target-tree` |
| `unmounted` | exact mount absence receipt durable | `reap-invalidated-target-job` |
| `job-reaped` | whole job empty and namespace destruction receipt durable | `seal-invalidated-target-audit` |
| `audit-sealed` | complete launch audit and cleanup receipt root sealed | `retire-invalidated-target-principal` |
| `bound` | principal retirement, service closure and invalidation terminal bound | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | identity/audit ambiguity retained while kernel ingress fence and guardian containment remain active | `maintain-target-containment-and-diagnose` |

The same presence-or-absence receipts work from every interrupted launch phase.
A conflict may delay proof, but cannot restore GO/serving or disable external
containment.

The launch audit stream has its own closed dispatcher: `reserved ->
arm-target-launch-audit`, `recording -> resume-target-launch-observation`,
`draining -> drain-and-seal-target-launch-audit`, `sealed -> noop`, and
`gap-conflict -> diagnose-only`. It is `recording` before namespace creation,
may enter `draining` only after whole-job reap, and seals only after enumerating
all events/checkpoints and cleanup receipts.

Each launch binds a monotonic launch generation/parent, exact target artifact and
runtime/loader closure, launcher/command/environment profile, principal
allocation, supervision job, namespace, spawn and GO receipts, scoped session,
mount/unmount, endpoint, audit and retirement receipts. A target restart is not
another installation: after exit, the durable cleanup phases `access-revoked ->
endpoint-closed -> unmounted -> job-reaped -> audit-sealed -> reaped` observe and
bind each revoke/close/unmount/reap/seal/retire effect separately; no step infers
the next one from a final snapshot. Only after `reaped` may the still-current
sealed bundle generation return to
`launch-eligible` and reserve `launch_generation + 1` pointing to that parent.
Each serving transition creates the exact current `control_bundle_activation`;
process exit moves it to `draining`. The same transaction that binds launch
`reaped`, its complete service-closure root and generation history terminalizes
the activation as `closed-after-exit` and returns the generation to
`launch-eligible`; an intermediate reaped-launch/current-activation state is
impossible. Successor review authority therefore
always binds the live launch rather than a generation label alone. The launch
schema has a closed `oneOf`: generation one requires the one-use target-guard
handoff and a null parent; every later generation requires the exact terminal
parent service-closure root, audit seal and absence receipt and may only
reference the inherited guard as history, never consume it again. One
nonterminal launch per target generation is enforced. A survivor, audit gap,
live endpoint/session/mount or unretired principal makes restart conflict.

The control generation and activation, not only a launch snapshot, own the
serving capability fence and revocation dependency closure. Every endpoint
ingress, serving capability use, mount-broker request and phase action resolves
that dependency against the current revocation head. It does not require the
current head to equal an older admitted head—unrelated facts may advance it—but
any accepted fact in this dependency closure makes the predicate false. A
compromise commits generation quarantine/fence increment, launch/activation
invalidation, endpoint denial and exact reap intents in the same transaction.

Activation recovery is closed independently of target-launch phase:

| Control-bundle activation state | Unique recovery action |
| --- | --- |
| `current` | `observe-current-control-bundle-activation` |
| `handoff-reserved` | `resume-owned-predecessor-handoff` |
| `draining` | `resume-activation-service-closure` |
| `closed-by-this-installation` | `noop` |
| `closed-after-exit` | `noop` |
| `invalidated` | `resume-target-launch-invalidation` |
| `manual-conflict` | `maintain-target-containment-and-diagnose` |

`current` may carry one pending `current-bound` handoff without changing its
activation RecoveryAction or ingress predicate; the handoff aggregate alone may
execute the atomic fence. `handoff-reserved` is reachable only in that fence
transaction and therefore always has the same exact fenced handoff owner.
`closed-by-this-installation` simultaneously moves its generation to
`handoff-closed`; no generic activation recovery can make that generation
launch-eligible.

The plan-governance bundle contains the immutable staging-runner/oracle contract,
expected-state model, sandbox profile and adversarial qualification vectors.
The later bootstrap-TCB authorization contains their exact implementation
source/artifact/runtime closure. Under each exact-target staging authorization,
the runner executes only that authorization's one untrusted A0/A1/C0/successor
artifact under a separate OS
principal or equivalent capability boundary and denies the coordinator/registry,
keys, state/install roots, privileged IPC, HOME, network, host Git common-dir and
parent paths. The coordinator never imports target code. It supplies inputs,
kill schedule and expected WAL/FK/CAS/rollback outcomes from outside the SUT and
records raw OS/filesystem/process observations; target-provided harness/results
are untrusted diagnostics only. Round ten reviews and qualifies this runner/
oracle/sandbox specification without executing future candidate code. The
bootstrap-TCB authorization statically reviews the exact runner/oracle
implementation and frozen escape/oracle-spoof vector identity; its post-
authorization staging attempt executes those fixtures before any A0 target.
The later A0 artifact authorization consumes the raw
observations produced for the exact A0 target.
If the platform cannot enforce it, dynamic staging and bundle update are
unsupported/read-only rather than deferred to C0. C0 later delivers the
production manager/worker/gate sandbox, not this bootstrap prerequisite.

Repair mode is closed to `resume-same-object | abort-to-old |
supersede-with-new-authority`. It binds the failed installation/materialization,
all observed pointer/generation/inventory hashes, failure evidence and a new
fence. `resume-same-object` is allowed only when an external observer proves no
target generation ever served and the exact authorized object can be restored;
it tombstones unreachable bytes and CASes the same reserved installation back
to a registry-derived phase. The API cannot choose that phase. One immutable
`InstallResumeClassificationV1` binds intercepted phase, complete install/
action/audit/principal/guard histories, external observations and exactly one
observation class/target from this closed table:

| Resume observation class | Required exact proof | Derived target phase |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pre-quiesce-no-effect` | intercepted durable phase is exactly `prepared`; qualification is valid, no quiesce capability/effect exists and all earlier histories remain current | `prepared` |
| `predecessor-closed-target-absent` | intercepted durable phase is exactly `quiesced`; exact predecessor handoff/closure is bound, target effect is absent or tombstoned and pointer is old | `quiesced` |
| `target-fsynced-pointer-old` | intercepted durable phase is exactly `materialized`; exact inventory/tree/fsync receipt exists, pointer is still old and no later effect exists | `materialized` |
| `target-pointer-bound-no-exec` | intercepted durable phase is exactly `pointer-updated`; pointer is exact target, continuous install/guard audit proves no target execution and settle remains pending | `pointer-updated` |
| `all-install-executors-terminal` | intercepted durable phase is exactly `executor-reaped`; every generation/action/audit/principal is terminal, pointer/guard/dependencies are exact and final seal is absent | `executor-reaped` |

Thus `derived_resume_target_phase` is closed to `prepared | quiesced |
materialized | pointer-updated | executor-reaped`. A sticky qualification
FAIL/conflict, audit gap, served target, ambiguous pointer/effect, invalidated
dependency, multiple matching classes or any caller-supplied target makes this
mode illegal. The intercepted phase is a registry history fact, not a request;
the exact-phase predicates make the five rows mutually exclusive. `abort-to-old` and `supersede-with-new-authority` require the
classification/target fields null. Resume preserves every old failure/repair/
qualification/history root and CASes only the derived phase.

`abort-to-old` exists only for a successor update with a still-
valid predecessor seal/generation. Before the fence it cancels the handoff and
leaves the exact current activation untouched; after quiesce it cannot resurrect
the reaped process. It permanently tombstones the successor reservation/
materialization/authorization, restores or verifies predecessor pointer
eligibility, then uses a fresh seal-bound target-launch generation and activation
for the predecessor bundle. First install has no old generation and forbids this
mode. A post-fence abort always completes the exact owned service closure. If
the abort repair is already active, `observe-predecessor-service-closure`
atomically binds that closure, moves the handoff directly to
`restore-predecessor-pending` and moves the predecessor generation from
`serving` to repair-owned `launch-eligible`. If closure won first, repair
creation atomically CASes handoff `closed-by-this-installation ->
restore-predecessor-pending` and generation `handoff-closed -> launch-eligible`.
Both set `launch_eligibility_kind=abort-to-old-restoration` and the exact repair
as owner. There is no persisted active abort repair with handoff
`closed-by-this-installation`; its final-seal RecoveryAction therefore remains
unique. Only that repair may
reserve the fresh launch. Its successful launch/activation atomically clears the
eligibility owner and terminalizes the handoff
`aborted-after-restored-launch`. Ordinary restart, successor final seal and a
second repair cannot consume that eligibility. Another successor attempt needs
fresh authority.
Repair creation and successor final seal race on the same handoff/generation/
installation revisions: repair-first installs the active owner and blocks seal;
seal-first retires the predecessor and makes abort-to-old ineligible. There is
no post-seal restoration branch.
`supersede-with-new-authority` permanently tombstones the failed template/update
authorization and requires a fresh bootstrap authority (first install) or fresh
previous-supervisor+human successor authorization; it never resets a consumed
nonce or rebinds a template to another object. Repair creation and the selected
phase transition are one external-registry transaction. Repairs are fenced sagas
with `prepared | qualification-pending | executor-armed | effect-observed |
failed-install-tombstoned | successor-created | bound | manual-conflict`,
expected installation/pointer revisions and one closed
mode. BTS-0 and the unprivileged coordinator only sequence them. Every repair
external effect requires a freshly qualified disposable executor, per-action
capability, complete audit/reap and principal retirement; no permanent process is
an executor. Every repair/history event is retained in the installation and
sealed audit roots. `supersede-with-new-authority` creates a new installation and
authorization lineage after tombstoning the old one; it is never a third spelling
of `abort-to-old`. Only `abort-to-old | supersede-with-new-authority` terminal
repair bind leaves the failed installation in one closed disposition `aborted |
superseded | tombstoned`; ordinary phase actions, slot reuse, final seal and
qualification all reject those dispositions. `resume-same-object` instead
atomically clears the active repair, restores the same installation to its
derived nonterminal phase and requires `resulting_failed_installation_disposition`
null. For `abort-to-old` or `supersede-with-new-authority`, terminal bind additionally
requires the failed installation's target guard and denial stream to be
`cancelled` with complete no-exec/audit/principal-cleanup receipts. A
`resume-same-object` repair instead retains the same live guard/stream and proves
their cursor continuity at the derived phase; it may not replace or reset them.

| Install-repair phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | unique repair owner/mode/approvals/observations/fences frozen | `drive-repair-principal-qualification` |
| `qualification-pending` | exact repair executor qualification aggregate current | `arm-qualified-repair-executor` |
| `executor-armed` | fresh executor/action capability/audit ready | `perform-or-observe-repair-effect` |
| `effect-observed` | exact restore/abort/tombstone effect and audit range bound | `settle-observed-repair-effect` |
| `failed-install-tombstoned` | old installation/materialization/authority permanently ineligible; only supersede may continue | `create-exact-authorized-successor-installation` |
| `successor-created` | new authorization/materialization/installation triple binds originating repair and frozen old root | `bind-supersede-repair` |
| `bound` | owner cleared and repair roots terminal; resume atomically restores the same installation to its derived nonterminal phase with null disposition and continuous guard, while abort/supersede binds cancelled guard/stream plus exact terminal restore/successor disposition | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | mode/receipt/revision/fence/effect/successor differs | `diagnose-only` |

Transport is explicitly untrusted. Operators may acquire the artifact from the
npm/release channel named in the manifest or from an air-gapped bundle; the
offline bundle contains artifact, canonical manifest, signer/rotation chain,
revocation snapshot and human-readable fingerprints. Verification of signature,
hash, package identity and extracted inventory occurs before any code executes,
so channel TLS or registry metadata is not the trust root. Missing offline
revocation/rotation material fails closed.
An npm/release channel is download transport only: the trusted installer fetches
the packed bytes without running lifecycle scripts and stages/extracts them
exclusively beneath the protected external installation root. It never runs
`npm install` in a candidate checkout and never resolves an executable, loader,
module or dependency from project `node_modules`, a package-manager project
prefix/cache, or the current working directory. `state doctor` and launch-time
provenance fail closed on any such path even when its bytes coincidentally match
a manifest. The air-gapped bundle also carries every qualified optional native
adapter artifact/prebuild for its declared execution cells, or explicitly
downgrades those cells before installation.

Sidecar endpoints use a bounded base32 digest of project/checkout, PID and a
128-bit random nonce and are registered under an exclusive checkout lock; the
protected registry stores the full identity/endpoint binding. Before launch the
adapter proves the encoded Unix path is below the actual platform `sun_path`
limit (including NUL), runtime parent ownership/mode and no symlink traversal;
Windows proves pipe namespace/ACL equivalently. A new sidecar never reuses an
occupied endpoint. Stale endpoint cleanup requires liveness, endpoint nonce and
lock proof. Path-length boundary, collision, hostile symlink, spaces in the
persistent state root and cleanup-after-kill are qualification faults. CI uses
distinct state and runtime roots per job or explicit serialization for one
checkout.

Manager-captured worker results first enter a durable control-plane inbox with
an episode/result idempotency key, then settle exactly once into kernel state.
Delivery is at-least-once; manager death after worker exit can lose availability
but cannot create two binds or a trusted success without the durable inbox.
The capture transaction persists `pending` before any task/result bind. Inbox
recovery is closed: `pending` maps to `resume-inbox-exactly-once-bind`, which
atomically writes the exact result bind and `settled`; an already exact bind is
settled idempotently, while a divergent bind becomes `dead_letter`. `settled`
maps to `noop`, and `dead_letter` to `diagnose-only`. Therefore there is no
separate bind-before-inbox-ack window.

#### Trust-root and approval envelope

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/trust-root.schema.json` and
`migration-approval.schema.json`. The local trust root is Ed25519. The private
key is non-exportable where the platform key store supports it
(Keychain/libsecret-or-agent/DPAPI-backed provider); the public key ID and
revocation/rotation chain live in the protected registry. CI uses an explicitly
provisioned ephemeral signing identity and records its issuer. `state route adopt`/`init`
shows the package/supervisor hash and public key fingerprint for external human
approval before pinning.

Approval bytes use RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization and a domain-separated
Ed25519 signature over the canonical SHA-256 digest. The schema includes key ID,
issuer/actor, domain-separated purpose, `projectId`, `checkoutId`, relevant
run/goal/task/track audience, plan/contract hash, authority/policy epochs, nonce,
issued/expiry times, conflict/timeout policy and surrendered capabilities. It
also carries a typed `approvedObjectHash`: plan approval binds the exact
candidate plan/snapshot; commit approval equals the exact immutable
`CommitApprovalManifestV1` payload hash, which binds plan/checkpoint, ordered task/track/
file/evidence/DocStore roots, candidate integration snapshot, base/ref continuity,
every approved tree/deterministic commit and preallocated Git-saga ID plus the
applicable contract/proof roots;
migration approval binds the exact migration tuple.
Criterion-proof receipts and waivers used for either task or goal completion
bind an immutable typed `completionDraftId` and `completionInputHash`. A task
draft additionally binds the exact task/contract, fully settled Git saga/
settlement, lineage mode, complete transition root, protected ref generation,
predecessor/head and derived ancestry proof or settlement-equal history-rewrite
authorization; a goal draft binds its stable goal lineage/contract and goal/
intent revision plus the signed baseline/complete settlement slice, with origin
run retained only as audience provenance. Both bind
the exact project/checkout, criterion/verifier and waiver-slot requirements, and final
ref/commit/tree without including result-envelope hashes. A proof or waiver for
a same-tree predecessor commit therefore has a different input hash and cannot
be substituted into any successor or replacement draft. The final proof-set
hash is computed only after the bound result envelopes exist, avoiding a
self-referential signature. A purpose or audience cannot be reinterpreted for
another object.

Signature verification, unused-nonce CAS, durable approval record, dependency
index and the first authorized state transition occur in one kernel transaction.
For commit approval this transaction makes the exact manifest current and creates
only its first ordered `prepared` saga; subsequent preallocated sagas are created
by that manifest's closed recovery action. For migration it
creates the maintenance intent/lease. A replay, object/audience drift, expiry or
concurrent consumer leaves both nonce and target state uncommitted. Later saga
steps use only that frozen object and fail on approval revocation. An approval or
key revocation writes its append-only fact and invalidates every active
dependent saga, task proof and goal attestation in the same transaction; the
only exception is the separately sealed bootstrap historical anchor described
above, which is no longer an active signing credential. Git phase actions,
terminal policy, `canCountTaskCompletion()`, `canCountAsTrustedProof()` and
`canCountGoalCompletion()` all require the approval/key to remain current: before
publication effect revocation contains any live hook/lock actor and then records
`manual-conflict`; after ref effect the
exact publication rolls forward but cannot become trusted; `kernel-bound`
remains untrusted;
TaskDoneProvisional/TaskDone/GoalComplete become stale without erasing history.
Rotation requires old+new signatures; revocation is monotonic. Irreversible
finalization and an intentional history rewrite each require two distinct
approver key IDs, approval rows and nonces: the pinned previous-supervisor
release identity and the human/operator identity. The two signatures bind one
common typed object hash and are verified/consumed through a dedicated
aggregate; two signatures by one key or two independently shaped objects are
never “two-key”.

For a planned history rewrite, one transaction verifies and consumes both
approval nonces, creates the `history_rewrite_authorizations` aggregate and an
exact `prepared` Git saga, marks the governed ref head `rewrite-pending`, and
invalidates the affected task lineage/head and every dependent proof. It creates
no completion draft or attestation. The external Git saga must subsequently
finish cleanup, commit the exact `GitSagaSettlementV1`, release its broker writer
fence and reach `settled`; only then may a new exact-tip task draft and fresh
verifier receipts be evaluated. Revocation or crash leaves the old lineage
invalid and the saga recoverable/manual-conflict, never implicitly restores it.
A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/bootstrap-authority.schema.json`,
`bootstrap-slot-template.schema.json`,
`bootstrap-slot-materialization.schema.json`,
`bootstrap-grant-ceremony.schema.json`,
`bootstrap-target-saga.schema.json` and
`bootstrap-target-repair.schema.json`, plus
`bootstrap-staging-runner.schema.json` and
`qualification-oracle.schema.json`. For the initial release, an external
bootstrap previous-supervisor key generated/stored by `BootstrapHostRootV1`
outside every project route and explicitly human-approved in the detached review
manifest acts as the bounded previous-supervisor identity. Its manifest pins
public key, baseline release,
plan/review-governance-bundle/operator-decision,
coordinator/staging-contract, schema and fault hashes,
and a finite set of single-use
slot-policy templates for the declared initial execution-cell matrix. Round ten
cannot know future A0 artifacts, C0 bundle hashes or D2 reports, so it freezes no
wildcard object grant. Each template instead fixes one closed purpose, subject
slot ID, audience shape, release lineage, allowed cell dimensions, required
provenance/conformance/report predicates, signer pair, expiry ceiling and
exactly-once materialization rule. It may only:

`required_predicates_hash` is not a bag of generic reports. It commits a closed
typed policy DAG over `EvidenceStatementV1`, `EvidenceSignatureV1` and
`EvidencePolicyV1`. V1 permits only `single | all-of-same-object |
report-plus-audit-chain`; it has no arbitrary m-of-n:

| Evidence statement/policy | Closed composition and signer domain |
| --- | --- |
| `source-build-equivalence` | external reproducible-build verifier over both isolated builder outputs; neither builder nor target signs the verdict |
| `runtime-closure` | pinned external artifact/runtime verifier |
| `review-authorization` | `report-plus-audit-chain`: two disjoint auditor statements over the raw set, then operator decision over both exact hashes |
| `staging-observation` | BTS-0 external observation sealer; never the adapter, TCB oracle or target |
| `staging-history` | external registry/auditor over complete execution/outcome roots and all three observation seals |
| `no-install-effect` | protected registry/filesystem/process audit sealer |
| `external-conformance` | pinned external conformance oracle named by the template |
| `execution-cell-qualification` | current external supervisor oracle for the exact cell/runner/fault profile |
| `soak-execution-report` + `soak-report-audit` | `report-plus-audit-chain`: supervisor statement plus independent auditor statement whose subject is the exact report hash |
| `approval-signature` | `all-of-same-object`: exactly the two distinct previous-supervisor/bootstrap and human-operator roles, domains and keys sign one canonical approval statement |
| `revocation-snapshot` | external trust registry for the exact authority/key generations |

Every predicate schema binds its kind/version, exact subject and audience,
issuer role/domain/key/generation, signing-operation ID, producer/verifier
artifact hash, referenced raw inputs, issued sequence, expiry and revocation
identity. Composite policies freeze exact role slots, multiplicity, domain/key
distinctness, common statement hash and parent-report relation. Each purpose template
enumerates the exact required policy DAG; a later
materialization supplies only their exact object hashes. Unknown kinds,
candidate/under-review signers, same-domain signer substitution, a generic
`report` field or a future evidence kind not installed through a reviewed
trust-control successor is rejected before reservation.

1. reserve and durably complete one `a0-trust-control-install` slot for the exact A0
   tree/control-bundle artifact after byte-identical schema installation and the
   separately authorized bootstrap-TCB hash, external reviewed conformance
   report, sealed exact-target `staging_launch_receipt` and fresh exact-tree/artifact/runtime-closure four-perspective
   `a0-merge-install` manifest all pass;
2. authorize first adoption plus fixture-scoped qualification grants and
   disposable irreversible-finalization records by materializing their
   predeclared policy slots with exact release/cell/runner/purpose hashes;
3. after matching D2 reports pass, materialize and co-sign with the independent
   human key the first production activation/grant for each predeclared cell;
   and
4. co-sign one rotation that pins the qualified first supervisor.

Materialization begins in one external-registry transaction that verifies the
immutable template, two distinct current keys/nonces and every required report,
fills the exact object/audience hashes, consumes both approval nonces and
reserves the slot to one immutable materialization ID. Its closed purpose union
then selects exactly one post-effect; unknown or mismatched purpose is rejected:

- only `a0-trust-control-install` creates
  `control_bundle_installations.phase=qualification-pending`, and its slot becomes consumed
  at that installation's `bound` transaction;
- adoption, fixture/production grant, disposable finalization and
  rotation-with-successor-grants create an external
  `bootstrap_target_sagas.phase=reserved`, never an install row. Their target
  StateKernel rows are inert and carry the materialization ID until the
  cross-boundary saga below activates them.

The target saga phases and sole recovery actions are:

| Bootstrap target phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | external slot reserved; no kernel target row/effect | `resume-bootstrap-target-prepare` |
| `target-prepared` | exact kernel target rows exist as inactive/pending and expose a signed receipt | `resume-bootstrap-slot-consume` |
| `slot-consumed` | external slot is irrevocably consumed; any rotation/bootstrap anchor remains pending and unsealed; target remains inactive | `resume-bootstrap-target-activate` |
| `target-activated` | kernel target is locally activated with the external consumed receipt but remains globally ineligible | `resume-bootstrap-target-external-bind-prepare` |
| `external-bind-prepared` | external registry binds the exact activation receipt and pending anchor; kernel bind barrier may be absent or exact after lost acknowledgment | `resume-bootstrap-target-bind-barrier` |
| `bound` | external transaction sealed the exact anchor/final receipt; kernel final acknowledgment/barrier release may still be pending | `ensure-bootstrap-target-kernel-finalize` |
| `repairing` | one unique two-key repair owns the saga revision/fence; ordinary phase actions are denied | `dispatch-bootstrap-target-repair` |
| `tombstoned` | repair permanently disabled the target/materialization without reopening its slot | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | target/revision/fence/receipt or purpose diverged | `diagnose-only` |

Each action observes the other authority through a signed content-addressed
receipt and exact revision/fence; no cross-database atomicity is claimed.
`resume-bootstrap-target-external-bind-prepare` first writes an immutable
external preparation receipt and phase. The next phase's sole recovery action
first runs one kernel transaction that rechecks the target revision/fence and
absence of a conflicting open/maintenance/reverse/capability operation, creates
the scope-specific `bootstrap_target_bind_barriers` row and CASes the target
from `local-pending-bind` to `bind-barrier-armed`. That barrier denies every
conflicting consumer in the target's project/checkout/cell scope. If this
transaction committed before acknowledgment, the action observes the identical
barrier and does not rewrite it. Only then may one external transaction CAS the
saga to `bound`, seal the anchor and emit the final signed bound receipt.
The same CAS verifies the purpose-specific authority tuple frozen by the
materialization: finalization requires the expected active SQLite epoch with
reverse still available; a completed reverse, epoch/backend/phase change or
already-surrendered policy writes the durable rejection below rather than
binding later. Adoption, grant and rotation use their own closed expected tuple,
so a sequential state transition cannot make an old pending target newly valid.
If a conflicting reverse/maintenance/terminal operation won before the barrier
CAS, one kernel transaction appends a unique
`bootstrap_target_bind_rejections` record keyed by target saga/revision,
bind-preparation receipt and target revision. It binds the conflicting operation
kind/ID/sequence/fence and observed authority tuple, emits the signed rejection
receipt, and makes no barrier/target change. Before reevaluating current state,
every retry must load that unique record; once present, the external action can
only bind its receipt while CASing the saga to `manual-conflict`. A crash after
the kernel record but before the external CAS therefore cannot turn a transient
conflict into later success. The action never polls until the conflict
disappears or silently chooses another phase, so the consumed slot can enter the
declared repair path.

`ensure-bootstrap-target-kernel-finalize` verifies that final receipt and in one
kernel transaction stores its hash, CASes `bind-barrier-armed` to
`external-bound-acknowledged`, marks the barrier `bound` and installs dependency
edges. For a disposable or production finalization purpose, that same
scope-appropriate transaction also changes the checkout/fixture capability
policy to `l2-enabled/reverse-surrendered`; neither the local target row nor
external bound alone changes that policy. An exact lost acknowledgment is a no-op; a mismatch is an integrity
conflict. Until that transaction commits, the barrier keeps all conflicting
operations denied even though the external saga is already `bound`. A crash in
any window therefore re-enters one action without admitting a reverse/bind,
open/adoption or grant/terminal race. A grant, finalization, adoption or
successor rotation is never locally activated before its slot is consumed and
never globally eligible before both external `bound` and kernel final
acknowledgment. A consumed slot with a pending target resumes only the same
activation. The already-used approval nonces are not needed to resume either
exact saga ID.

`isBootstrapTargetGloballyEligible(targetKind, targetId, boundReceipt)` is the
only bridge from these external records to a trusted kernel read. For any row
with a non-null `bootstrap_materialization_id`, it returns true only when the
kernel row has `activation_state=external-bound-acknowledged`, its stored
preparation and final-receipt hashes, `bootstrap_target_bind_barriers.state=bound`,
and materialization/purpose/target/revision/fence match
the supplied coordinator-signed final receipt, the external saga in that
