receipt is `bound`, and the named immutable sealed anchor has the same hashes.
A missing/unavailable registry, pending phase, locally `current` label,
unverified/cached candidate object, repair/tombstone or mismatch is hard false.
Bound bootstrap anchors are immutable and cannot enter target repair; later
ordinary typed grant/finalization/adoption/rotation revocation remains a kernel
dependency. Architecture lint forbids direct consumption of a bootstrap-backed
`activation_intent`, `capability_grant`, `irreversible_finalization` or successor
rotation without this predicate. The open/maintenance dispatcher, forward and
reverse entry/flip, effective-capability computation, candidate-execution,
terminal/promotion policies, `canCountTaskCompletion`,
`canCountGoalCompletion`, `canCountAsTrustedProof`, approval, calibrated
feedback/learning, release/publish and projection paths all call it and bind the
final receipt hash in their dependency set.

`manual-conflict` has no automatic retry. A new two-key
`bootstrap_target_repairs` aggregate binds the exact conflicted saga, immutable
observation set, materialization, target and expected receipts and has the
closed mode union `resume-same-object | tombstone-before-bind`.
Its creation transaction consumes approvals from two distinct current keys and
two fresh nonces, CASes the exact
`manual-conflict` saga revision/fence to `repairing`, installs one
`active_repair_id` and allocates a new repair fence. A database unique index
allows at most one nonterminal repair per target saga. A competing mode/repair,
ordinary saga resume or stale-fence action changes nothing. Repair phases and
their only actions are:

| Repair mode / persisted phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resume-same-object / prepared` | unique repair owns the conflicted saga; immutable observations prove one exact object and reconstructible prior phase | `apply-bootstrap-target-resume-repair` |
| `tombstone-before-bind / prepared` | unique repair owns an unbound target; kernel target may be absent, pending or locally activated but is globally ineligible | `resume-bootstrap-target-kernel-tombstone` |
| `tombstone-before-bind / kernel-tombstoned` | exact kernel tombstone/absence receipt is bound; external materialization remains consumed but not yet tombstoned | `resume-bootstrap-target-external-tombstone` |
| `either / bound` | exact repair terminal receipt, original saga outcome and slot disposition agree | `noop` |
| `either / manual-conflict` | receipt, revision, fence, mode or object diverged | `diagnose-only` |

`apply-bootstrap-target-resume-repair` is one external-registry transaction: it
revalidates the observations and CASes the original saga from `repairing` to
the single reconstructed phase while CASing the repair to `bound` and clearing
`active_repair_id`; it never changes or reopens the materialization. The
tombstone action CASes the exact kernel target revision/fence to `tombstoned`
and tombstones any exact bind barrier in the same transaction, or proves their
exact absence, then emits a signed receipt. If that kernel CAS
committed before the external phase update, the same action observes the exact
receipt and only advances the repair to `kernel-tombstoned`. The next action is
one external transaction that permanently tombstones the materialization/slot,
CASes the original saga `repairing -> tombstoned`, binds the kernel receipt,
CASes the repair to `bound` and clears `active_repair_id`. Every action requires
the repair fence and expected source revisions; no age/timeout or caller choice
selects a branch. The original slot and all approval nonces remain consumed.
Neither mode may repair an already `bound` target; that requires its ordinary
typed revocation/rotation path. If neither mode is provable, only a new offline
bootstrap authority may supersede it after the conflicted object is fail-closed;
the old saga is never overwritten.

There is no prefix, “any future hash”, candidate-selected predicate or later
template edit. Candidate `check:*` output may be one hashed observation but
cannot authorize its own A0 install; the external conformance result, fresh
detached implementation-review manifest and both signatures are mandatory. The
review manifest binds the exact A0 source tree, packed artifact, build
provenance, runtime closure and trust-control diff and uses the already frozen parser/model-class rules, so
it introduces no candidate parser. The first pinned supervisor must countersign
the `rotation-with-successor-grants` materialization; its successor grants are
prepared inactive, the external registry irrevocably consumes the slot and
records a pending rotation anchor; the exact kernel activation receipt then
passes external-bind preparation and kernel barrier arming before the external
transaction binds the target saga and seals that anchor; the final kernel
acknowledgment makes it globally eligible. No bootstrap authority is sealed before that
saga is `bound`; ordinary task/goal proofs never
depend on the bootstrap key. Sealing records the historical install/adoption/grant/rotation objects as
immutable anchors and permanently disables unused slots. A later bootstrap-key
revocation forbids future signatures but does not retroactively invalidate
sealed authority or successor grants; a revocation effective before a slot's
seal invalidates that ceremony and blocks production. Compromise before sealing
enters `manual-conflict` and requires a new external bootstrap manifest rather
than re-adopting or overwriting authority. This is the complete initial signer
chain, not an implicit “previous supervisor” assumption.

After the first A0 bundle, every changed manager/launcher/RPC client/sidecar/
loader/dependency byte is a successor bundle, including A1 and C0 delivery. The
currently pinned supervisor qualifies the staged artifact with fresh disposable
fixture processes; neither the permanent control coordinator nor a production
install executor runs candidate bytes. The artifact must have source↔build
provenance, a fresh detached four-perspective review, the full external
conformance suite and the track's exact-cell qualification/fault receipts before
activation. One external-registry transaction verifies those immutable inputs,
the dual-signed successor candidate policy/program/global-equivalence owner and
complete-history freeze described below,
and consumes distinct previous-supervisor and human approvals into a
`control_bundle_update_authorizations` row. Its one consumption transaction
creates an immutable `control_bundle_update_materialization` plus the exact
installation at `qualification-pending`; the
unprivileged coordinator sequences the same disposable-executor install saga.
The staged bundle never needs
to be active to qualify and cannot sign its own update. A1/C0 merge is blocked
until the resulting generation is `bound` and its exact execution-cell receipt
is current; no A0 or prior-bundle receipt is relabeled.

Successor selection is a signed program, not a succession of unrelated update
IDs. Before the first candidate reservation for one installed predecessor, the
current supervisor and human sign the same canonical
`SuccessorCandidatePolicyV1`. It binds registry/project/checkout, predecessor
final seal and current activation/generation, semantic update-intent hash,
proposed program ID, allowed change classes, stable candidate-equivalence
profile, variant/termination policy, finite candidate/equivalence maxima,
budget-accounting point and extension mode. V1 fixes one semantic review per
stable candidate equivalence, accounts budget at candidate reservation, returns
the global owner on duplicates, makes any substantive negative/ambiguity sticky,
and forbids extension. A future extension requires its own dual-signed chain over
old+delta=new and complete prior roots; a new program or renamed intent cannot
reset the installed predecessor's cumulative epoch.

Each installed predecessor generation owns one
`successor_candidate_epoch_head`, one current or terminal
`successor_candidate_program`, and a globally unique
`successor_candidate_equivalence_owner` for each stable semantic candidate. The
stable `candidate_equivalence_hash` is domain-separated over registry/project/
checkout, predecessor final seal and generation, the externally authorized
`successor_update_intent_hash`, and `candidate_behavior_hash`. The intent hash is
derived from the dual-signed normalized objective/observable contract/protected-
surface object; caller labels, prose, whitespace and a renamed change class are
excluded, so relabeling cannot create a new intent. `change_class` is produced by
the pinned trusted diff classifier, checked against the signed allowed set and
retained as evidence, but is not an owner-key component. Source/artifact/build/
runtime bytes that affect execution already enter `candidate_behavior_hash`.
Qualification and review identities append context/evidence history to that same
owner and never mint another semantic verdict owner. Program/candidate/update/
review lineage, materialization/installation/handoff, ceremony/run/session/nonce
and provider allocation IDs are likewise excluded. The existing
`formal_review_equivalence_hash` remains the exact review-input owner and includes
the selected program/candidate, policy, pre-review program root and exact review
context/input. Both owners are required: the first prevents cross-lineage,
change-class and qualification-context result shopping; the second prevents an
exact request from being resent. V1 has no negative-resolution transition for a
successor owner: CRITICAL/P1/FAIL/ambiguity is permanent for that predecessor,
normalized intent and behavior. A future harness-repair escape hatch requires a
new schema version and a dual-signed typed resolution over the complete old
finding/outcome root; a later model PASS can never be that resolution.

Program and candidate recovery are closed:

| Successor-candidate program state | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `open` | `reserve-next-successor-candidate` |
| `candidate-active` | `resume-current-successor-candidate` |
| `installing` | `resume-selected-successor-installation` |
| `bound` | `noop` |
| `budget-exhausted` | `noop` |
| `invalidated` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

| Successor-candidate phase | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `reserved` | `freeze-successor-candidate-subjects` |
| `subjects-frozen` | `drive-or-bind-successor-fixture-history` |
| `static-review` | `settle-owned-successor-static-review` |
| `authorization-ready` | `create-exact-control-bundle-update-authorization` |
| `authorized` | `consume-exact-successor-update-authorization` |
| `installing` | `resume-exact-successor-final-seal-saga` |
| `bound` | `noop` |
| `rejected` | `settle-rejected-successor-candidate-and-consider-next` |
| `aborted-pre-go` | `settle-aborted-successor-candidate-and-consider-next` |
| `invalidated` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

| Successor equivalence-owner state | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `reserved` | `create-exact-successor-review-ceremony` |
| `review-current` | `settle-exact-successor-review-ceremony` |
| `pass-settled` | `noop` |
| `negative-settled` | `noop` |
| `ambiguous-settled` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

`create-exact-control-bundle-update-authorization` verifies/consumes the distinct
final update approvals and records the exact available authorization, moving the
candidate to `authorized`; it does not create an installation. The next action
consumes only that authorization and atomically creates its materialization,
`qualification-pending` installation and candidate/program `installing` states.

The exact-cell fixture history settles before static review so reviewers receive
the complete execution/outcome roots. Every reservation, fixture result,
transport/run history, review decision, rejection, abort, authorization and
installation transition appends by expected count/root/revision CAS to candidate,
program and predecessor-global histories. Possible provider send consumes the
equivalence owner's sole semantic review; only the existing whole-ceremony,
same-formal-input recovery whose four slots and every turn have terminal typed
no-send/no-acceptance/no-model-execution/reap/no-late-send proofs is legal. A
changed review context/input, program, qualification harness or lineage is not
infrastructure recovery. A prior CRITICAL/P1/FAIL/ambiguous outcome for the
stable equivalence prevents a later ceremony or selected PASS. A distinct
behavior may consume the next signed candidate ordinal. Cosmetic intent or
change-class changes return the existing owner; a substantively different
normalized intent requires a newly dual-signed policy but does not erase the
predecessor epoch's append-only global history.

Before ceremony creation, one acyclic
`SuccessorCandidateReviewContextFreezeV1` binds policy/program/selected candidate,
equivalence owner/hash, pre-review program and predecessor-global history roots,
exact-cell roots and exact review input/context. It contains no ceremony,
decision, review-authorization or later object. Signed successor scope,
ceremony/decision/review authorization repeat that pre-review freeze and roots;
the decision/authorization separately bind the resulting complete ceremony
history.

After the review authorization and its outcome/history events are durably
appended, but before update authorization, one acyclic
`SuccessorCandidateHistoryFreezeV1` binds the pre-review freeze, review decision/
authorization, terminal equivalence-owner verdict, complete review-outcome,
through-review program and predecessor-global history prefixes and exact-cell
roots. It contains no future update authorization/materialization/installation/
seal ID and is explicitly a prefix freeze, not the final history root. Every
later update-authorization/materialization/installation object repeats that
freeze, records the then-current program/global counts and roots, and proves the
frozen prefix against them before appending its one canonical transition. The
successor final-seal transaction first appends the preallocated terminal
candidate/program/global events and atomically binds the resulting final counts/
roots in the seal. Those terminal event hashes exclude the final-seal row hash,
outer lifecycle/revision and signatures; they bind the exact preallocated
`SuccessorFinalSealIntentV1` ID/hash, target generation, closed transition kind
and predecessor roots. The intent was created before those events and contains
no terminal history or future envelope hash, so the graph is acyclic. The final
seal statement/envelope must repeat that intent. The final roots must extend the post-review freeze and every
intermediate snapshot with no omitted or divergent suffix. First-install
branches make all successor-program fields mandatory null.
`isReviewAuthorizationCurrent` for installed-successor
recomputes the global owner, dual-signed policy, budget, one-semantic-review
limit, absence of a prior sticky negative, complete ceremony/transport history
and exact pre-review freeze; update/install predicates additionally recompute the
post-review prefix and current suffix. A selected PASS or the through-review
prefix alone is insufficient.

`ControlBundleInstallFinalSealV1` has a closed `seal_kind` `oneOf`. The
`first-install` branch requires the bootstrap program admission, retained review-
root admission/materialization, plan/TCB/A0 authorizations, implementation
program/run and complete staging/applicability/history evidence. The
  `successor-update` branch instead requires the consumed
  `control_bundle_update_authorization`, predecessor final seal, exact current and
  target generations, current installed supervisor identity, distinct previous-
  supervisor and human approvals, fresh successor review authorization,
  successor candidate policy/program/selected candidate/equivalence owner and
  acyclic through-review history freeze plus exact terminal program/global
  history roots and prefix proofs,
  source↔build proof, conformance, exact-cell fixture qualification and the full
predecessor service-instance/operation/session/endpoint closure root plus the
full successor installation histories. Bootstrap-only fields are mandatory null for
the successor branch; successor-only fields are mandatory null for first install.
Both branches bind the same pointer/inventory, revocation head, dependency/
signing-operation roots, target-denial stream, executor/principal retirement and
empty pre-seal target-launch ledger, then atomically make only the target
generation `launch-eligible`. The successor branch also moves the exact
predecessor generation `handoff-closed -> retired`; an abort repair must win its
owned restoration CAS before this seal and therefore cannot race a retired
predecessor back to eligibility. Lost acknowledgment returns the same seal.

Successor exact-cell fixture qualification is never a selectable receipt set.
It uses the same global behavior/context execution substrate as A0 staging:
unique `behavior_outcome_ledgers`, `staging_execution_histories`, immutable
attempt/launch/audit events, sealed launch receipt and mandatory
`staging_history_applicability_binding` for the exact successor artifact,
runtime, fixture, platform cell and review context. The first run gets an
identity binding; later reuse requires a real historical-prefix proof and no new
execution. FAIL/conflict is sticky for that behavior/context and every later
update review sees the complete outcome root. Update authorization,
materialization, installation and successor final seal bind the full execution-
history count/root, behavior-outcome root, applicability-binding set root and
receipt set. A caller-selected PASS suffix or receipt hash cannot satisfy the
branch.

Successor activation evidence is intentionally transitional. The signed scope
preallocates update, materialization, installation and
`control_bundle_predecessor_handoff` IDs and names the exact current activation.
Review-authorization creation first records the unconsumed activation dependency
and absent preallocated handoff. At update-authorization consumption, that
activation must still be current; the transaction creates/binds the handoff to the exact installation,
sets its unique pending handoff pointer and leaves the activation `current`.
Ingress therefore continues before the actual fence. Only
`fence-and-freeze-predecessor-inventory`, after the installation is `prepared`,
and the exact closure-audit stream is already `recording` with a durable
coverage-start receipt, may atomically revalidate the same current
activation/pending handoff, deny new
admission, capture the high-water/member inventory and change activation
`current -> handoff-reserved` together with handoff `current-bound -> fenced`.
Thereafter the dependency predicate follows only that handoff/installation/fence
through its monotonic `current-bound | fenced | draining |
closed-by-this-installation | final-sealed` phases. It neither requires the
activation to remain `current` after consumption nor accepts an unrelated
handoff, ordinary exit, replacement activation or fence. Explicit repair moves
the handoff to its own closed cancel/restore branch; it never rewrites history.

| Predecessor handoff phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `current-bound` | exact still-current activation/generation/launch, unique pending pointer, proposed successor IDs, closure contract and inventory-enumeration policy frozen; ingress remains open, no member snapshot is claimed, and fence waits for exact closure audit `recording` plus coverage-start receipt | `fence-and-freeze-predecessor-inventory` |
| `fenced` | one transaction denied new predecessor capability/operation/endpoint admission, captured the service high-water boundary and materialized the complete member inventory/root; closure audit active | `drain-predecessor-service` |
| `draining` | existing operations/sessions/endpoints/jobs are closing under exact audit; an already active abort repair changes only this action's terminal destination | `observe-predecessor-service-closure` |
| `closed-by-this-installation` | service closure root binds all launch/audit/event/checkpoint, operation/session/endpoint and revoke/close/unmount/reap/namespace/principal receipts | `bind-control-bundle-install-final-seal` |
| `final-sealed` | exact successor final seal terminal-sealed the handoff dependency | `noop` |
| `cancel-before-fence-pending` | two-key repair owns the still-unfenced handoff; activation remains current while closure-audit stop/reap/seal is pending | `cancel-predecessor-closure-audit` |
| `cancelled-before-fence` | two-key repair atomically cleared the pending pointer and cancelled the still-unfenced handoff; exact predecessor activation stayed current and the successor lineage is tombstoned | `noop` |
| `invalidate-before-fence-pending` | activation/fence/history changed before fence; dependency/update are already ineligible while closure-audit cleanup remains | `invalidate-and-reap-predecessor-closure-audit` |
| `invalidated-before-fence` | named activation exited/restarted/was revoked or its fence/history changed before atomic fence; update lineage is ineligible | `noop` |
| `restore-predecessor-pending` | two-key repair owns the closed handoff; successor is tombstoned, predecessor is stopped and its `handoff-closed -> launch-eligible` receipt is owned by this repair | `launch-restored-predecessor-generation` |
| `aborted-after-restored-launch` | fresh seal-bound launch/activation of the still-valid predecessor bundle and repair receipt are bound; no old process was resurrected | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | activation, installation, inventory, fence or closure diverged | `diagnose-only` |

The handoff/service-closure aggregate is not a caller summary. Its fence
transaction closes admission, changes the activation state and enumerates every
predecessor service instance, operation, session and endpoint through the same
committed high-water in one registry transaction;
there is no pre-fence snapshot race. Immutable member rows contain initial
identity/expected terminal only; separate append-only closure rows bind future
terminal receipts after they exist. Append/checkpoint roots use expected
revision/count/root CAS. The successor
signed update authorization freezes the handoff ID, contract and inventory-
enumeration policy; its consumption, materialization, installation and final
seal bind the same ID, fenced inventory root and eventually observed frozen
closure root. Its independent closure-audit stream begins before the fence,
shares the service high-water boundary and seals only after all member closure
receipts, so an unanchored event root cannot satisfy the handoff. The final-seal
transaction alone advances `closed-by-this-installation -> final-sealed`. A
normal crash/restart closure and an update-driven closure remain distinguishable.
Consumption creates the audit stream `reserved` in the same transaction as the
`current-bound` handoff. Its first action durably allocates one arm generation,
principal/job/nonce/source identity and arm fencing token and enters `arming`
before any external observer can exist. `arming` may start only that observer as
a blocked job; its registration receipt enters `observer-registered`, still
without source recording. Release then CASes the current arm fence, attaches the
exact source and enters `recording`. Start/release/source attach all enforce the
same target-side arm fence. The launcher broker linearizes every job-registration
commit against cancellation; its no-late-arm barrier waits out in-flight tokens
and proves no lower-fence job can register afterward. The handoff
fence action is a deterministic no-effect wait while that stream is not exact
`recording`. Arm acknowledgment loss therefore cannot create a fence-before-
coverage execution order.
Pre-fence repair cancellation atomically moves the handoff to
`cancel-before-fence-pending` without stopping the current activation. Its sole
action first increments the arm fence and installs a linearizable no-late-arm
barrier. It maps `reserved` to cancelled with a no-arm proof, or maps `arming |
observer-registered | recording | gap-conflict` through `cancel-draining`, where
it denies release/source attach, closes any source, reaps the exact job and
retires the principal. Only a bound no-late-arm/source-close/job-reap receipt
may reach `cancelled`. Only then does one transaction clear the pending pointer, tombstone
the successor lineage and reach `cancelled-before-fence`. No closure observer or
source handle is orphaned.
If the named activation ceases to be exact current before the fence, the same
handoff action cannot substitute a restart: it atomically invalidates the
successor activation dependency/update/installation and moves the handoff to
`invalidate-before-fence-pending`. Its sole cleanup action cancels/reaps the same
audit stream, clears the pending pointer and only then reaches
`invalidated-before-fence`. Fresh activation requires fresh successor review
authority.

#### Sidecar IPC protocol

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/control-rpc.schema.json` and
`schemas/vnext/control-inbox.schema.json`, plus
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-installation.schema.json`,
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-update-authorization.schema.json`,
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-update-materialization.schema.json`,
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-install-final-seal.schema.json`,
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-install-repair.schema.json` and
`schemas/vnext/control-bundle-install-repair-event.schema.json`. Transport is a four-byte
big-endian length followed by UTF-8 RFC-8785 JSON. `hello` performs
challenge-response HMAC-SHA-256 only between hashed control-bundle components
using the bundle-memory session secret and binds protocol version, endpoint
nonce and process identity. Requests carry request ID,
method, capability, authority epoch and payload; responses carry request ID,
status, typed error and optional result.

The privileged closed method set is `doctor`, `readSnapshot`, `submitObservation`,
`acquire|renew|releaseLease`, `prepare|bindGitSaga`, `recordApproval`,
`drainOutbox`, and `shutdown`. Capabilities are HMAC-authenticated canonical
objects containing method, project/checkout/run/task audience, fencing token,
control-bundle generation, single-use nonce, authorized-operation ID and expiry.
Only the sidecar may mint
them, only the hashed RPC client may present them, and replay nonces are
transactionally consumed. The separate candidate proposal ingress implements
none of these methods. Unknown
method/field/version, oversized frame, expired/reused token, audience/epoch/fence
mismatch, or unauthenticated peer returns a stable fail-closed error code. Worker
and candidate manager/router/CLI processes receive neither privileged endpoint,
secret/handle nor capability; env/descriptor scrubbing has an allowlist test on
every spawn surface.

Core records include:

A0 `RouteKernelV1`-owned records then include:

  It has no independent lifecycle state: availability is exactly the referenced

- immutable `installed_git_hook_chains(id, route_id, route_generation,

  `preserved-user-hook | docstore-legacy-argv-shim | docstore-vnext-typed`.
  Legacy-wrapper contains exactly one shim member; its frozen backup identity is
  internal input to that wrapper and is never also a separately executed member,
  and the row is permanently nonauthorizing. VNext-dispatch contains at most one
  preserved member followed by exactly one typed DocStore member for managed

  never mix legacy and typed managed members. Trusted governed Git accepts only

  allowance_delivery_intent_hash, terminal_backend_action_intent_id,

  set root is recomputed. The closed `hardlink-create` branch requires exact
  source and absent destination identities, qualified same-device policy and an
  after identity equal to the source inode/File ID and its non-null
  `hardlink_same_inode_receipt_hash`; its rename receipt is canonical null.
  `rename-replace` requires
  exact source/destination, replace/atomic/same-volume policies, paired intent
  and both observed identities plus non-null `rename_replace_receipt_hash`; its
  hardlink receipt is canonical null. `delete` requires one exact leaf and absence
  result; `parent-fsync` requires the exact parent identity/role and fsync
  receipt. `read | create | write-append | hardlink-create | rename-replace |
  delete | parent-fsync` is a closed `oneOf`; every branch requires all
  inapplicable source/destination/policy/receipt fields canonical null. Thus no
  rename or fsync hides behind an aggregate/lower-saga hash. RouteGit's index-witness operation
  explicitly enumerates the witness link, index rename, both parent fsyncs and
  later witness unlink—none is hidden inside a lower saga. Every effect under a
  publication writer fence requires the exact capability/actor/backend-
  authorization composites, issued audience/fence, committed actor-delivery
  intent, pre-effect terminal-backend action intent and observed terminal
  result/slot tombstone that the backend validated;
  every effect outside that branch nulls all allowance fields. The effect
  receipt hash includes those fields, and the later allowance terminal member
  must composite-FK to this same row, so equal effect bytes from another actor/
  authorization cannot be spliced. Its backend ordinal/semantic/primitive
  fields must also equal the accepted backend observation-effect member; the
  Route receipt may include the action-result hash without feeding that hash
  back into the backend semantic root. Operation phases are
  closed as above. Every writer/child stores route ID,
  generation and operation ID; all old operations/leases/children are rejected
  after a route-generation CAS;

  `cancelled-before-child` is reachable only from `reserved | sandbox-armed |

  registration-close, whole-job-empty, namespace-close and zero-effect audit
  seal with null process-start/GO/effect fields. It is the closed cancellation
  result of that source phase's one `*-or-close-*` action, never a second action
  competing with arm/reconcile. Once persisted it is terminally ineligible for
  release. For a control-attempt owner, `settle-cancelled-route-spawn` first
  wakes/awaits the separately phase-owned guard no-send and zero-writer mailbox-
  seal machines; it performs no external call for them. Once those immutable
  prerequisites exist, its one local owner-role transaction performs the
  principal/failed-attempt transition, binds exact retirement and settles. A lost response resumes the same
  preallocated child/spec; absence or age alone cannot select this branch;

A1 extends that same authority/transaction head and writer in place. The

  applied-idempotent-actor-closed | applied-nonretryable-actor-closed`.
  A DB/FK predicate requires parent `recovery_class` and closure kind to match:
  `fenceable-actor` permits its applied-fenceable or cancelled-no-effect branch,
  `target-idempotent` permits only applied-idempotent, and `nonretryable` only

  other pairing is rejected before closure, so a fenceable actor cannot relabel
  itself idempotent to omit the target fence.

  or the full cancelled-no-effect fence/reap/barrier set; target-idempotent

  preallocated same-inode witness, real index bytes and absent source lock. A
  live predecessor binds the existing effect; a dead predecessor may be closed
  and replaced only by a `post-publish-two-lock` generation after reap/
  descriptor-close proof. The alternate exact no-rename branch may replace it
  with three-lock acquisition. Any third state enters containment. In
  `index-lock-consumed`, successor recovery additionally requires exact
  witness/index-byte classification and may never recreate or reacquire an
  `index.lock` for the already-published candidate. The ref-lock
  helper FK must equal this sole owner and inherited
  descriptor; it never acquires a second guardian. `release-git-publication-
  lock-set` releases exactly `active_lock_member_root_hash`; in the post-publish
  branch that is integration+guardian only, never the historical acquired root
  containing the consumed index lock. In the zero-lock branch the same action
  closes/reaps the cleanup RouteSpawn and records the canonical empty active
  root without invoking any Git lock acquire/release primitive.
  `reconcile-published-index-owner`
  revalidates the current two-lock active root, live writer fence, same-inode
  witness and real-index bytes and returns the existing receipt while the
  publication is `index-published | verified-held`; a dead owner follows the
  exact post-publish successor path above. A kernel-bound parent must already
  have atomically moved the current two-lock owner to `release-pending`.
  `reconcile-post-bind-cleanup-owner` may resume only the exact unbound cleanup
  suffix under the still-armed broker fence; its result transaction seals the
  cleanup result prefix and moves the zero-lock owner to `release-pending`.
  Any other parent/owner tuple is containment, not an undefined action;
- immutable `git_publication_lock_acquire_intents(owner_id, ordinal, lock_role,
  lock_path_identity_hash, expected_before_kind, expected_owned_candidate_hash,
  acquire_mode, intent_hash)` and append-only
  `git_publication_lock_acquire_results(owner_id, intent_ordinal, result_kind,
  observed_before_identity_hash, observed_after_identity_hash,
  ownership_receipt_hash, result_hash, recorded_sequence)` are unique by owner/
  ordinal and exact-equal the owner's counts/roots. `lock_role` is `integration |
  guardian | real-index-publish`; `pre-publish-three-lock` has exactly those
  three, while `post-publish-two-lock` has only the first two and
  `post-bind-cleanup-zero-lock` has no intent/result rows plus canonical empty
  roots. Result kind is
  `acquired-new | resumed-held | adopted-exact-owned-lock-after-reap`. The last
  is legal only for a dead pre-publish predecessor's operation-owned lock after
  whole-job reap/descriptor close: before candidate materialization it must be
  the exact expected created-empty/prepared lock identity; afterward it must be
  the exact candidate/witness/source identity. Every acquired prefix is
  enumerated and either safely inherited/adopted or explicitly released before
  successor creation; any unclassified partial acquire or third state enters containment.
  An `actor-registered` death closes that generation only after all per-lock
  results/effects are classified and then creates the sole successor. A
  post-publish two-lock successor that settles both results atomically rebinds
  the existing consumed-lock receipt/witness and enters `index-lock-consumed`
  directly; it never passes through three-lock `locks-held` or repeats index
  publication. A zero-lock successor atomically validates the predecessor's
  complete lock-absence and cleanup-prefix receipts before entering
  `cleanup-active`; it never visits either lock-held phase;

  broker_boot_identity_hash, broker_generation, broker_generation_budget,
  owner_generation_budget,
  writer_scope_member_count,
  writer_scope_member_root_hash, fence_spec_hash, arm_intent_hash,
  receipt_count, receipt_chain_root_hash, current_receipt_id,
  current_receipt_hash, arm_receipt_id, arm_receipt_hash,
  current_armed_observation_receipt_id,
  current_armed_observation_receipt_hash, armed_observation_count,
  armed_observation_root_hash, control_broker_continuity_receipt_count,
  control_broker_continuity_receipt_root_hash,
  current_control_broker_continuity_receipt_id,
  current_control_broker_continuity_receipt_hash,
  control_broker_reservation_count, control_broker_reservation_root_hash,
  current_control_broker_reservation_id,
  current_control_broker_reservation_hash,

  control_broker_failed_attempt_root_hash,

  release_intent_hash, release_receipt_id,

  conflict_receipt_hash, phase, revision,

  RouteSpawn spec/child attempt, boot and generation are composite-bound to the exact current
  `principal_instance_allocations` fence-broker branch and protected supervisor
  job; a process-supplied instance string is not broker authority. Arm requires

  The finite broker-generation budget is governed by
  `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_admission_heads(id, fence_id,
  broker_generation_budget, current_broker_generation,
  last_writer_generation, next_generation_ordinal, generation_claim_count,
  generation_claim_root_hash, current_generation_claim_id,
  current_generation_claim_hash, positive_effect_admission_remaining_count,
  positive_effect_admission_remaining_root_hash, drain_intent_id,
  drain_intent_hash, drain_closure_id, drain_closure_hash,
  budget_exhaustion_receipt_id, budget_exhaustion_receipt_hash,
  phase, revision, created_sequence, sealed_sequence,
  closed_sequence)` with `UNIQUE(fence_id)`. Phase is `writer-open |
  drain-closing | writer-drained-control-open | control-closed | manual-
  conflict`; it never reopens or regains writer admission. Immutable
  `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_claims(id, head_id,
  generation, claim_kind, allocation_id, allocation_identity_hash,
  control_reservation_id, control_reservation_hash,
  predecessor_terminal_barrier_id, predecessor_terminal_barrier_hash,
  predecessor_broker_exit_receipt_hash,
  predecessor_broker_whole_job_reap_receipt_hash,
  predecessor_broker_route_spawn_audit_seal_hash,
  predecessor_broker_principal_retirement_receipt_hash,
  expected_head_revision, resulting_head_revision, previous_claim_id,
  previous_claim_hash, previous_claim_root_hash, resulting_claim_root_hash,
  claim_hash, created_sequence)` have `UNIQUE(head_id,generation)`, partial
  `UNIQUE(head_id,previous_claim_id)`, `UNIQUE(head_id,allocation_id)` and a same-head ordinal predecessor. The
  first claim has generation one and an explicit zero-predecessor terminal-
  barrier composite; every later `recovery-writer` claim has
  `generation=previous.generation+1` and composite-FKs the immediately previous
  writer-admitted generation's exact predecessor terminal barrier: predecessor
  exit, whole-job reap, RouteSpawn audit seal and principal retirement must all
  already be bound before the claim inserts. `claim_hash` excludes row ID,
  resulting root, its own hash, creation sequence and time and includes every
  allocation/reservation/predecessor-barrier semantic field; the resulting root
  domain-binds the previous root plus this claim ID/hash. Claim insertion,
  head count/root/current pointer and exact revision CAS commit together. That
  CAS has a closed generation-write rule: `arm-writer | recovery-writer` while
  `writer-open` set both `current_broker_generation` and
  `last_writer_generation` to the new claim generation; `control-attempt` sets
  only `current_broker_generation` and must preserve the already-frozen
  `last_writer_generation` scalar, while the drain closure's last-writer claim
  composite remains the immutable authority. No other action may write either
  head field. An in-place reservation appends no claim and leaves both
  values unchanged.
  A `recovery-writer` claim does not itself authorize a write: RouteFS/RouteGit
  writer-effect admission must prove `allowance-eligible ∧ armed ∧ writer-open ∧
  broker_generation = head.current_broker_generation`, so a stale live broker or
  a future generation can never obtain second-writer effect authority from mode
  bits alone.

  Claim kind is a closed `arm-writer | recovery-writer | control-attempt`
  oneOf. `arm-writer` is generation one and `recovery-writer` is legal only in
  `writer-open`; both require the exact writer-admitted allocation and null
  control reservation, but only `recovery-writer` requires the exact
  predecessor terminal-barrier composite while `arm-writer` requires the
  explicit zero-predecessor branch. `control-attempt` is legal only in `drain-closing |
  writer-drained-control-open`, requires one exact successor reservation and
  its precomputed allocation identity, and can never authorize a writer. The
  ID-only claim↔reservation reverse relation is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY
  DEFERRED` and checked at transaction commit: reservation hash is computed
  first, then allocation/claim hashes, and no reverse hash edge exists. An
  arm/recovery claim composite-FKs a materialized writer allocation immediately,
  and a recovery claim additionally carries the predecessor barrier FKs so
  successor claim ordering can never outrun predecessor exit/reap/audit/
  retirement.
  A control claim's allocation ID/hash is instead a precomputed reservation
  token: its reservation outcome must later bind either that exact allocation
  row or a `never-materialized` terminal receipt whose transaction anti-joins
  it. Until one outcome binds, the claim/reservation is nonterminal and blocks
  every final/release classifier.
  An
  in-place reservation reuses the current writer claim and therefore does not
  append or consume a generation; every new successor does. Generation is
  derived only from this claim chain—failed-reservation counts are never used as
  generation arithmetic. While `writer-open`, a dead current writer can
  transfer only to the exact next `recovery-writer` generation and every unused
  future broker generation's actor-slot head/capability remains open/
  preallocated—it cannot be classified never-selected, terminalized or closed
  early.

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_budget_exhaustion_receipts(

  resulting_head_revision, expected_fence_phase, expected_fence_revision,
  resulting_fence_revision, successor_requirement_kind,
  current_broker_generation, broker_generation_budget,
  current_generation_claim_id, current_generation_claim_hash,
  dead_broker_exit_receipt_hash, dead_broker_whole_job_reap_receipt_hash,
  dead_broker_route_spawn_audit_seal_hash,
  dead_broker_principal_retirement_receipt_hash, receipt_hash,
  created_sequence)` have unique head/fence. They are legal only when current
  generation equals the frozen budget, the exact broker is terminally closed and
  a generated successor-required predicate selects exactly one closed kind:
  `writer-recovery-required` at `writer-open`, `drain-root-controller-required`
  at `drain-closing`, or `release-controller-required` at `writer-drained-
  control-open`. Each kind independently proves the current allocation cannot be
  retained, no successful unclassified reservation/continuity is available and
  the phase-specific writer effect, drain-root or physical-release obligation is
  still unresolved; a caller boolean is never accepted. The owning head
  RecoveryAction inserts this receipt and atomically CASes the exact expected
  head phase/revision to `manual-conflict` plus the exact expected fence `armed |
  release-pending` revision to `conflict-containment-pending`; no retry loops on
  an impossible claim. Receipt hash
  includes every listed semantic field except row ID, its own hash, creation
  sequence and time.

  Immutable `git_publication_required_effect_no_write_observations(id,
  publication_id, required_effect_ordinal, required_effect_hash,
  route_operation_id, target_ordinal,
  git_continuity_qualification_id, git_continuity_qualification_hash,
  result_verification_identity_hash, observation_challenge_hash,
  expected_generation_head_id, expected_generation_head_revision,
  effect_authority_count, effect_authority_root_hash,
  effect_authority_revision_root_hash,
  live_or_inflight_effect_authority_count,
  live_or_inflight_effect_authority_root_hash,
  expected_after_existence, expected_after_mode,
  expected_after_identity_hash, expected_after_content_hash,
  observed_after_existence, observed_after_mode,
  observed_after_identity_hash, observed_after_content_hash,

  normalized row is precomputed and inserted only by the drain-seal transaction

  effect-no-write-challenge-v1", {publicationId,requiredEffectOrdinal,
  requiredEffectHash,routeOperationId,targetOrdinal,
  gitContinuityQualificationId,gitContinuityQualificationHash,
  resultVerificationIdentityHash,expectedGenerationHeadId,
  expectedGenerationHeadRevision,effectAuthorityCount,

  caller nonce. The qualified observer durably keys its one immutable result by
  that challenge, so retry/query returns the same receipt rather than resampling
  a later favorable target. Expected/observed after tuples are
  exact-equal to the frozen target; semantic-effect count/root is zero/canonical-
  empty. The authority set is the complete normalized projection of every
  allowance/generation/actor/action that could perform that required effect;
  its revision root binds the generation head plus every relevant actor-head,
  capability and backend-saga revision. Live/in-flight count/root must be zero/
  canonical-empty. Every raw observation selected for one seal batch names the
  same generation-head revision and authority/revision roots. The drain-seal
  transaction revalidates those exact values, inserts all normalized
  observation plus `already-applied` result rows, recomputes the result-missing
  projection and CASes `writer-open -> drain-closing` once; any intervening
  claim, issue, delivery or action intent makes the whole batch stale. Thus the
  CAS fences every future claim at the same linearization point and the
  observations prove no already-authorized writer can act afterward.
  `observation_hash` includes every listed semantic field and
  excludes only row ID, its own hash, creation sequence and clock time.

  Immutable `git_publication_required_effect_results(id, publication_id,

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_drain_intents(id,

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_drain_intent_members(

  satisfying_fence_scope_effect_ordinal,

  `UNIQUE(drain_intent_id,required_effect_hash)`. The frozen logical required-

  matchingScopeEffectCanonicalHash})`. Required count/root are generated from this projection and can never

  `applied | already-applied`; each member composite-FKs the exact immutable

  domain and domain-specific empty value. Result/member IDs never enter either
  identity root. `satisfied_required_effect_root_hash` is the
  separate ordered projection of those same leaves.
  Success requires `required_effect_count = satisfied_required_effect_count =
  member_count` and `required_effect_root_hash =

  lastWriterGenerationClaimHash,
  requiredEffectCount,requiredEffectRootHash,satisfiedRequiredEffectCount,
  satisfiedRequiredEffectRootHash,positiveEffectAdmissionRemainingCount,
  positiveEffectAdmissionRemainingRootHash,memberMissingCount,

  ID, its own hash, creation sequence and clock time are excluded.

  The head's positive-effect remainder is the generated ordered anti-join of the
  frozen logical required-effect universe against normalized required-effect
  results, not against not-yet-created drain members. Each missing-result row
  has canonical hash `H_D("publication-writer-required-effect-result-missing-v1",

  the seal transaction inserts those normalized rows, recomputes it to zero plus

  never asks a projection over absent drain members to equal zero.

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_broker_generation_drain_closures(id,
  head_id, fence_id, drain_intent_id, drain_intent_hash,
  expected_head_revision, resulting_head_revision, last_writer_generation,
  last_writer_generation_claim_id, last_writer_generation_claim_hash,
  required_effect_count, required_effect_root_hash,
  satisfied_required_effect_count, satisfied_required_effect_root_hash,
  positive_effect_admission_remaining_count,
  positive_effect_admission_remaining_root_hash, member_missing_count,
  member_missing_root_hash, member_count,

  drain intent. `closure_hash = H_D("publication-writer-drain-closure-v1",

  satisfiedRequiredEffectCount,satisfiedRequiredEffectRootHash,
  positiveEffectAdmissionRemainingCount,
  positiveEffectAdmissionRemainingRootHash,memberMissingCount,

  creation sequence and clock time are excluded. It is the immutable success authority for the head transition and
  composite-FKs the exact intent/member roots; the mutable head pointer alone is
  never accepted downstream.

  `seal-publication-writer-recovery-admission` is one transaction from
  `writer-open` to `drain-closing`: it inserts that complete drain intent/member
  set plus the immutable drain closure, stores both composites on the fence/
  head and CASes the head. It freezes `last_writer_generation` and its claim
  composite to the exact current `arm-writer | recovery-writer` claim; later
  control-attempt claims may change only `current_broker_generation`. For every
  pending `already-applied` candidate it revalidates the raw no-write
  observation's common expected generation-head revision, complete authority/
  revision roots and zero live/in-flight projection, then inserts every
  normalized observation/result in this same CAS. It is eligible only when
  every required logical publication effect has an exact terminal `applied`

  `positive_effect_admission_remaining_count=0` after those result inserts but
  before member insertion, and `member_missing_count=0` afterward; an intent or observation without its
  terminal result/member is not enough. The transition permanently denies another
  writer-generation claim. Only then may unused future generations be shrink-
  terminalized and their actor-slot heads closed; a broker replacement from
  then on is `control-attempt`, never writer-admitted.
  The `bind-current-publication-writer-drain-root` mutation branch of the sole
  head RecoveryAction `reconcile-drain-or-control-attempt` requires `drain-
  closing`, every
  actor-slot head closed and the immutable fence-global backend-terminal
  projection complete, then atomically binds the drain root and CASes this head
  to `writer-drained-control-open`. Control-attempt claims remain legal in that
  phase so a final/release-lost-ack broker can recover without reopening writer
  admission. The fence RecoveryAction `release-publication-writer-fence` alone
  owns the physical release-receipt transaction and CASes this head to
  `control-closed`; no later allocation or claim is legal. The head action is
  `writer-open -> maintain-or-seal-writer-recovery-admission`, `drain-closing ->
  reconcile-drain-or-control-attempt`, `writer-drained-control-open ->
  maintain-control-or-bind-release`, `control-closed -> noop`, `manual-conflict
  -> diagnose-only`. `maintain-control-or-bind-release` may own a legal
  pre-release successor reservation. Once the persisted release intent/result is
  bindable it only wakes/awaits `release-publication-writer-fence`; it may not
  write the head or fence revision. The fence action's one local transaction
  appends the release receipt and paired-CASes head `writer-drained-control-open
  -> control-closed` plus fence `release-pending -> broker-retirement-pending`.
  Neither action may mutate either revision in separate transactions; successor
  reservation and release bind still compete on the same expected head/fence
  revisions.

  Every in-place demotion or control-only process launch first reserves immutable
  authority in `git_publication_writer_fence_control_broker_reservations(id,
  fence_id, reservation_ordinal, reservation_kind,
  broker_generation_admission_head_id,
  expected_generation_admission_head_revision,
  resulting_generation_admission_head_revision,
  expected_fence_phase, expected_fence_revision,
  resulting_fence_phase, resulting_fence_revision,
  expected_current_continuity_receipt_id,
  expected_current_continuity_receipt_hash,
  expected_current_continuity_root_hash, target_broker_generation,
  generation_claim_id, generation_claim_hash,
  previous_reservation_id, previous_reservation_hash,
  previous_reservation_root_hash, resulting_reservation_root_hash,
  previous_terminal_attempt_receipt_id,
  previous_terminal_attempt_receipt_hash,
  previous_successful_continuity_receipt_id,

  `UNIQUE(fence_id,reservation_ordinal)`, partial
  `UNIQUE(fence_id,previous_reservation_id)`, partial
  `UNIQUE(generation_claim_id)` and at most one nonterminal
  reservation per fence. The append-only reservation root is recomputed from
  the same-fence predecessor plus this reservation ID/hash. Ordinal is one iff
  predecessor is null/canonical-empty; otherwise it equals
  `previous.reservation_ordinal+1`, and the fence reservation count equals the
  current ordinal. Reservation kind is
  `in-place-drain-root | post-death-drain-root | post-root-control-successor`.

  Reservation-kind phase mapping is closed. Both drain-root kinds require the
  fence `armed` and generation head `drain-closing` and can bind only an
  authenticated armed observation. `post-root-control-successor` requires
  generation head `writer-drained-control-open` and fence `armed | release-
  pending`. Under `armed` its total outcome is armed. Under `release-pending`,
  it binds the already-durable original release intent/key but does not guess
  its result: one immutable observation intent accepts the closed authenticated
  result `still-armed | released-or-tombstoned`. The first appends armed
  continuity and later resumes the same release intent; the second appends
  release-tombstone continuity and permits the release receipt bind. A state
  change between reservation commit and observation is therefore data, not a
  mismatched reservation kind. Resulting fence phase equals expected phase in
  every reservation transaction.

  Its canonical hash is computed before any new allocation/process/observation.
  It includes all preallocated allocation/RouteSpawn/claim/guard-intent/mailbox-
  binding/endpoint IDs, raw namespace/channel epochs, the precomputed control-
  audience template and every predecessor exit/
  reap/audit/retirement/handoff receipt hash. It excludes resulting reservation
  root and every current-reservation descendant hash: `generation_claim_hash`,
  the current `allocation_identity_hash`, `control_broker_audience_hash`,
  `continuity_guard_operation_intent_hash`, `writer_mailbox_binding_hash`, all
  three endpoint hashes, every later result pointer/hash, mutable phase/
  revision, created/settled sequences and clock time. Predecessor allocation/
  continuity/attempt identities remain included; the exclusion applies only to
  objects derived from this reservation. The topological order is fixed:
  preallocate IDs/raw channels and derive role-audience templates; hash the
  reservation; derive the reservation-
  scoped control audience and allocation identity; derive the guard intent,
  claim, mailbox binding and endpoint hashes; then insert the complete rows and
  head/root CASes in one deferred-FK transaction. No immutable row is patched
  after commit. Its insertion transaction keeps the fence phase unchanged, increments
  and records the exact fence/head revisions, and CASes the current-
  continuity pointer and generation-admission-head revision together with the
  reservation-root append and any successor claim; the physical release bind
  contends on those same fence/head revisions. An in-place reservation names
  the existing writer-admitted allocation and mailbox binding,
  has a null generation-claim composite and targets the current claim's
  generation. Its reservation transaction also CASes that allocation's exact
  expected state/revision and prior `current_control_broker_reservation_*` to
  this reservation and resulting revision; no independent retarget is legal.
  Successor reservations null those expected mutable-allocation fields until
  their one allocation materialization bind. Each successor reservation atomically appends the exact
  `control-attempt` claim and preallocates the only authority/mailbox binding
  allowed to create its `control-only-born` allocation. The successor mailbox
  binding and claim hashes are computed from the already-fixed reservation hash
  and stored only in excluded composite columns. The reservation's
  `bind-or-terminalize-unmaterialized-control-attempt` action has a closed
  materialization protocol. Its prelaunch transaction inserts or exact-replays
  the preallocated `reserved` principal allocation plus the exact RouteSpawn
  spec/child descriptor and birth-reservation composite, without a process-start
  or GO fact and without advancing the reservation. Its successful post-start
  transaction binds the exact RouteSpawn child/GO/process-start tuple, CASes
  allocation `reserved -> bound-to-process`, sets its immutable birth and
  current reservation composites, and CASes reservation `reserved -> allocation-
  bound` with the exact expected/resulting allocation revision. Its no-
  allocation and cancelled-before-child branches instead use the normalized
  terminal classifiers below. Every unique replay returns the same rows; no
  transaction may bind only allocation, process or reservation state.
  `previous_terminal_attempt_receipt_*` points
  only to the immediately preceding failed reservation's normalized terminal
  receipt; it is never a claim alias. The complete failed-attempt root contains
  every failed reservation, including repeated failed same-generation in-place
  attempts, while the separate failed-generation-claim root contains only failed
  successor reservations that consumed `control-attempt` claims.

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_control_broker_guard_operation_intents(

  `observe-armed-for-drain-root | reconcile-post-root-guard-for-continuity`
  oneOf. The drain-root branch nulls the target-release field and accepts only
  armed. The post-root branch under an armed fence also nulls it and accepts
  only armed; under `release-pending` it requires the exact persisted original
  release intent and accepts the total `still-armed | released-or-tombstoned`

  `git_publication_writer_fence_control_broker_guard_no_send_receipts(id,

  dispatch head/intent/reservation. Their transaction recomputes the canonical-
  empty dispatch projection and CASes `reserved -> cancelled-no-send`; receipt
  hash excludes row ID/hash/time. Immutable
  `git_publication_writer_fence_control_broker_guard_conflict_receipts(id,
  dispatch_head_id, operation_intent_id, operation_intent_hash, reservation_id,
  reservation_hash, backend_guard_observation_id,
  backend_guard_observation_hash, conflict_kind,
  expected_dispatch_revision, resulting_dispatch_revision,
  expected_reservation_revision, resulting_reservation_revision,

  RecoveryAction for the current dispatch
  phase alone inserts this receipt and in one transaction CASes dispatch and
  reservation to `manual-conflict` plus the fence to `conflict-containment-
  pending`; the parent may only wake/await it. In particular,
  `query-or-replay-control-guard-observation` owns the divergent-authenticated-
  result branch from `send-authorized`; a parent reservation action and
  `diagnose-only` may neither create nor repair that receipt. Receipt
  hash includes every listed semantic field except row ID, its own hash,
  creation sequence and time. A backend absence response, missing process or
  caller assertion is not no-send evidence. If a query after `send-authorized`

  and queries again. Once dispatch remains `send-authorized`, that exact exit is
  bound for the same reservation, and the same operation key still returns
  authenticated absent, the child action inserts one
  `send-authorized-exited-absent` conflict receipt and paired-CASes

  Reservation phase/action is closed: `reserved -> bind-or-terminalize-

    process-start row for the preallocated IDs;

  session composite. Neither branch may rewrite allocation identity merely to
  retry control. RouteSpawn spec, qualification and control channel repeat the
  applicable birth/template relation. The session audience has no RouteFS/RouteGit target, actor-slot admission,

  is authoritative without these members.

  Immutable `git_publication_writer_fence_allowance_phase_tuples(fence_id,

  null, zero/canonical-empty allowed effect and phase-tuple projections, and a
  denied projection exactly equal to the complete applicable universe.

  frozen RouteFS/RouteGit operation and target, one exact budgeted owner

  one allow effect member and current phase tuple; unmatched effects are denied.

  witness phase, operation, target, actor slot/binding, issued audience/fence and

  containment/manual recovery rather than an online scope extension. There is
  no broker, helper or recovery privileged bypass outside these rows;

  | `delivery-committed` | capability is issued and one exact mailbox envelope is durable; delivery acknowledgment may be lost | `reconcile-exact-allowance-delivery` |

  | `manual-conflict` | slot/continuity/query/effect/actor identity is ambiguous or divergent | `diagnose-only` |

  generation may bind; every unclaimed future generation returns a no-mutation
  wait and may not take the never-dispatched branch. After `drain-closing`, no
  writer claim is possible and those future broker slots may take only the
  shrink terminal branch. A generation consumed by `control-attempt` is likewise
  permanently ineligible for an allowance actor. The shrink transition and a
  competing generation claim CAS the exact same broker-generation-admission-
  head revision, so an
  early close cannot win independently.
  `prepare-or-terminalize-bound-allowance` has one closed decision over the
  already durable binding: if the actor/parent/phase tuple is still valid it
  appends the `prepare-intent` admission and exact prepare action intent; after
  that actor/control caller is fenced or the parent is invalid it instead
  creates the shrink-only terminalizer/outcome/predecessor/intent bundle from
  the absent slot and records stage `selected-before-prepare`. It cannot create
  a prepare intent merely to make revocation reachable. Each later issue-phase reconcile action
  may choose its already-frozen positive successor or atomically supersede it
  with the one terminal intent after the old control caller is fenced. The
  backend slot orders a racing delayed prepare/activation against terminalize:
  terminalize wins with a permanent tombstone, or the exact prepared/active
  identity is returned and then tombstoned—never a new key/identity. A terminal
  result whose high-water contains a previously unacknowledged physical effect
  first reconstructs the immutable Route operation-effect row from the exact
  backend identity; non-unique reconstruction is `manual-conflict`, never
  `revoked-unused`. A never-dispatched slot has no actor binding: if its
  preallocated actor materialized, it participates in that actor's finite
  admission-closing barrier; otherwise the same recovery action CAS-closes the
  exact admission head with a `never-materialized` zero-writer closure and advances directly
  to `actor-barrier-bound` with null barrier.

  `close-seal-and-bind-allowance-actor-terminal-barrier` is one resumable
  RecoveryAction with normalized local substate, not three hidden actions. If a
  materialized actor's closure is absent, one transaction verifies all sibling
  terminal results, CAS-closes its admission head and inserts the closure plus
  exact mailbox-seal intent; the saga remains `backend-terminal-observed`. It
  then queries/replays only that seal key until the authenticated observation
  binds. Routing is by frozen writer role, not by whichever allocation is now
  current. A RouteSpawn actor or historical broker whose generation is not
  `generation_head.last_writer_generation` inserts its ordinary barrier. A
  broker actor with `broker_generation = generation_head.last_writer_generation`

  head `reconcile-drain-or-control-attempt`, then waits for its
  `bind-current-publication-writer-drain-root` result. The fence action and the
  active in-place or post-death control reservation may also wake that head
  action but cannot own the root CAS. The head action alone,
  after every other head is closed, consumes the already-closed last-writer
  closure/seal, inserts the sole drain-origin barrier plus root continuity
  receipt and binds the barrier pointer for all affected sagas. Under `writer-
  open`, a broker becomes historical by first binding its exact retired-broker
  barrier; only after that barrier exists may a later `recovery-writer` claim
  win the same generation-head revision, so the two routes cannot invert or
  race into dual live writers.
  Lost acknowledgments at any substep return the same rows.
  A never-materialized head closes through its zero-writer closure and needs no
  mailbox call. Thus every materialized head has an enabling close action, and
  seal intent can never race a later delivery admission;

  The transaction entering `backend-terminal-observed` binds the final Route
  effect prefix and releases only the temporary parent tuple barrier; the
  capability/saga remain nonterminal and continue to block settlement,
  successor actor admission and any reuse until the actor barrier and semantic
  receipt bind;

  and enters `active`, or—after fencing that ordinal and observing actor/parent
  invalidity—commits the one terminal action intent while keeping the exact
  envelope immutable. It never interprets a missing acknowledgment as
  nondelivery and never allocates another ordinal. A later terminal effect may
  itself prove delivery, but only because its action intent was already durable
  and names that delivery row;

  Query and shrink-only terminalization authority belongs to the protected
  guard supervisor/allowance coordinator, not to a candidate, publication actor
  or successor broker. It can inspect one preallocated slot and force only
  `absent | prepared-inactive | active-sealed | terminalizing -> tombstoned`;
  it cannot prepare/activate a new slot, choose a different effect, mint an
  envelope or perform a writer effect on behalf of a dead actor. If an old
  actor's exact terminal action already won, the coordinator can only query and
  bind that result; otherwise it may request only the policy's zero-effect
  outcome. Terminal-intent commit already closes new dispatch; the backend slot
  CAS orders that supervisor request against any exact in-flight actor request,
  and the later actor barrier closes the physical channel after all tombstones.
  This shrink-only path breaks dead-
  broker recovery cycles without creating a privileged writer bypass;

  No phase transition claims a SQLite/backend transaction. The only SQLite
  multi-row binds are local: actor-slot admission/subject/head revisions,
  action/result composites, capability/receipt/delivery and parent pointers, or
  terminal head-closure/barrier/control-continuity/final pointers commit all or
  none. Backend prepare, activation, terminal effect/tombstone and actor-channel
  delivery are separate observed boundaries. Kill/lost-ack recovery always
  reuses the same action key, slot, actor and envelope; a new actor/key requires
  the prior slot tombstone and complete actor barrier. The hash direction is

  `reserved -> arm-next-git-hook-member-attempt`, `executing ->
  reconcile-current-git-hook-member-attempt`, `settled -> noop`,
  `conflict-containment-pending -> contain-git-hook-program`,
  `manual-conflict -> diagnose-only`, with terminal conflict permitted only after
  every owned RouteSpawn/job is reaped and its containment receipt sealed;
- Hook-program phase/action is `pre-object-pending ->
  reconcile-pre-object-git-hook-program`, `pre-object-settled ->
  reconcile-pre-object-settled-git-hook-program`,
  `post-commit-pending -> reconcile-post-commit-git-hook-program`, `settled ->
  noop`, `cancelled-before-ref-effect -> noop`,
  `conflict-containment-pending -> contain-git-hook-program`, and
  `manual-conflict -> diagnose-only`. Every vNext member is a RouteSpawn with
  exact settlement/reap/audit and read-only candidate index/message/tree inputs.
  Message- or index-modifying legacy semantics are explicitly unsupported in
  trusted mode; a write attempt or byte drift is contained/conflict, not silently
  accepted. Before the first pre-object RouteSpawn or commit-object, one complete
  program preflight validates all four members; any legacy-unsupported member,
  including post-commit, rejects with zero program child/object/ref effect.
  `reconcile-pre-object-settled-git-hook-program` has a closed parent-conditioned
  result: the exact stale/no-effect CAS moves it to
  `cancelled-before-ref-effect`; the exact index-publish bind installs the
  trigger and moves it to `post-commit-pending`; otherwise it returns typed
  waiting with zero mutation. Thus stale and publish do not provide two actions
  for one phase. Post-commit runs only
  after ref/worktree/index publication and must
  settle before the combined publication seal. For vNext dispatch, the final
  member result, chain execution `settled`, program `settled`, and copied
  post-commit receipt on saga/publication commit in one transaction; lost
  acknowledgment returns the same execution/result/receipt and cannot launch a
  second RouteSpawn. The absent branch performs the same parent/program
  transaction with no execution and a trigger/member-bound domain-separated
  empty receipt. Thus there is no child-settled/parent-receipt window.
  A post-commit negative result, input drift, actor/audit/reap ambiguity or
  receipt mismatch has one coordinated transition that first puts the exact
  execution/program, publication/saga and any live witness/lock owner into their
  matching containment phases. Hook actors are fenced/reaped/audited before
  publication resources close; no member may independently reach terminal
  `manual-conflict`, publication verification or kernel bind. Only after the
  combined containment receipt may all affected aggregates become matching
  `manual-conflict`;

  goal_lineage_hash, goal_contract_id, final_ref, head_key_hash,
  current_goal_contract_revision, head_attestation_id, head_generation,
  revision)` with one current row per stable goal-lineage/contract/ref,
  `UNIQUE(registry_id,project_id,checkout_id,goal_lineage_hash,goal_contract_id,
  final_ref)` and a composite unique key including that tuple plus
  `head_key_hash = H_D("goal-completion-head-key-v2",
  {registryId,projectId,checkoutId,goalLineageHash,goalContractId,
  canonicalRef})`.
  Draft `expected_head_key_hash` and attestation `goal_head_key_hash` are
  generated columns and full-tuple-plus-hash composite FKs equal to this
  recomputation and the selected head row; callers cannot supply them. Draft
  uniqueness and the attestation/head CAS use the recomputed composite key, and
  any repeated hash mismatch is integrity conflict. The canonical object
  encoding supplies field names, types and length boundaries; the property
  corpus includes every adjacent-field `("a","bc")` versus `("ab","c")`
  boundary vector rather than relying on delimiter-free concatenation.
  `run_id` is
  attestation/draft provenance only and cannot partition head authority; contract
  revision advances this one CAS row rather than inserting another current head;
- `goal_completion_attestations(id, completion_draft_id,
  completion_input_hash, goal_lineage_hash, goal_contract_id,
  goal_head_key_hash, goal_contract_revision, goal_git_baseline_id,
  goal_git_baseline_hash, ref_generation,
  ref_head_revision, reflog_anchor_hash, final_ref,
  final_commit_oid, final_tree_oid, final_git_saga_id,
  final_git_saga_settlement_id, final_git_saga_settlement_hash,
  approved_settled_git_transition_count,
  approved_settled_git_transition_root_hash, proof_set_hash,
  verification_freeze_id, verification_freeze_hash,
  verification_proof_root_hash, verification_lineage_count,
  verification_lineage_root_hash, verification_slot_count,
  verification_slot_set_root_hash,
  completion_verifier_attempt_policy_set_root_hash, promotion_proof_hash,
  execution_cell_hash, environment_observation_id, capability_grant_id,
  calibration_set_hash, receipt_head, config_hash, constraint_snapshot_hash,
  trust_closure_hash, supersedes_id, status, invalidated_by)`;
  Every task/final-goal/member settlement ID is an FK to the same saga's unique
  `GitSagaSettlementV1`, and every repeated hash/parent/commit/tree/final tuple
  must equal that immutable row. Its closed authority branch already proves the
  consumed manifest entry or two-key history-rewrite authorization; completion
  schemas expose no parallel caller-supplied cleanup or authority-transition
  field. Goal transition members may mix those settlement authority branches
  only in actual governed ref order. Task/goal drafts each have a unique exact completion-input/head-scope key;
  duplicate creation returns the original open/consumed draft. Slot/attempt,
  equivalence-owner, lineage and freeze membership/count/roots are recomputed
  from normalized rows rather than accepted as aggregate hashes;
- `approvals(id, purpose, audience_hash, approved_object_hash, nonce,
  key_id, state, consumed_sequence)` and append-only
  `approval_revocations(approval_id, reason_code, actor, sequence)`;
- `key_revocations(key_id, reason_code, actor, sequence)`,
  `receipt_revocations(receipt_id, reason_code, actor, approval_id, sequence)`,
  `waiver_revocations(waiver_id, reason_code, actor, approval_id, sequence)` and
  `calibration_revocations(calibration_id, reason_code, actor, approval_id,
  sequence)`;
- `proof_dependencies(source_kind, source_id, dependent_kind, dependent_id)`
  for transactional invalidation fan-out;
- `calibration_runs(id, project_id, checkout_id, candidate_snapshot_hash,
  candidate_tree_oid, stable_gate_id, profile_hash, mutation_spec_hash,
  trust_control_closure_hash, execution_cell_hash,
  environment_observation_hash, clean_before_attempt_id,
  mutation_attempt_id, clean_after_attempt_id, phase, current_calibration_id,
  fencing_token)`;
- `calibrations(id, run_id, candidate_snapshot_hash, stable_gate_id,
  profile_hash, trust_control_closure_hash, execution_cell_hash,
  receipt_set_hash, issued_at, expires_at, state, invalidated_by)` with one
  current fact per exact candidate/gate/profile/closure/cell tuple;
- `evaluation_opportunities(id, contract_revision, criterion_id,
  logical_change_set_id, causal_root_id, evaluation_cluster_id, cohort_key,
  selection_snapshot_hash, approval_id, status)`;
- `evaluation_clusters(id, project_id, candidate_tree, logical_change_set_id,
  causal_root_id, independence_class_id, cluster_fingerprint, approval_id,
  status)` with a unique externally derived default fingerprint;
- `constraint_feedback(opportunity_id, constraint_version,
  selection_snapshot_hash, exclusivity_group_id, outcome_value, state,
  supersedes_fact_id)` with a unique current-settlement key;
- `cohort_settlements(cohort_key, constraint_version, exclusivity_group_id,
  current_fact_id, outcome_value, state)` with a unique current cohort slot;
- constraint, feedback, receipt, chain, archive, and calibration tables defined
  in later sections.

Database checks make activation fields phase-dependent rather than accepting
empty placeholders: a protected head ID/hash is mandatory from
`reverse-flipped` through every active protected tuple; the reverse export pair
is mandatory from `reverse-verified`; the protected activation generation ID is
mandatory from `reverse-materializing` and its hash from
`reverse-materialized`. A normal protected open therefore cannot satisfy its
tuple with null, partial, or cross-intent identifiers.
For bootstrap-backed kernel targets, `activation_state` is closed to
`inactive | local-pending-bind | bind-barrier-armed |
external-bound-acknowledged | tombstoned | revoked`; only the exact
`external-bound-acknowledged`, a `bound` barrier and a verified final external
`bound` receipt can satisfy global eligibility. A non-null bootstrap
materialization requires its preparation/final receipt fields according to
phase, and a null
materialization forbids all bootstrap receipt/activation fields. The external
registry enforces unique materialization-to-target, one `active_repair_id`, one
nonterminal target repair and monotonic saga/repair fences. These constraints,
not a stored `state=current` label, prevent a locally activated target from
becoming authority.

Transactions use revision CAS and database-issued monotonic fencing tokens.
Lease time only makes an owner eligible for recovery; steal/renew/release always
CAS the current fencing token. Tests skew time backwards/forwards while stale
tokens remain unable to mutate state.

Lease scopes form a documented lattice: project-maintenance dominates workspace,
run, task/track, worker, projection, and external-effect scopes. A child scope
cannot outlive or override a fenced ancestor. A3 quiescence enumerates every
scope and blocks on any live descendant rather than checking task claims alone.

Canonical hashing uses a versioned JSON canonicalization specification, UTF-8,
Unicode normalization rules, and explicit handling of file mode, symlink,
submodule, tracked/untracked input, and allowed generated output. Legacy import
preserves both original byte hash and normalized semantic hash.

A0 freezes aggregate boundaries, maximum document size and hotspot split
thresholds; high-churn leases/receipts/feedback never live inside one growing
generic JSON document. The JSON adapter remains a supported legacy L1 reader and
pre-cutover writer, but receives no new L2 features; its retirement/capability
policy is explicit rather than an indefinitely duplicated transaction engine.

### 4.2 Backend qualification

SQLite remains the preferred durable backend, but A0/A1 must prove the selected
package rather than assume it.

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/durability-environment-class.schema.json`,
`execution-cell.schema.json`, `environment-observation.schema.json`,
`environment-observation-invalidation.schema.json`,
`backend-qualification-receipt.schema.json`,
`capability-grant.schema.json` and
`checkout-capability-state.schema.json`, plus
`backend-qualification-revocation.schema.json` and
`capability-grant-revocation.schema.json`. The pinned sidecar, not candidate code,
derives the execution cell and binds it into IPC hello, every receipt and every
capability decision.

An execution cell never means generic `Linux/x64/glibc`. Its externally
approved durability environment class constrains OS release and kernel ranges,
architecture, libc implementation/version, filesystem type/version, local vs
network storage, mount/locking options, container/VM storage driver, and the
required WAL/lock/fsync/file+directory-sync/atomic-rename probe specification.
At sidecar start, and again whenever mount/device/container identity changes or
the observation expires, the trusted probe records the exact environment and
proves it maps to one approved class. Unknown range, unsupported filesystem,
network mount, missing directory-fsync, lock/WAL divergence or failed probe is
`read-only-diagnosis`. Candidate code may not propose the mapping. Qualification,
soak and grants bind the class plus probe spec/hash; a receipt from another
class cannot be inherited merely because OS/arch/libc labels look similar.

| Candidate | Intended role | Known constraint | Decision gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `libsql` embedded | provisional maintained-Node primary candidate | SQLite-compatible fork; native platform package coverage must be proven; remote/sync features forbidden | qualify only if local-only WAL/FK/CAS/restart/concurrency and platform install matrix pass |
| `better-sqlite3` | fallback candidate | postinstall/native binding conflicts with current `--ignore-scripts` distribution smoke; supply-chain and prebuild coverage | qualify only with an explicit safe install policy and all platform receipts |
