| `node:sqlite` | optional version-gated adapter | unavailable on Node 20 and stability varies by Node release | may reduce native install risk on proven Node versions; never the sole adapter |
| `sql.js`/WASM | portability research only | no proven multi-process durable file transaction parity | cannot become default unless the full StateKernel contract passes |
| `sqlite3` | rejected pending reversal | current maintenance/deprecation concerns and native install cost | requires a new ADR to reconsider |

Qualification uses one packed tarball in Linux/macOS/Windows jobs across the
declared maintained Node lines plus a distinct Node 20 legacy-compatibility
cell that can never issue a backend-qualification or default-capability grant.
Receipt cells explicitly distinguish x64/arm64
and, on Linux, glibc/musl plus the approved durability environment class where
the runner exists; untested kernel/filesystem/mount classes are not implied by
an OS label. Qualification does not hide installation scripts with
`--ignore-scripts`. Each maintained-line qualification job must actually create/open the DB,
enable WAL and foreign keys, perform CAS and concurrent writers, restart the
process, inject a kill, migrate, rollback, and reopen. Claims are limited to the
matrix with receipts; unsupported platforms fail clearly or remain on the
legacy JSON adapter without being described as SQLite-capable.

A dedicated candidate `validate:backend-qualification` command may expose the
SUT fixture, but only the coordinator-owned external runner/oracle and CI matrix
produce trusted receipts; candidate verdicts, expected values and summaries are
ignored. The core package carries no unconditionally loaded native module. The
qualified adapter is a lazy optional dependency: JSON-only/help/diagnostic paths
must start when it is absent or installed with scripts disabled, while selecting
SQLite requires a successful adapter-load receipt. Native binaries are not
bundled into the project tarball; the current unpacked-size budget remains a
distribution gate (`unpackedSize <= 2,000,000` bytes). The selected dependency declaration and lazy-load behavior
are frozen by the A1 backend ADR before any default change.
The declaration must be `optionalDependencies` (or an equivalent
platform-scoped optional mechanism), never an unconditional production
dependency; only the adapter module may use dynamic `import()`, and absence,
ABI/load or install-script failure returns the typed lower capability without
breaking help/doctor/legacy reads.

The qualification harness is distinct from `validate:distribution`: the latter may keep its
script-suppressed quick smoke for supply-chain safety, but it is never backend
evidence. At revision-ten planning time, the
[official Node release table](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases)
marks Node 20 EOL, Node 22/24 LTS and Node 26 Current. The initial matrix is
Linux/macOS/Windows × Node 20 legacy + Node 22/24/26 qualification × available
x64/arm64, with glibc/musl split on Linux; support claims are narrowed when an
OS/architecture/libc/durability-class cell has no successful receipt.
Each maintained qualification-cell receipt records Node major/ABI, the approved
durability class ID and probe spec/hash, exact OS/kernel/arch/libc/filesystem/
mount/container observations, and a redacted deterministic environment
snapshot, exact package-manager/install command and script policy,
toolchain/prebuild source, backend module load, database/WAL/FK/CAS results,
kill/reopen and rollback results. Local-only candidates additionally record an
explicit remote/sync-disabled assertion and the negative URL/environment tests
that proved it. A successful install with a failed module load, remote denial,
or behavior test is `unsupported`, not qualified. A Node 20 job emits only a
typed legacy install/distribution/JSON smoke receipt; even a coincidentally
loadable native adapter cannot upgrade that receipt or authorize a post-cutover
mutation. No receipt or grant is inherited across a different Node major/ABI,
durability class/probe, backend-package hash or supervisor hash. The backend PR subset uses
Linux/Node 22 (the oldest maintained line) within the 15-minute budget; Node 20
keeps a JSON/manual distribution smoke. The full matrix is nightly/release and
records the release-schedule source so future lifecycle drift cannot silently
preserve a trusted claim.

A1 necessarily stages a new bundle when it adds StateKernel/adapters. The
current A0 supervisor/coordinator qualifies that exact inactive A1 artifact in
the fixture, then the successor authorization/install saga binds and activates
the same hash. If A2 or C0 changes any manager/launcher/RPC-client/
sidecar/dependency byte, it repeats that staged review/qualification/
authorization/install sequence and creates a different execution cell before
the track may merge or A3 may cut over. A shadow, A0 or earlier-bundle receipt
cannot be relabeled as evidence for the resulting A1/C0 bundle.

The provisional `libsql` adapter accepts local filesystem URLs only, rejects
remote URLs and `TURSO_*`/sync configuration, and is protected by an import
denylist outside the adapter. Static, dynamic `import()`, URL, environment and
runtime sync-client denial tests are all required. It remains merely a candidate
until matrix receipts pass.

The JSON adapter preserves current legacy operations. Its contract is split:

- L1 single-aggregate CAS and existing explicitly hardened transitions are
  supported;
- L2 arbitrary multi-aggregate atomicity, receipt/feedback transactions, and
  final vNext authority cutover require SQLite;
- unsupported operations return a typed capability error; tests may not infer
  parity merely from identical final projections.

Backend identities are not conflated. `legacy-json` names repository-local files
before first cutover only. `protected-json-v2` is the lossless reverse target: a
service-owned generation under the external state root, inaccessible to
candidate and pre-vNext processes, with repository JSON/YAML/Markdown remaining
projections. It supports only declared L1/manual capabilities; L2 state blocks
reverse. After first cutover, `legacy-json` can never appear in an authority row.
The authority backend enum is database-constrained to `sqlite |
protected-json-v2`; the legacy pre-authority case has no authority row.
`protected-json-v2` rolls document representation back, not the protected
supervisor/control-metadata prerequisite: post-cutover open and head CAS still
require the pinned sidecar and its qualified control database. Missing control
metadata is `diagnose-only`, never permission to infer authority from JSON.

No execution cell receives a new-install default grant until that exact cell's
qualification, cutover/fault and soak requirements pass. There is no global
backend-default boolean. Failure leaves only that cell downgraded and requires
an ADR revision before any claimed equivalence-class substitution.

Capability levels are explicit and reported by `state doctor --json` and
cockpit. One canonical policy computes the effective level as the minimum of the
checkout backend maximum, the current exact execution-cell qualification and
default grant, sandbox/trust-control state, and required per-gate calibration;
a stored label alone is never authoritative. Before taking that minimum, every
bootstrap-backed factor must pass
`isBootstrapTargetGloballyEligible(...)`; a locally activated/current factor is
otherwise treated as absent, never provisional evidence for a stronger level:

`backend_max_level` is only a representation ceiling: active SQLite writes
`full-trusted`, while active protected JSON writes `protected-json-manual`.
Writing the SQLite ceiling grants nothing by itself; absent downstream factors
still evaluate to `sqlite-provisional`. Conversely no downstream grant can lift
the protected ceiling. This makes D2 promotion a current-factor change, not an
ambiguous mutation of the authority backend ceiling.

| Level | Required predicates | Allowed / forbidden boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `full-trusted` | active SQLite document authority; irreversible finalization and the exact maintained execution-cell per-cell default grant are current and, when bootstrap-backed, each has an exact globally eligible bound receipt; current backend qualification, C0 sandbox, C1 contracts/proofs and every required C2 calibration are current | governed unattended worker/gate/approval/commit, `TaskDone`, `GoalComplete` and calibrated learning may run |
| `sqlite-provisional` | active SQLite authority and exact cell qualification/C0 are current, but finalization, production grant, C1/C2 trust closure or required calibration is incomplete | state/core tests and explicitly authenticated L1/manual flows may run; only a finalized checkout with the separately scoped `candidate-execution` capability may create L2 candidate receipts; no unattended approval/commit/trusted terminal or automatic learning |
| `protected-json-manual` | active `protected-json-v2` authority plus exact maintained control-DB cell qualification/C0 | L1/manual state and observational projections only; L2 receipts/feedback/calibration, trusted terminal and unattended commit are forbidden |
| `legacy-json-manual` | no post-cutover authority row; repository-local legacy JSON | compatibility plan/check/manual nontrusted result only; no vNext trusted terminal or automatic learning |
| `read-only-diagnosis` | missing, unsupported, revoked or mismatched execution-cell/control predicates | doctor, qualification and migration-plan inspection only; no production mutation |

Migration authority is a separate transient capability rather than a circular
use of `full-trusted`. `migration-qualified` requires the exact maintained
execution-cell backend receipt and current environment observation, C0 boundary,
quiescence predicates and a signed
single-use migration/finalization manifest. It may execute only the frozen
forward/reverse/finalize saga; it grants no worker, gate, approval, commit or
terminal operation. A bootstrap-backed first-adoption intent additionally
requires its exact globally eligible bound receipt before the open/forward
dispatcher may select it. Thus first adoption can move from `legacy-json-manual` to
SQLite, while an unqualified/manual runtime cannot invoke migration merely by
claiming a steady-state level.

Candidate production is also non-circular. An operation-scoped
`candidate-execution` capability requires active SQLite, exact cell
qualification plus an unexpired matching environment observation, C0
containment, a current irreversible-finalization record, an approved current
plan/task contract, and
either the production default grant or an externally signed
qualification-fixture grant. Any bootstrap-backed finalization or grant must
also pass the global-eligibility predicate and bind its final receipt hash in
the operation capability. It permits only an isolated worker, gates and the
known-bad calibration needed to create candidate-scoped evidence; it cannot
approve, update a Git ref, commit trusted state, settle learning feedback or
mint any Done status. Candidate-specific calibration is therefore an output of
this restricted capability, not a prerequisite for starting the worker that
produces the candidate. Only after those receipts are current can the separate
`full-trusted` approval/commit/terminal operations run.

Grant scope is closed to `production | qualification-fixture`. A
qualification-fixture grant is short-lived, signed by the previous trusted
supervisor, and binds one external runner, project/checkout, execution cell,
candidate release, fault manifest and test purpose. It may exercise the full
terminal path only inside that disposable runner so C2/D2 can test the path
before a production grant exists; `canCount*` rejects it in every production
audience. The resulting soak report can support a new production grant, but the
fixture grant itself cannot be promoted, copied or have its audience widened.

All levels allow `state doctor`, `state qualify` and `state migrate --plan`
read-only. Only
`migration-qualified` may apply/rollback/finalize. `candidate-execution` may run
the contained worker/gate/calibration prefix; `full-trusted` alone may run
unattended approve/commit/terminal/learning. Other provisional/manual flows
require explicit human intent and remain nontrusted; `read-only-diagnosis`
rejects every mutation.

`schemas/vnext/state-doctor-output.schema.json` and
`state-migration-plan-output.schema.json` freeze JSON output, capability/error
codes, exact execution-cell hash, qualification/default-grant IDs and expiry,
downgrade reasons, irreversible-finalization/reverse status, bootstrap
authority/rotation seal, target-saga/local/global activation state and final
bound-receipt hash, route inventory, live effects, proposed mutations and
rollback matrix.

A1 may implement adapters and a shadow sidecar, but no production worker/gate
path receives a control capability before C0 passes. Backend/platform failure
selects the lower declared level; it never silently emulates a higher level.
Existing JSON-only `check:*` commands remain available under the explicit
`legacy-json-manual` capability and emit a machine-readable downgrade event.
No existing PR gate silently starts requiring SQLite; only the separately named
backend/state-fault profiles may require a qualified SQLite cell until vNext is
explicitly granted for that exact execution cell.

### 4.3 Migration phases and authority transfer

Migration is deliberately separated from writer conversion:

1. `state doctor` inventories files, schemas, writers, locks, live processes,
   hashes, legacy trust, projection generations, and rollback capability.
2. `state migrate --plan` emits a deterministic manifest only.
3. A1 implements `shadow-import`: import and verify without an authority marker,
   default switch, or writable SQLite path.
4. A2 moves every existing registered writer behind StateKernel while JSON
   remains authoritative, adds generation metadata, and enforces architecture
   lint. Its shadow schema includes broker-generation heads/claims/budget-
   exhaustion receipts, normalized required-effect/no-write-observation/results
   and drain intents/members/closures, control reservations/guard dispatch/no-
   send/guard-conflict/no-allocation-or-process attempt outcomes, mailbox bindings/endpoints/head-
   serialized seal intents/observations, continuity and post-final release
   suffix members. Migration may reconstruct those rows only from exact existing
   normalized facts and authenticated receipts; it never backfills authority
   from an aggregate hash or prose inference. A legacy in-flight publication
   missing any composite is quarantined/read-only or `manual-conflict`, not
   grandfathered as drained/sealed. New L2 receipt/feedback features remain
   dark and unwritable.
5. Only A3 may run `state migrate --apply` authority cutover.
6. C1/B2a/B2b/C2 add live L2 trust/feedback features only after A3 establishes one
   SQLite authority.

Operator UX is non-interactive and machine-readable: `state doctor --json` and
`state migrate --plan --json` list every live lease/external effect, proposed
action and rollback capability. `state migrate --apply --conflicts=fail|drain
--timeout-ms N --approval-manifest PATH` either drains within the bound or exits
nonzero without cutover. No “force success” mode exists. Finalization consumes a
separate authenticated approval manifest and prints the exact capability loss.

The migration approval manifest is signed by the pinned trust root, single-use,
and binds the exact plan hash, current/target authority epoch, monotonic nonce,
expiry, conflict mode and timeout. Reuse, drift or expiry fails closed. The
irreversible-finalization manifest additionally enumerates every surrendered
rollback capability and requires a second independent trust-root approval.

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/irreversible-finalization.schema.json`. Finalization
is the only production transition allowed to surrender reverse capability. An
ordinary post-bootstrap finalization uses one kernel transaction to
verify/consume both distinct approvals, bind the current authority epoch and
rollback-capability-table hash, write the complete
`irreversible_finalizations` record, and change the checkout capability policy
from `reverse-available/L1-only` to `l2-enabled/reverse-surrendered`. For the
initial bootstrap-backed finalization, target preparation writes only the inert
record; the target saga's final kernel acknowledgment is the corresponding one
transaction that binds the final external receipt and changes this policy.
Before an ordinary record is current or a bootstrap record is globally
eligible, every reverse-blocking L2 writer—including receipt chain,
constraint feedback, calibration, TaskDoneProvisional/TaskDone and goal
attestation—fails before allocating an ID or external attempt. A later L2 write
cannot be the event that silently removes rollback.

`candidate-execution`, C1/B2a/B2b/C2 production paths and full-trusted capability all
require this finalization record and, when it is bootstrap-backed, its exact
global-eligibility receipt. A locally activated but unbound finalization neither
surrenders reverse nor permits any L2 writer. Their code may merge dark beforehand; tests
use a disposable, fixture-scoped two-key finalization that cannot authorize a
production checkout. Once production finalization commits, reverse remains
disabled even if L2 rows are later archived or revoked; doctor/cockpit prints
the exact surrendered set and approval IDs. Conversely an unfinalized checkout
with no L2 state retains the reverse matrix. This is a runtime activation gate,
not an implicit delivery-track dependency.

During A2, production mutations update only the JSON authority adapter. The
SQLite shadow is immutable validation output and is never incrementally written,
queried for control decisions, or used to block/approve work. A2 conversion has
a module checklist for sprint-board, loop, parallel runner, intent, Colony,
observability/eval, plan-review, orchestration/workspace, human-board and config
proposal paths. Journals/JSONL are regenerated idempotently from kernel audit
rows rather than appended in place.

The checklist explicitly includes `auto-pilot-orchestrate.mjs`,
`worker-launcher.mjs`, `auto-pilot-plan-from-goal.mjs`, `goal-backlog.mjs`,
`scripts/lib/gate-trust.mjs`, `scripts/auto-pilot-gates.mjs`,
`scripts/auto-pilot-intent.mjs`,
`scripts/auto-pilot-intervene.mjs`, `scripts/auto-pilot-observe.mjs`,
`scripts/lib/eval-history.mjs`, `scripts/va-parallel-runner.mjs`,
`scripts/auto-pilot.mjs`, the `bin/va-auto-pilot.mjs` router, and every evidence
materializer in `auto-pilot-loop.mjs`, in addition to the modules above. It
specifically converts intent/parallel journal appends and every
`gates maintain --apply` config write into kernel audit or reviewed proposal
effects. In an adopted project, `init --force` may not overwrite config,
`package.json` scripts, templates or trust-control data directly; it emits a
signed reinitialization proposal. `state doctor --json` compares live static/runtime writer discovery to
the checked registry; any nonempty diff blocks A2 merge.

A2 also migrates terminal semantics across every existing surface: state enum,
loop, orchestrated phases, parallel runner, recovery, sprint-board CLI, MCP,
templates, distribution validation, schemas/protocol fixtures and all tests.
It introduces `ReadyToCommit` and `GitBoundUntrusted`, prevents direct `Done`
updates without a bound Git saga plus a C1-approved task contract/proof, and
imports historical Done items as display-only
`legacy-completed` evidence unless an exact commit/tree binding is reconstructible.
Legacy completion never counts toward a new goal contract.

`GitSagaV1` exists during A2 with `receiptHead: null` and a mandatory
`terminalSagaPolicyVersion`; exact parent/ref/tree/commit binding is already
required. A successful bind reaches `GitBoundUntrusted`, never Done. C1 upgrades
the contract to require a non-null receipt head/current task contract and is the
first phase allowed to reach `TaskDoneProvisional`. C2 is the first phase that
may exercise calibrated `TaskDone` with an external fixture-scoped grant; D2 is
the first phase that may activate it for a release execution cell. Pre-C1 results are re-proven or
remain nonterminal after C1 activation; missing/not-current C2 calibration can
never be interpreted as merely “not revoked.”

C0 qualifies the trust boundary before A3. It installs the pinned sidecar and
worker sandbox, proves the candidate cannot open/mutate the control DB/WAL,
socket/pipe, approval store, supervisor bytes or manager handles, and proves the
trusted manager can still perform scoped operations. The receipt must show an
OS-enforced denial, not path secrecy. On a platform without a qualified adapter,
A3 cutover and all worker/gate/approval/commit operations are unavailable; only
read-only migration diagnosis remains.

A3 enters a persistent maintenance phase, blocks new leases/outbox work, fences
existing owners, and waits for or explicitly halts live workers. Quiescence
requires no live lease, no pending/in-flight required outbox effect, no
unobserved Git saga/index lock, no DocStore mutation, and no gate/receipt append.
Every fenced process must also be reaped or proven dead; a recorded fence alone
does not quiesce a non-cooperative JSON/Git writer. The project-maintenance lease
is exclusive and concurrent migrate/apply/finalize attempts fail closed.
An unresolved external effect must be an explicit terminal manual conflict. A3
takes a final snapshot only after quiescence. `authority` is a SQLite row committed with the
first authoritative revision; a small discovery hint may exist on disk but is
not a commit point. Hint/DB disagreement fails closed and `doctor` repairs from
the DB authority row.

The first authoritative SQLite revision is built only after quiescence and the
exclusive maintenance lease. A1 shadow bytes are diagnostic only; mismatch
fails closed and a shadow without an authority row is never production input.

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/activation-intent.schema.json`,
`activation-seal.schema.json`, `authority-row.schema.json`, and
`reverse-export.manifest.schema.json`,
`protected-json-generation.manifest.schema.json` and
`protected-json-write.schema.json`, plus the closed
`recovery-action.schema.json`. Durable control paths are
`$STATE_ROOT/projects/<projectId>/checkouts/<checkoutId>/activation/intent.json`,
`seal.json`, and `freeze-gen/<generationId>/MANIFEST.json`. Intent fields include
`activationSubphase`, candidate epoch, generation/route-set hashes, lease owner
and fencing token. The authoritative pre-cutover intent is an
`activation_intents` record in the protected control database, committed in the
same transaction as the maintenance lease; `intent.json` is a signed/fsynced
mirror, never the only crash oracle. Seal/generation file records use
fsync+rename durable writes and content hashes.

`authority.phase` is closed to `activating | active | reverse-transition |
manual-conflict`. The first forward authority transaction installs
`phase=activating`; only the final exit transaction may set `active`. Recovery
first derives one `effectiveActivationSubphase`: before an authority row exists
it comes from that protected control record; after the authority row exists its
DB value takes precedence and intent files are only repairable mirrors. Normal
production open is legal only for the tuple `(phase=active,
activationSubphase=none)` with no extant maintenance lease; every unfinished forward
or reverse tuple is recovery-only. An impossible phase/subphase tuple is
`diagnose-only`, never a fallback backend choice.

Each matrix below states the exact commit boundary for advancing its subphase;
there is no global write-ahead shortcut. Recovery is a function only of the last
committed, validated tuple. Dispatch first applies this closed tuple table; a
non-matching tuple stops at `diagnose-only` and never reaches subphase dispatch:

| Authority source | Backend | Phase | Allowed subphase set | Maintenance lease | Dispatch class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no authority row and no control intent | legacy JSON | n/a | `none` | absent | normal legacy open |
| control intent, no authority row | legacy JSON input only | pre-authority | `intent, inventory, freeze-partial, freeze-verified, importing` | extant | subphase recovery |
| authority row | protected JSON v2 | `activating` | `intent, inventory, freeze-partial, freeze-verified, importing` | extant | subphase recovery |
| authority row | SQLite | `activating` | `activated, sealed, projected` | extant | subphase recovery |
| authority row | SQLite | `reverse-transition` | `reverse-intent, reverse-export, reverse-verified, reverse-materializing, reverse-materialized` | extant | subphase recovery |
| authority row | protected JSON v2 | `reverse-transition` | `reverse-flipped, reverse-projected` | extant | subphase recovery |
| authority row | SQLite | `active` | `none` | absent | normal SQLite open after authority/seal validation |
| authority row | protected JSON v2 | `active` | `none` | absent | normal protected open only after the fixed control-root head ID, sealed manifest, every document hash, graph hash and route-set hash exactly match the authority row; otherwise `diagnose-only` |
| control intent, no authority row | legacy JSON input only | pre-authority | `manual-conflict` | extant | `diagnose-only` |
| authority row | SQLite or protected JSON v2 | `manual-conflict` | `manual-conflict` | extant | `diagnose-only` |

The subphase enum is closed and, only after tuple validation, maps each value to
exactly one action:

| Subphase | Unique recovery action |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | normal backend open selected by the validated tuple |
| `intent` | `resume-inventory` |
| `inventory` | `resume-inventory` |
| `freeze-partial` | `resume-freeze` |
| `freeze-verified` | `resume-import` |
| `importing` | `rollback-uncommitted-import-and-resume-import` |
| `activated` | `resume-seal` |
| `sealed` | `resume-project` |
| `projected` | `verify-and-exit-maintenance` |
| `reverse-intent` | `resume-reverse-export` |
| `reverse-export` | `resume-reverse-export` |
| `reverse-verified` | `resume-reverse-materialize` |
| `reverse-materializing` | `resume-reverse-materialize` |
| `reverse-materialized` | `resume-reverse-flip` |
| `reverse-flipped` | `resume-reverse-project` (recovery-only) |
| `reverse-projected` | `verify-and-exit-maintenance` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

Every recovery mutation first acquires the exclusive project-maintenance lease
with fencing CAS against the epoch and route-set hash carried by the selected
record; failure returns read-only diagnosis. `diagnose-only` performs no
mutation. `RecoveryAction` is the union of this table and the named saga actions
in the external-effect/fault annex; generic `resume` is not a valid value. No
prose alternative may override this table.
`verify-and-exit-maintenance` is not an untyped shared implementation: the
validated authority backend/phase chooses the forward or reverse verifier and
its distinct manifest predicates before any mutation.

A migration maintenance lease spans an epoch switch explicitly: before the
switch its current `authority_epoch` equals `transition_source_epoch` and it
carries the target epoch plus `epochTransitionId`. The
reserved source epoch `0` represents first-adoption legacy JSON and is never a
post-cutover writer epoch. The
forward activate or reverse flip DB transaction atomically installs the new
authority epoch, rewrites the lease's current epoch to the transition target
with a fresh fencing token, and
updates authority/activation-intent fencing fields. The transaction commits old
tuple/old lease or new tuple/new lease as a unit. The prior token cannot mutate;
recovery reads the committed tuple and CASes only its matching lease epoch.
Authority-epoch changes are limited to these forward/reverse maintenance sagas.
Routine goal, constraint, config, policy and trust revisions use their own
monotonic revisions/hashes and transactional invalidation; they cannot bump the
authority epoch around an in-flight external effect. A future new epoch-changing
saga must reuse the same quiescence/lease-rebind contract and extend the pinned
fault manifest before it is callable.

The forward matrix is normative:

It covers both first adoption and a later reactivation after a completed reverse.
First adoption atomically creates the control intent with the maintenance lease;
reactivation atomically CASes an existing `(backend=protected-json-v2, phase=active,
subphase=none)` authority row to `(phase=activating, subphase=intent)` with that
lease. Applying forward to an already active SQLite epoch is an idempotent
diagnostic no-op. The activate transaction inserts or CAS-updates the authority
row against the exact expected backend/epoch; it never guesses from files.

| Operation | Durable entry subphase | Exact advance boundary | Non-cooperative writer rule | Action while entry persists |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter maintenance | no intent | maintenance-lease CAS and protected `intent` write complete before inventory starts | all governed mutation denied | signed entry operation; a surviving `intent` selects `resume-inventory` |
| start inventory | `intent` | CAS to `inventory` before the first scan | no writer admitted | `resume-inventory` |
| finish inventory/arm freeze | `inventory` | only a complete writer/route/FD scan allocates and persists one database-issued `generationId` while CASing to `freeze-partial`, before the first freeze copy | enumerate, reap and prove dead every registered writer; timeout has no force | `resume-inventory` |
| freeze authority graph | `freeze-partial` | protected generation, sentinels and double-read verification complete before CAS to `freeze-verified` | any sentinel overwrite, FD write, hash/graph drift leaves entry phase unchanged | `resume-freeze` |
| record semantic conflict | `freeze-partial` | one transaction records the deterministic finding hash and CASes the pre-authority control intent (first adoption) or authority row plus intent (reactivation) to subphase/phase `manual-conflict` | fixed paths remain non-authoritative maintenance surfaces; no further freeze/import step is eligible | `diagnose-only` |
| arm import | `freeze-verified` | CAS to `importing` before opening the transaction | shadow DB ignored | `resume-import` |
| import/activate authority | `importing` | one DB transaction atomically commits documents, selects SQLite, sets the representation ceiling `checkout.backend_max_level=full-trusted`, binds generation/graph/route-set hashes, installs authority epoch with `phase=activating`/subphase `activated`, and rebinds maintenance lease/intent with a fresh fence; this ceiling is not a grant, so missing exact-cell/default/C1/C2 predicates still compute `sqlite-provisional` | no JSON/SQLite writer starts during maintenance | `rollback-uncommitted-import-and-resume-import` |
| seal | `activated` | protected seal is durable and verified before DB CAS to `sealed` | legacy writes become integrity conflicts only | `resume-seal` |
| project | `sealed` | projection/hint generation is durable and verified before DB CAS to `projected` | projection writes cannot change kernel truth | `resume-project` |
| exit | `projected` | after all bindings verify, one DB transaction sets `phase=active`, subphase `none`, releases the maintenance lease and enqueues intent-mirror cleanup | new governed writes start only after that transaction | `verify-and-exit-maintenance` |
| diagnose conflict | `manual-conflict` | external signed repair creates a new intent/epoch | no mutation by recovery | `diagnose-only` |

The final snapshot is exactly the protected canonical byte generation created
while the same lock generation remains continuously held through import and
authority commit. A corpus process that bypasses an advisory lock may overwrite
a fixed path, but it cannot alter the protected source; the sentinel/integrity
guard aborts pre-commit or classifies post-commit drift. This is the required
forward exclusion mechanism, not an assumption that old writers honor locks.

Quiescence mechanically requires all lease-lattice checks plus those exclusive
path locks, dead/reaped inventoried writer PIDs, no foreign Git index lock/saga,
and drained external effects. Failure to acquire any lock within the bounded
drain timeout means no cutover; there is no force mode. The packed legacy corpus
attacks these locks during quiescence and the projection/integrity boundary
after cutover.

The writer inventory is the union of lease owners, corpus-entrypoint processes,
all live open-FD writers for every registry canonical path/file identity, and all
observed dynamic-route invocations. For every authority identity, an exclusive
lock and no-live-FD predicate must hold; every observed route is either globally
reserved to this registry or quarantined standalone. Alias/hardlink attacks and
a second manager are mandatory A3 fault rows.

The protected route service reserves canonical path, parent generation root,
and current device/inode or Windows File ID across all projects and checkouts.
Before freeze it performs an OS-level open-handle scan for every reserved file
identity and generation root, re-resolves all route aliases, and CASes only an
expected atomic-replacement identity. An uninspectable handle table, hardlink,
cross-project alias, changed parent identity, or live writable handle makes the
platform/cutover unsupported; an advisory lock alone never closes this check.

The normative open algorithm resolves a fixed external control-root mapping,
activation intent/seal, opens the fixed control database when present, and
reads its `authority` row. For an active `protected-json-v2` tuple it derives
the generation path only from `authority.protected_json_head_id`, verifies the
sealed generation manifest and every content/graph/route-set hash against that
row, and only then opens the adapter. It never accepts a repository route,
projection pointer, directory scan or caller hint as the protected head. A repository hint is
only a projection; missing/stale hint never selects legacy JSON,
`protected-json-v2`, or SQLite. Hint
materialization is its own recoverable kill point and mtime is never consulted.

Before granting any production lease or dispatch, the pinned sidecar derives
the current execution-cell hash and requires an exact current qualification for
that Node major/ABI, approved durability class and unexpired matching environment
observation, release artifact, backend package and supervisor.
The effective capability policy then requires the matching per-cell default
grant and current calibrations for `full-trusted`. Node 20 is hard-capped at
`legacy-json-manual` before cutover and `read-only-diagnosis` after cutover,
regardless of whether a native module happens to load. A missing, revoked,
expired or other-cell receipt denies production mutation; neither
`minimum_writer_version` nor successful DB open substitutes for this check.

The open decision table is executable: absent mapping/activation intent selects
legacy JSON/init; shadow DB without authority and without activation intent is
read-only while production selects legacy JSON; any pre-authority activation intent
first passes global eligibility when bootstrap-backed and otherwise remains
read-only; only an eligible intent enters the one action selected by its
persisted subphase and never normal open;
an authority row with `phase=activating|reverse-transition` enters only the
subphase recovery action and denies ordinary leases/outbox/task mutation; only
`phase=active, subphase=none` selects its backend for production after the
backend-specific predicates in the tuple table pass. A finalized activation
seal plus missing/corrupt/mismatched DB, or a missing/corrupt/mismatched
protected head, fails closed without fallback. Unknown or
inconsistent phase/subphase, epoch/writer mismatch, duplicate checkout, any
extant maintenance lease under an active tuple,
`phase=manual-conflict`, or hint disagreement is
`diagnose-only`. Every pre/post-authority cell has an injected-kill fixture,
including `activated`, `sealed`, `projected`, `reverse-flipped` and
`reverse-projected`, and asserts that production mutation is rejected.

Every post-cutover transaction/outbox/lease must CAS `authorityEpoch`. A process
started before the barrier cannot commit afterward. Pre-vNext binaries are not
supported as writers after cutover. A3 tests a real packed pre-vNext CLI.
Control state remains protected by the external sandbox/service boundary;
attempted legacy projection/Git writes become integrity conflicts and cannot
change kernel truth. Fixed legacy paths either contain a cross-version
fail-closed migration sentinel proven against the finite compatibility corpus
frozen in A0 (named package artifacts/versions), or
cutover is refused. No fixed-path multi-file view is claimed atomic for unaware
readers, and it never exposes authoritative terminal/approval decisions.

Kill-order recovery is specified for: shadow import, maintenance entry,
quiescence, final snapshot, DB authority commit, each projection generation,
manifest-pointer/hint switch, outbox ack, Git saga bind, archive segment seal,
rollback export/reverse-authority switch, and epoch switch. Each
point is assigned exactly one named action from the frozen recovery enum in the
fault manifest; generic “resume/rollback” choices and “pick the newest file” are
invalid specifications.

Rollback first seals an immutable versioned export bundle, verifies every table
and artifact, then materializes and verifies a distinct protected JSON
generation before the authority-head/epoch flip. Repository projection pointers
switch only afterward and remain observational. Reverse enters the same
maintenance/fencing barrier. If constraints, feedback, receipt anchors, or
schema features cannot be represented losslessly, rollback is refused. Before
the first irreversible feature is used, the operator must run
`state migrate --finalize --irreversible` with explicit approval.
Before finalization, reverse-authority has an explicit export → verify →
protected-generation materialization → head/epoch transition matrix. L2-only state blocks reverse unless
the rollback capability table proves lossless representation.

The reverse matrix is normative:

Reverse entry requires exactly `(backend=sqlite, phase=active,
subphase=none)`, no extant maintenance lease and no completed irreversible
finalization before its entry transaction. A bootstrap-backed finalization is
"completed" here only if the global-eligibility predicate verifies its final
bound receipt; an inactive, local-pending or external-bind-prepared row cannot
block reverse.
An active protected-JSON backend, unfinished phase, or existing lease is
diagnostic and cannot enter reverse.
The entry transaction also proves that no live or historical L2-only receipt,
feedback, calibration, trusted task/goal terminal or other unrepresentable row
exists. Such a row without finalization is an integrity violation (because its
writer should have failed); either it or a valid finalization refuses reverse
before `reverse-intent`. This predicate is rechecked under quiescence
immediately before flip, closing a race with late L2 settlement.

Reverse never promotes repository files back to authority. A0 freezes
`schemas/vnext/reverse-export.manifest.schema.json` and
`schemas/vnext/protected-json-generation.manifest.schema.json`. A3 writes the
sealed export bundle under
`$STATE_ROOT/projects/<projectId>/checkouts/<checkoutId>/reverse-exports/<reverseExportId>/`
and materializes the candidate graph only under
`$STATE_ROOT/projects/<projectId>/checkouts/<checkoutId>/json-authority/generations/<generationId>/`,
inside the already qualified control-root boundary. The generation ID is bound
before its first byte, and candidate/pre-vNext processes cannot open, rename or
link that root. Repository state/board/journal/constraint files remain
observational projections, so their bytes or Git-index status cannot influence
backend selection or kernel truth. After activation, only the trusted service
may mutate the protected JSON graph through its L1 adapter. Legacy handoff is
not a vNext operation and cannot inherit trusted state or receipts.

The immutable reverse export and the protected activation generation are two
different objects. `reverseExportId/reverseExportHash` identify the canonical,
lossless source bundle. `protectedJsonActivationGenerationId` and its generation
hash identify the graph materialized from that exact bundle. The activation
intent binds both pairs; the authority row preserves the export provenance and
uses the activation generation as its initial protected head. The flip
transaction binds these IDs/hashes plus route-set and graph hashes and sets
`authority.phase=reverse-transition`; open is recovery-only until the final
`verify-and-exit-maintenance` transaction verifies the already switched
protected head, sets phase `active` and subphase `none`, and releases the
maintenance lease. Projection verification alone never activates protected
JSON. Thus a kill after flip cannot expose an unverified graph.

| Operation | Durable entry subphase | Exact advance boundary | Concurrent-writer rule | Action while entry persists |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter reverse maintenance | `none` | one DB transaction acquires the maintenance lease and sets `phase=reverse-transition`, subphase `reverse-intent` before quiescence | all other mutation denied and processes reaped | signed entry operation; a surviving `reverse-intent` selects `resume-reverse-export` |
| arm export | `reverse-intent` | complete quiescence allocates/persists one database-issued `reverseExportId` while CASing to `reverse-export`, before the first export-bundle write | SQLite remains document authority | `resume-reverse-export` |
| export and verify bundle | `reverse-export` | write/fsync the complete lossless bundle, seal its manifest, and persist `reverseExportHash` before CAS to `reverse-verified`; lossy capability atomically sets phase/subphase `manual-conflict` | SQLite remains document authority | `resume-reverse-export` |
| arm materialization | `reverse-verified` | one DB transaction allocates `protectedJsonActivationGenerationId`, binds the exact sealed export ID/hash, and CASes to `reverse-materializing` before the first protected-generation write | protected JSON normal open remains denied | `resume-reverse-materialize` |
| materialize protected graph | `reverse-materializing` | materialize only from the bound export bundle; write/fsync and hash every protected JSON document/manifest, then persist the activation-generation hash while CASing to `reverse-materialized` | SQLite remains document authority; repository routes are projections only | `resume-reverse-materialize` |
| flip authority | `reverse-materialized` | re-hash both the sealed export bundle and protected generation and re-prove that no unrepresentable L2/trusted terminal exists; only then may one DB transaction select `protected-json-v2`, set checkout backend maximum `protected-json-manual`, invalidate cached/full capability projections, preserve export provenance, install the protected head ID/hash, bind graph/route-set hashes, bump epoch, record `reverse-flipped`, and rebind maintenance lease/intent with a fresh fence; mismatch records `manual-conflict` | stale SQLite writers fail epoch/fence CAS; protected JSON normal open remains denied | `resume-reverse-flip` |
| switch projection pointer | `reverse-flipped` | materialize/verify repository projections from the protected source, switch their observational pointer, then DB CAS to `reverse-projected`; phase remains `reverse-transition` | projection or Git-index drift cannot alter authority | `resume-reverse-project` |
| activate protected JSON and exit | `reverse-projected` | re-hash the protected generation and authority binding; only then may one DB transaction set `phase=active`, subphase `none`, release maintenance and enqueue projection/intent repair | only the trusted service writes protected JSON after that transaction | `verify-and-exit-maintenance` |
| diagnose reverse conflict | `manual-conflict` | external signed repair creates a new intent/epoch | no mutation by recovery | `diagnose-only` |

The effective-capability policy always rechecks the current authority backend.
No SQLite qualification/default grant survives a reverse flip as permission for
trusted work: a still-running control DB or sidecar can support protected L1
mechanics but cannot raise the checkout above `protected-json-manual`.
`canCountAsTrustedProof()` and `canCountGoalCompletion()` include this backend
maximum as a current dependency. Reverse is refused while an actual L2/trusted
terminal exists; when only an unused full/default grant exists, the flip
atomically lowers the checkout maximum so no cached green capability survives.

There is no interval in which SQLite-authoritative and protected-JSON-authoritative writers
both succeed. Finalize, sentinel creation, concurrent migrate/apply, archive seal,
commit-object creation, ref CAS and kernel bind each have an explicit fault row.

Steady-state protected JSON writes are copy-on-write; a generation is immutable
once sealed. Write state is closed to `prepared | materialized | bound |
manual-conflict`. The adapter never edits the current head in place. Under the
checkout writer lease, the first control transaction validates the active tuple
and authority epoch, persists the bounded canonical mutation bytes/schema/hash
with the exact base head, allocates a target ID, and records
`protected_json_writes.state=prepared` before any target byte. Materialization
builds and verifies a complete target from only that durable record, with no
caller memory/request dependency, then records `materialized`. One final control transaction CASes the
authority epoch/current head from the frozen base to the exact target ID/hash,
updates the graph and route-set hashes to the target manifest's persisted
values, and records `bound`; only this transaction makes the mutation
authoritative, releases the checkout's nonterminal-write slot/lease, and only
afterward may the API report success. The immutable bound row remains history
but does not block the next write. A
partial or complete but unbound target is unreachable data and can be rebuilt
or garbage-collected by ID; it is never selected by scan or mtime.

The closed write recovery map is `prepared →
resume-protected-json-materialize`, `materialized →
resume-protected-json-bind`, `bound → noop`, and `manual-conflict →
diagnose-only`. The bind action accepts only the exact frozen base/head/epoch;
concurrent or divergent identity records `manual-conflict`. This protocol keeps
the immutable reverse activation binding as audit provenance while the
authority row's protected head advances verifiably with normal L1 mutations.

Legacy import policy is strict:

- original files/lines and byte hashes are preserved with importer version and
  mapping decision;
- unknown-governance constraints become `legacy-unverified/probation`;
- legacy evidence becomes `legacy-untrusted` and cannot enter the canonical
  receipt chain, feedback, promotion, or calibration;
- malformed lines, duplicate IDs, semantic conflicts, or fake PASS history are
  quarantined and block cutover.

### 4.4 External effects and projections

Outbox states are `pending | in_flight | done | dead_letter |
dead_letter_resolved`. A0 freezes
`schemas/vnext/external-effect.schema.json` and
`schemas/vnext/external-effect-attempt-closure.schema.json` plus
`schemas/vnext/external-effect-dead-letter-repair.schema.json`; every effect type names a bounded
apply operation, an independent observation oracle, idempotency key, ambiguity
policy and required receipt fields. Arbitrary shell text is not an effect type.
Recovery is closed:

| Persisted outbox state | Unique `RecoveryAction` |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | `drain-outbox-pending` |
| `in_flight` | `reconcile-outbox-in-flight` |
| `done` | `noop` |
| `dead_letter` | `reconcile-dead-letter-disposition` |
| `dead_letter_resolved` | `noop` |

Attempt recovery is separately closed: `reserved ->
dispatch-external-effect-attempt`, `dispatched ->
reconcile-dispatched-external-effect`, `applied ->
close-applied-external-effect-actor`, `applied-closed ->
bind-outbox-effect-done`,
`closed-no-effect -> reopen-outbox-after-attempt-closure`, and `ambiguous ->
dead-letter-ambiguous-external-effect`. The reopen action verifies the immutable
closure and old target commit fence in the same CAS that clears
`current_attempt_id`; it cannot run on an absence observation alone.

`reconcile-outbox-in-flight` never treats a point-in-time absence observation as
permission to replay. Every registered effect type freezes one recovery class:
`target-idempotent`, `fenceable-actor`, or `nonretryable`. Under the effect-scoped
lease, `drain-outbox-pending` first CASes `pending` to `in_flight` and creates the
immutable attempt identity, external idempotency key, actor/job/session and
commit-fence reservation before invocation.

Recovery is closed. Exact applied identity first records `applied`; every
process-bearing positive attempt must bind its exact applied receipt, actor exit,
whole-job/session reap, principal retirement and RouteSpawn effect/audit seals in
the recovery-class-specific positive closure. A fenceable actor additionally
advances/consumes its target fence and binds the target's linearizable no-late-
commit barrier. Target-idempotent and nonretryable actors do not invent a target
fence, but their process closure is equally mandatory. Only `applied-closed`
atomically records parent `done`; an observed positive effect with a live,
unreaped or unaudited actor remains `in_flight`. A durable
no-send/no-actor proof may close the same attempt as `closed-no-effect` and return
the outbox row to `pending`. `target-idempotent` may redeliver only the exact same
attempt/key while remaining `in_flight`, and only when the qualified external
target durably deduplicates that key across process restart and exposes a
linearizable query. `fenceable-actor` may create another attempt only after an
`ExternalEffectAttemptClosureV1` binds cancel/fence, actor/job/session reap and a
linearizable post-fence no-late-commit barrier from the effect target. A mere
“absent now”, observer timeout, lost actor identity, or any target without those
semantics becomes `dead_letter`; it never CASes back to `pending`. The old
attempt's fence is checked by every target commit, so a late actor cannot win
after closure. `nonretryable` always dead-letters uncertainty.

Dead-letter history is never erased or casually reopened. A separate
`ExternalEffectDeadLetterRepairV1` owns one exact row and one signed repair
disposition: `bind-observed-applied | successor-after-proven-no-effect |
cancel-dependent-transition`. Its recovery is closed:

| Dead-letter repair phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | exact dead letter, dependency, mode, signed semantic authority, prior attempt/closure and complete repair-history roots frozen | `prove-dead-letter-repair-precondition` |
| `precondition-bound` | late applied identity, linearizable no-effect/no-late-commit barrier, or exact dependency-cancel authority is bound | `apply-dead-letter-repair-disposition` |
| `successor-pending` | one transaction-created exact-equivalent successor effect with signed authority and parent repair is current; old actor remains fenced | `reconcile-dead-letter-successor` |
| `settled` | original row is `dead_letter_resolved` with immutable applied/successor-done/dependency-cancelled outcome | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | proof, actor fence, dependency, successor or outcome diverged; sticky terminal repair owner remains unresolved | `diagnose-only` |

`bind-observed-applied` requires the exact old effect identity. A successor is
legal only after the old attempt's cancel/fence/reap and target-side linearizable
no-late-commit barrier. Its exact signed semantic authorization binds the parent
dead letter, dependency, effect type, canonical payload, expected external
identity and effect-equivalence hash. The precondition transaction derives and
creates the successor row itself; caller-selected existing IDs or changed
payload/equivalence are rejected. V1 permits successor depth at most one for the
whole lineage; a successor dead letter may only bind its exact observed apply or
cancel the dependency, never spawn another successor. This is a new actor/
idempotency generation for the same effect, not replay of an uncertain actor or
result resampling. `nonretryable` uncertainty cannot select successor mode and
must cancel its dependent transition or remain unresolved. The main outbox row
reaches `dead_letter_resolved` only in the same transaction that binds the
terminal repair outcome and the complete ordinal/parent/history root. A
`manual-conflict` remains the terminal current owner and no later repair can
change mode or hide it.

`canCountExternalEffectSatisfied()` is the only positive predicate. It accepts
only direct `done`, exact `bind-observed-applied`, or an exact successor `done`
bound through its terminal repair/history root. `dependency-cancelled` never
satisfies the effect: its settlement transaction must atomically move the exact
dependent aggregate to its typed closed negative state and bind that receipt.
`terminal_resolution_kind` is derived from mode plus observed result, never
caller supplied. Without a valid repair row,
`reconcile-dead-letter-disposition` leaves the row blocking and emits the exact
required operator action rather than guessing.

Git is explicitly excluded from this generic outbox and uses the dedicated saga
below. Human annotation uses instruction/content CAS. Other required effects
must qualify one of the three exact recovery contracts before registration.
Retries are bounded; unresolved dead letters block the dependent transition and
appear in cockpit with commands that create/observe the typed repair above.

Receipt/archive sealing is also explicit: a content-addressed segment is
written and verified while `archive-preparing`, then one catalog CAS records
`archive-sealed`; restore verifies adjacent anchors before exposure.
`archive-preparing` maps to `resume-archive-seal`, `archive-sealed` to `noop`,
and any anchor divergence to `diagnose-only`. Shadow import similarly maps its
untrusted incomplete generation to `restart-shadow-import`; it can be discarded
because it is never an authority input.

Recovery dispatch is scoped by aggregate plus persisted saga phase, not merely
by a filename or generic operation type. A steady-state projection uses
`resume-projection-pointer`; an A3 projection uses its activation subphase
action. Authority-epoch changes are never a standalone recovery choice: each is
atomic inside its owning forward/reverse/policy saga and inherits that saga's
single action.

Projection output is a complete versioned generation containing
`authorityEpoch`, source revision/range, canonical content hashes, and minimum
reader/writer versions. Files are written and verified before one manifest
pointer switches. New consumers fail closed on stale generation. Unaware old
consumers are observational only after SQLite cutover and may not dispatch,
approve, or write.

`run-journal.md`, sprint boards, state JSON, constraint YAML, evidence/eval
JSONL, plans, snapshots, and heartbeat files are projections. There are no
unlocked append writers after A2.

Runtime config remains external input. Existing adaptive-gate mutation is
replaced by an explicit reviewed config proposal/outbox operation; candidate or
learned code cannot silently rewrite trust-control configuration. Applying a
proposal triggers the bootstrap trust-control policy and a new contract/config
hash.

`ReadyToCommit` crosses a dedicated commit-approval aggregate before any Git
saga. Human selection originates only from the real public `orchestrate
approve-commit --tasks ...` invocation; task IDs are deduplicated by first
occurrence (`B,A,B -> B,A`). Automatic selection is an internal branch of the
persisted `orchestrate await-workers` operation after exact worker settlement;
it freezes `selectCommitReadyTasks` in authoritative sprint order and never
fabricates approve-commit argv. A separate sorted stable-identity projection is
used only for membership equality.

The selected source/profile builds the isolated candidate-integration
preparation/chain. The manifest cannot enter `prepared` until that exact
preparation is `settled` and bound. For automatic mode, the immutable final
manifest payload and exact member rows are frozen before policy evaluation. The
pure evaluator's deterministic output is included in one kernel transaction:
`auto-approve` inserts `approval-pending` manifest + decision + preallocated
signing operation `prepared`, while `human-required` inserts that terminal-
waiting manifest + decision with no signing operation. There is no payload-only
or decision-only orphan. The exact policy snapshot, risk/gate/file
context, decision, approval scope and protected signing operation all reverse-
bind that payload. Journal output is only an admission projection,
never pre-signing authority. `approvedObjectHash` is exactly the immutable
`CommitApprovalManifestV1` payload hash; decision, signature and lifecycle fields
are outer metadata and cannot hash themselves. One kernel transaction verifies
the closed mode selector/source, current policy and signature, consumes the
nonce, CASes the ref-level head, stable batch owner and manifest `prepared ->
current`, creates the first entry's exact preallocated `GitSagaV1(prepared)` plus
all dependency edges, and leaves every later saga ID frozen but absent. Ack loss
returns the same manifest/saga.

| Commit-approval manifest phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval-pending` | exact payload/member rows and source mode frozen; human envelope absent, or automatic decision/signing operation is exact but not yet bound | `reconcile-commit-approval-evidence` |
| `human-required` | automatic decision durably requires human; no automatic signer/envelope can authorize it and owner/claims remain pinned | `await-human-commit-approval` |
| `prepared` | exact human or automatic approval envelope is bound; approval nonce unconsumed and no Git saga | `admit-exact-commit-approval` |
| `current` | exact approval/nonce consumed and exactly the current ordinal's prepared-or-later Git saga owns progress | `reconcile-current-commit-approval` |
| `consumed` | every ordered saga is `settled` with exact settlement and released broker writer fence; each task reached `GitBoundUntrusted`, and every authority/prefix transition plus physical closure is exact | `noop` |
| `stale` | an ordinary pre-current-entry-effect context drift was durably recorded with exact terminal consumed-prefix/remaining-suffix/no-ref-effect roots; owner and ReadyToCommit claims remain pinned and old approval can never revive | `await-fresh-commit-approval` |
| `superseded` | an automatic human-required manifest was atomically replaced by the exact same-batch human successor; its decision is consumed and immutable | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | head/manifest/saga/ref/object identity is missing, forked or divergent | `diagnose-only` |

`reconcile-commit-approval-evidence` observes a human envelope or drives only the
preallocated automatic signing operation; a crash at any signing phase returns
the same operation. It CASes to `prepared` only after object/scope/policy/key/
fence equality. A `human-required` decision can never be reinterpreted as
automatic PASS. A later real approve-commit invocation may atomically create a
human selection/successor `approval-pending` manifest, CAS the ref head/current
manifest, consume the old decision and move the old automatic manifest to
`superseded`, but only with exactly equal execution, membership, source,
preparation and candidate roots. Competing successors admit one; lost
acknowledgment returns it. Any changed member/order requires the existing
two-key replan transaction, never mode switching.

`reconcile-current-commit-approval` never mints a selectable saga. It resumes the
linked exact Git saga. Only after the exact publication verification, external
cleanup, actor/reap/lock/witness closure, final five-part revalidation and still-
armed broker writer fence are durable may one kernel transaction create the
unique `GitSagaSettlementV1`, move publication/saga to
`settlement-committed`, advance the manifest ordinal and consumed-prefix
count/root, and create the next preallocated saga as
`blocked-predecessor-fence`—or record the final prefix pending fence closure.
The sole recovery action releases the exact broker fence; its closure
transaction moves the prior saga/publication to `settled`, unblocks the next
saga as `prepared`, or consumes the manifest after the last entry. The exact expected ref/commit prefix produced by
earlier entries is valid progress; any other ref/reflog transition is handled by
the Git continuity conflict rules. A manifest may become `stale` only while the
current saga is before publication reservation and has no publication actor,
integration/guardian/index lock, ref-lock attempt, child or GO that could later
publish any approved effect. Its hook program must be `pre-object-pending` or
`pre-object-settled`, every started member must have exact no-GO/no-exec or
exit/reap/audit closure, and no execution may remain live; post-commit trigger
ID/hash/row and receipt must all be null. The stale transaction CASes the exact
manifest, head, saga, hook program and fencing token together, moves saga and
program to `cancelled-before-ref-effect`, and records one no-ref-effect proof.
An active child is first closed through its exact lifecycle and cannot be
abandoned by the stale CAS. Creation of the
publication reservation races on the same tuple: stale-first prevents any helper
or staging actor; publication-first permanently denies stale for that entry and the exact approved saga
must finish or conflict. Task/track/result/file/evidence/DocStore settlement/plan/
checkpoint/route/policy/contract/proof drift observed after that boundary is
recorded as dependency invalidation, so the exact commit may bind but can never
become trusted completion. The stale transaction freezes the complete Git-bound
entry-hash prefix and the exact ordered suffix of original ordinal/task identity/
ReadyToCommit transition/claim. A fresh approval is a successor on the same
batch owner, must reference the exact current stale predecessor and payload,
inherits an exactly equal consumed prefix, and proves its remaining execution
root equals that predecessor suffix. It creates sagas only for the suffix and
never rewrites or replays committed entries. Each stale predecessor has at most
one active successor by predecessor/head/owner revision CAS. Adding, removing,
reordering or replacing a member requires the two-key batch-replan authorization,
which atomically closes the old owner/claims and creates a new owner; another
run/cycle or ordinary reapproval is not a replan. Zero/multiple heads,
absent/divergent linked saga, claim conflict or object-hash mismatch is
`manual-conflict`. `commit` observes/drives this aggregate and may recompute a
diagnostic comparison, but may not rebuild a new manifest as authority.
Automatic admission uses that same final transaction but only after its exact
automatic decision/signing lower saga is bound. `--waive-approvals`, dry-run and
`--no-commit` produce explicit nontrusted outcomes and cannot create a current
trusted manifest, Git saga, `TaskDone` or `GoalComplete`.
An unadopted/non-Git checkout may initialize and run nonauthorizing work, but it
cannot enter `ReadyToCommit`, create a commit batch/manifest or reach a trusted
terminal. It records a typed `git-adoption-required` manual outcome and must
complete `state route attach|adopt` before a fresh plan/checkpoint/ReadyToCommit
transition; null Git/ref fields are never a compatibility spelling of approval.

Human intent uses a stable embedded instruction ID. A manually authored item
without one is assigned an ID only under exact-byte CAS; duplicate text remains
distinct. Fingerprints detect content drift but are not identity. An annotation
outbox entry includes expected ID/content/checkbox state. Concurrent edits move
it to `dead_letter/needs-human` rather than checking the wrong line.

Git and DocStore remain independent domains. Git uses a dedicated saga, never a
generic outbox row. Saga mode is closed to `normal-commit | history-rewrite`.
Both record intent, object-scoped approval, expected old ref and expected
parent/ref/worktree plus receipt head. Normal commit binds the manifest candidate
snapshot; history rewrite instead binds its exact approved object bundle and
current two-key authorization. For `normal-commit`, expected old
ref equals the expected parent and the saga must be the exact current entry of a
current `CommitApprovalManifestV1`; history-rewrite uses its separate two-key
authorization and requires commit-approval fields null. For `history-rewrite`, the expected commit's
parent may differ, but the ref update still names one exact old OID. Its closed
phase table is:

Before a ref becomes governed, the external Git helper qualifies and pins its
exact Git version/runtime, object format, transaction-lock support, config
fingerprint, reflog format/storage behavior and retention policy. An established
ref must already have the exact retained ref log, real storage identity and
sealed anchor. A genuinely unborn symbolic branch instead freezes generation
zero, exact ref/log absence receipts and a synthetic genesis anchor; absence is
legal only in that closed branch and is never confused with an empty established
segment. The reviewed first-create path uses `--create-reflog` and must prove the
exact first entry for both SHA-1 and SHA-256. Bare, disabled, replaced,
unretained or otherwise unclassifiable continuity is
`git-continuity-unsupported`. Every approval, `prepared` saga and phase action
binds/rechecks the qualification receipt, helper/config/object-format hashes and
the branch-appropriate real or genesis identity. A platform/repository that
cannot retain this witness is read-only for trusted Git operations.

| Persisted Git phase | Required protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blocked-predecessor-fence` | manifest entry is preallocated but predecessor settlement is only `settlement-committed` and its broker writer fence/release broker is not fully released/retired; the exact predecessor release-closure transaction alone CASes this saga to `prepared` (or consumes the final manifest), so this action only observes/waits and has no independent unblock mutation | `await-predecessor-writer-fence` |
| `prepared` | exact mode/authorization/metadata/tree/parent/old-ref/ref plus protected head revision/generation/reflog anchor frozen; commit may be absent | `resume-git-commit-tree` |
| `commit-object` | exact deterministic commit exists; no publication is reserved and stale still races on the same owner tuple | `reserve-git-integration-publication` |
| `publication-reserved` | one exact lower publication owns the source and is `reserved | locks-held | staged`; stale is permanently denied and no ref effect exists yet | `reconcile-git-publication-staging` |
| `publication-staged` | one exact publication owns all locks, before/after intents, staged after-images and candidate real index; protected continuity and real worktree/index before roots still match | `resume-git-ref-cas` |
| `ref-updated` | ref/reflog effects equal the exact publication outcome; worktree/index publication may be incomplete | `resume-git-worktree-publication` |
| `worktree-published` | every worktree intent has one exact applied/already-applied result and complete/untouched after roots match | `resume-git-index-publication` |
| `index-published` | real `index.lock` is consumed, exact index bytes and ownership witness are durable, and the unique post-commit trigger/program is pending or settled | `reconcile-post-commit-and-seal-git-publication` |
| `publication-verified` | one held-lock receipt reverified ref, every reflog intent/result, commit tree, symbolic HEAD, worktree scope roots and real index bytes | `resume-git-kernel-bind` |
| `kernel-bound` | one kernel transaction bound the verified publication, advanced protected continuity and reached `GitBoundUntrusted`; actor/witness/advisory-lock cleanup runs while the broker writer fence remains armed | `finalize-git-publication` |
| `settlement-committed` / fence `release-pending` | cleanup plus final five-part revalidation, unique settlement and authority/manifest-prefix transition committed; physical guard release/tombstone is not yet bound and next saga is blocked | `release-publication-writer-fence` |
| `settlement-committed` / fence `broker-retirement-pending` | physical release receipt is exact; current broker exit/reap/audit/principal retirement and atomic release closure remain, with next saga still blocked | `finalize-publication-writer-fence-broker` |
| `settled` | broker fence release plus broker exit/reap/audit/principal-retirement closure is exact and any next saga is unblocked; no publication resource remains | `noop` |
| `cancelled-before-ref-effect` | owning manifest won before publication reservation; hook program is atomically cancelled from a closed pre-object state with null post-commit trigger/receipt, and exact no-actor/no-lock/no-ref/worktree/index-effect proof/fence are durable | `noop` |
| `conflict-containment-pending` | divergence is frozen but an owned actor/descriptor/lock/artifact may remain | `contain-git-publication-conflict` |
| `manual-conflict` | conflict/containment receipts are sealed and every owned actor/descriptor/lock is closed; foreign evidence is preserved | `diagnose-only` |

Ref update is only the durable roll-forward point, never Git-saga success. A
normal commit may kernel-bind only when the governed ref, complete reflog effect
set, `commit^{tree}`, real integration worktree and real index form one verified
five-part publication owned by the same saga. A ref already at the expected
commit while the worktree or index is old therefore resumes the exact
publication; it cannot return success, roll the ref back, or sample a new tree.

The nested `git_integration_publications` recovery is closed independently:

| Publication phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | saga/manifest stale CAS lost; exact owner and empty effect roots exist, but no external lock/effect is assumed | `acquire-git-publication-locks` |
| `locks-held` | integration, guardian and real-index publish locks plus owner marker are exact; before roots are revalidated | `stage-git-publication` |
| `staged` | immutable path intents, staged after-images and candidate index are fsynced; real ref/worktree/index remain at exact before state | `resume-git-ref-cas` |
| `ref-observed` | exact ref/reflog outcome is observed and bound; worktree member publication has not completed | `resume-git-worktree-publication` |
| `worktree-publishing` | an append-only prefix of intent results is durable; the next member accepts only exact-before or exact-after | `resume-git-worktree-publication` |
| `worktree-published` | every intent result and touched/untouched after root verifies | `resume-git-index-publication` |
| `index-published` | consumed-lock receipt, exact candidate bytes, live ownership witness and post-commit trigger are bound; program completion precedes the combined seal | `reconcile-post-commit-and-seal-git-publication` |
| `verified-held` | the five-part publication verification receipt is sealed while integration/guardian locks and the published-index witness remain held; no real index lock is claimed | `resume-git-kernel-bind` |
| `kernel-bound` | protected bind committed; external actor/witness/advisory-lock cleanup is not yet complete and writer fence stays armed | `finalize-git-publication` |
| `settlement-committed` / fence `release-pending` | cleanup/final-revalidation/settlement are exact; physical broker fence release remains | `release-publication-writer-fence` |
| `settlement-committed` / fence `broker-retirement-pending` | release effect is bound; broker exit/reap/audit/retirement closure remains | `finalize-publication-writer-fence-broker` |
| `settled` | writer fence is released and its broker-retirement closure receipt is bound after the unique saga settlement | `noop` |
| `conflict-containment-pending` | divergent state frozen while owned actors/locks/artifacts may remain | `contain-git-publication-conflict` |
| `manual-conflict` | owned resources are closed and immutable conflict/containment receipts retain foreign evidence | `diagnose-only` |

The nested `git_ref_lock_attempts` recovery is also closed:

| Lock-attempt phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `armed` | saga CAS-installed one current attempt plus exact RouteSpawn spec/child-attempt identities and GO nonce before any child; no Git command may run | `reconcile-git-ref-lock-helper-route-spawn` |
| `child-registered` | exact blocked child boot/process/executable identity, guardian ownership, consumed GO nonce and durable GO-result hash persist; delivery may be pending or lost-ack | `resume-git-ref-lock-attempt` |
| `prepared-observed` | exact helper/guard/lock observation was persisted; ref transaction may still be alive, killed or committed | `resume-git-ref-lock-attempt` |
| `settled` | exact update/abort/orphan-reap receipt is bound to the saga outcome | `noop` |
| `conflict-containment-pending` | helper/ref-lock ambiguity is frozen; publication owner still contains owned actors/descriptors | `contain-git-ref-lock-conflict` |
| `manual-conflict` | exact helper is reaped, owned descriptors/locks closed and foreign evidence untouched | `diagnose-only` |

The parent/lower phase relation is a closed DB matrix:
`publication-reserved -> reserved|locks-held|staged`,
`publication-staged -> staged`, `ref-updated -> ref-observed|worktree-publishing`,
`worktree-published -> worktree-published`, `index-published -> index-published`,
`publication-verified -> verified-held`, `kernel-bound -> kernel-bound`, and
`settlement-committed -> settlement-committed`, `settled -> settled`;
conflict/cancellation relations have their exact matching
terminal/containment rows. Every other pair is integrity conflict before action
selection.

Publication/lock-owner/index-witness/writer-fence relations are a second closed
generated matrix:

| Publication phase | Current owner phase/kind | Witness phase | Writer fence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` before owner registration | `reserved`, pre-publish-three-lock | null | `reserved | armed` |
| `reserved` acquisition/lost-ack | `actor-registered | locks-held`, pre-publish-three-lock | null | `armed` |
| `locks-held` | `locks-held`, pre-publish-three-lock | null | `armed` |
| `locks-held` recovery transient | `reserved | actor-registered`, pre-publish-three-lock | null | `armed` |
| `staged | ref-observed | worktree-publishing` | `locks-held`, pre-publish-three-lock | `reserved` | `armed` |
| `staged | ref-observed | worktree-publishing` recovery transient | `reserved | actor-registered`, pre-publish-three-lock | `reserved` | `armed` |
| `worktree-published` normal | `locks-held`, pre-publish-three-lock | `reserved | prepared` | `armed` |
| `worktree-published` pre-rename recovery transient | `reserved | actor-registered`, pre-publish-three-lock | `reserved | prepared` with exact pre-effect tuple | `armed` |
| `worktree-published` rename-applied/DB-old recovery only | `reserved | actor-registered`, post-publish-two-lock, or predecessor `locks-held` before classification | `prepared` with exact external post-effect tuple | `armed` |
| `index-published | verified-held` | `index-lock-consumed`, either acquisition kind, active root exactly integration+guardian | `published-held` | `armed` |
| `index-published | verified-held` recovery transient | `reserved | actor-registered`, post-publish-two-lock | `published-held` | `armed` |
| `kernel-bound` original-owner cleanup prefix | `release-pending | released`, pre-publish-three-lock or post-publish-two-lock with active root exactly integration+guardian | `release-pending | released` | `armed` |
| `kernel-bound` cleanup recovery | `reserved | actor-registered | cleanup-active | release-pending | released`, post-bind-cleanup-zero-lock | `release-pending | released` | `armed` |
| `settlement-committed` | `released`, pre-publish-three-lock, post-publish-two-lock or post-bind-cleanup-zero-lock | `released` | `release-pending | broker-retirement-pending` |
| `settled` | `released`, pre-publish-three-lock, post-publish-two-lock or post-bind-cleanup-zero-lock | `released` | `released` with exact release receipt and broker-retirement closure composites |

The `reserved`/`actor-registered` recovery rows are legal only after the exact
predecessor generation is terminalized with whole-job reap, descriptor-close
and complete partial-resource classification. They keep the publication phase
and revision unchanged and prohibit every parent publication effect. A
three-lock successor returns to that phase's normal `locks-held` tuple only in
the transaction that settles all three acquisition results; a two-lock
successor binds the existing consumed-index receipt/witness and enters
`index-lock-consumed` in its two-result transaction. Every acquired partial
prefix is adopted or released by explicit per-lock results before either
transition. After kernel bind, only the zero-lock branch may replace a dead
cleanup actor: it proves all predecessor lock absence/release and resumes the
exact cleanup prefix without reacquiring any Git lock. Cleanup prefix
combinations are ordered by immutable result roots, not arbitrary cross-
products. The rename-applied/DB-old row is the sole pre-DB external-state
exception and can only execute the three-way classifier above. Every other
tuple, incomplete owner-history root, ID/hash/consumed-receipt mismatch or
current-owner fork is integrity conflict before recovery action selection.
These rows, schema predicates and fault corpus are generated from one inventory.

Hook-program/trigger relations are independently closed. Before commit-object,
the program is `pre-object-pending | pre-object-settled`; from commit-object
through `worktree-published` it must be `pre-object-settled` with trigger and
post-commit receipt canonical null. The index-publish bind atomically installs
the unique trigger and moves it to `post-commit-pending`. `index-published`
admits only that pending program or its exact `settled` result;
`publication-verified | kernel-bound | settlement-committed | settled` require program `settled` and
equal post-commit receipt hashes on program/saga/publication. The no-ref-effect
branch requires program `cancelled-before-ref-effect` and no trigger row. A
program/trigger phase outside this matrix, a second trigger, or a parent/child
receipt mismatch enters integrity conflict before hook or publication recovery.

Each action first CAS-validates the frozen `git_ref_heads` revision/generation,
sealed reflog anchor and exact object/ref state and idempotently advances or
