records `conflict-containment-pending` when an owned resource may exist, or
terminal conflict only after its containment receipt; it cannot be selected by outbox state. Any
out-of-band reflog entry, anchor drift or A→X→A after `prepared` is detected
before another external Git write. The hashed control-bundle Git helper uses a
single Git reference transaction (`update-ref --stdin` start/prepare/commit or
an equivalently qualified reference-lock API): it acquires the real ref lock and
verifies the expected OID before the final continuity read, retains that lock
while reading the entire reflog segment from the sealed anchor, and only then
commits. Candidate/human normal Git cannot acquire that ref concurrently;
candidate direct ref writes are OS-denied, while a malicious trusted principal
is outside the local threat boundary.

`update-ref prepare` is not assumed to clean up after `SIGKILL`. Before spawning
Git, one kernel transaction installs a unique `armed` lock attempt on the saga,
including one exact RouteSpawn spec/current child-attempt identity, protected
supervisor/job handle and hashed single-use GO nonce.
`reconcile-git-ref-lock-helper-route-spawn` may only drive that RouteSpawn's
protected-trampoline registration machine; it never performs an unregistered
direct spawn. The publication's protected guardian owner already holds the
qualified advisory lock and passes only that exact descriptor to the reviewed
child; the child never contends for a second copy. It reports its boot/process-
start/executable/descriptor identity and remains unable to issue
any Git command while blocked on the attempt-scoped GO capability. One kernel
transaction verifies that identity, CASes the attempt to `child-registered` and
consumes the GO nonce while durably storing the exact GO capability result;
only that returned capability, audience-bound to the attempt, child generation,
process identity and fence, releases the child.
If the coordinator dies before registration, the RouteSpawn late-registration
barrier either recovers the same exact trampoline or proves broker terminal,
whole-job empty, namespace closed and registration `closed-no-child` before any
replacement generation. The blocked child can have made no Git change; if the
GO response is lost, the child/job identity plus consumed nonce deterministically
resends or observes the same capability and never authorizes another child.
After an exact child exit/reap, a replacement requires one kernel CAS that
records the RouteSpawn audit/reap and predecessor late-registration barrier,
returns the attempt to `armed`, increments `current_child_generation` and
allocates a new RouteSpawn spec/child attempt/GO nonce before reconciliation.
The prior child capability is then
wrong-generation and cannot release the replacement; audit events retain every
old identity.

The publication preallocates one `git_publication_lock_owner` and its RouteSpawn
before any lock call. That protected owner acquires integration, guardian and
real-index publish locks before staging; acquire-before-ack is observed through
the same actor/descriptor rather than another process. Integration and guardian
remain held through cleanup. The real-index publish lock exists only until its
qualified rename consumes `index.lock`; thereafter the owner binds the exact
published-index witness and may not claim or reacquire that consumed lock.
The guardian descriptor is deliberately inherited by the exact
reviewed Git child (and no candidate descriptor), so parent death cannot release
it while a child may still own a ref lock; it closes only after that process
identity exits or is reaped. All reviewed helpers must hold that guardian lock, and no candidate,
human Git process or repository principal may open its path or the governed ref
lock path. Qualification pins the ref-storage backend and the complete lock-path
set and injects parent-death/child-live and reboot recovery: a contender cannot
acquire while the exact Git child lives, then can acquire after that child is
reaped. The qualification also proves a stable OS/capability write guard that
excludes every in-scope native ref/reflog/worktree/index writer—including
ordinary `git add` and hook/helper descendants—from every protected path from
initial acquire through the final five-part revalidation and settlement-commit
CAS. Its backend must expose a durable per-capability slot with exact
idempotent prepare/activate/terminalize and linearizable same-key query across
process/host restart; keep prepared/active authorities audience-sealed and
nondeliverable until the SQLite delivery intent; require the committed terminal
action key for every effect; persist its own same-key terminalizing intent and
exact physical-effect result prefix before/following each OS boundary; linearly
order the final effect high-water versus zero-effect tombstone; preserve per-slot revision plus global continuity epoch/
observation sequence; authenticate every direct/query result under a
qualification-pinned verification identity; and permanently reject delayed prepare/activate/effect
after tombstone. Qualification fault-injects every intent/effect/result/bind,
GO/mailbox delivery and backend reboot boundary. A backend unable to return the
same semantic result/prefix or a unique conflict for the same operation key cannot
support trusted mutation. The
broker-owned fence survives publication-owner/process death and remains armed
after advisory locks/witness cleanup; integration/guardian locks alone are not
this proof. A backend/platform without reliable descriptor inheritance,
guardian primitive, same-device hardlink plus rename/fsync/file-identity
semantics, complete ref/reflog/worktree/index path and principal mapping, that
writer-exclusion guard or the durable allowance-slot/query/delivery contract is
read-only for trusted Git. The structured fence
policy denies that complete writer universe except for the exact current
publication's target-scoped RouteFS/RouteGit capabilities; it never relies on a
hidden privileged helper exemption.

On recovery, `resume-git-ref-lock-attempt` first recovers the same publication
lock owner/descriptor. Only after its exact actor/job is fenced and reaped, every
descriptor is proven closed and the publication state is reverified may the
lock-owner aggregate allocate a successor generation; the helper itself never
reacquires the guardian. This proves no conforming old helper still owns the transaction, and
revalidates the attempt/saga fences, boot/process identity, old-or-expected ref,
full reflog segment and qualified lock-path set. If no ref lock exists it starts
the exact transaction. If the observed lock set exactly equals the qualified
expected-orphan set and every member has the exact path, file identity and
content for this attempt while ref/reflog remain at the frozen old state, it is
orphaned: the helper hashes/quarantines the set, unlinks it, fsyncs every lock
parent, records one immutable reap receipt, then retries the same attempt.
If the ref and reflog already equal the exact expected outcome, the same exact
orphan proof may reap a leftover lock before lost-ack settlement. Any extra
lock, live guardian owner, content/path/backend mismatch, unexpected ref/reflog
or inability to prove exclusive ownership enters conflict containment without
unlinking foreign evidence; terminal `manual-conflict` waits for all owned
actors/descriptors/locks to close. Age, mtime, PID reuse, `git gc`, a generic lock cleanup command and
operator guess are never sufficient evidence. Thus a kill after lock creation
or `prepare: ok` cannot permanently strand `commit-object`, while a live or
foreign lock is never deleted.

The `resume-git-commit-tree` action first resumes the preallocated ordered Git
hook program over the frozen candidate index/message/tree. It cannot create a
commit object until all three pre-object program members are absent-with-empty-
receipt or vNext-dispatch `settled` with exact member-attempt/RouteSpawn receipts
and input nonmutation. `commit-tree` and `update-ref` do not implicitly execute
hooks, so absence of the explicit program receipt is not evidence that hooks ran.
For normal commit it then verifies/imports only
the exact sealed candidate-integration object bundle/tree named by its current
manifest entry, then creates the deterministic expected commit object only when
absent and persists `commit-object`; history rewrite follows its separately
approved exact object inputs. If that exact object already
exists while the ref is still the frozen old ref, it performs no Git write
and only persists `commit-object`. A non-exact object/ref relation records
`manual-conflict`, so a kill after `commit-tree` but before the phase CAS has one
recovery branch.

`reserve-git-integration-publication` CASes the same manifest/saga tuple used by
stale, creates the one lower saga and moves the parent to
`publication-reserved`. In that no-effect transaction its winner freezes one
source branch, the expected complete path/effect universe, every future RouteFS/
RouteGit operation/target and the corresponding deny/exact-allow fence-scope
members, normalized effect partitions, legal branch-phase tuples and allowance-
capability rows for every owner kind/generation of one policy-bounded recovery
budget. It then
preallocates the broker writer-fence spec/arm intent and first lock-owner
generation. Neither owner nor broker budget can expand after this transaction.
`acquire-git-publication-locks` must append the exact arm
receipt, re-enumerate the complete real scope under that physical guard and
reject any pre-arm drift before registering/acquiring any owner lock. Only then
do the already-frozen target/before/after identities become executable
authority; no target/hash is changed, and later actions cannot add a scope
member or broaden an allowance. For `isolated-result-commit`, intents are derived solely from the sealed
result object bundle/tree; no `merge --squash` or other reread/mutation runs in
the real integration tree. For `locked-integration-snapshot`, intents come solely
from the approved exact snapshot; paths already at their after-image still
produce `already-applied` results and use the same publication machine. Mixed or
missing source fields are conflict, not a fallback sample. A history rewrite
uses `history-rewrite-approved-object`: its consumed two-key authorization and
exact object/tree bundle replace manifest fields, but it derives the same full
scope/intents and publishes the same real worktree/index contract.

Before each guarded external write, the kernel first selects one preallocated
allowance and durably binds its exact broker or released RouteSpawn mailbox
actor through the slot's open admission head, which still has no writer
authority. The binding transaction leaves the backend saga
`actor-bound-pre-prepare`; if the actor dies there, the unique next action can
shrink-terminalize the absent slot without inventing prepare authority. If it
remains valid, the same admission head serializes the dedicated backend-slot
saga's `prepare-inactive` intent before calling the guard,
queries/replays only that exact idempotency key after lost acknowledgment,
binds the inert result locally, then commits and observes the separately keyed
activation. Activation yields an active but audience-sealed authorization;
only a later SQLite issuance transaction appends the exact mailbox delivery
intent and makes that envelope visible. The actor's earlier generic RouteSpawn
GO starts a deny-by-default mailbox loop and contains no writer capability or
backend action key. The actor therefore receives no raw
token before the durable issuance row, and a lost delivery acknowledgment can
only replay the same envelope/ordinal to the same actor.

The actor still cannot write with issuance alone. The kernel commits the exact
`terminalize` action intent—including Route operation/target/effect root and a
one-use dispatch—before the actor/backend sees an effect request. The backend
slot first persists its own `terminalizing` intent/result prefix, then linearly
orders that exact effect against revocation, freezes the final effect high-water
and tombstones the authorization. If its response is lost,
recovery queries the same slot/key and binds any exact effect row that already
occurred; it never resends under another identity. All sibling capability slots
for a RouteSpawn actor reach `backend-terminal-observed` before channel close,
exit/reap/audit and semantic consumption/revocation. The current broker's
drained mailbox/current-fence barrier also proves every actor-slot admission
head was CAS-closed, monotonically removes writer eligibility and starts the fence-level
control-broker continuity chain. The current or any exact successor broker stays
live only in `control-only-release` mode and is reaped after physical fence
release. Raw operation authority, aggregate hashes, pre-tombstone no-effect
observations or a matching generation without the exact tuple/action/delivery
chain can never call or satisfy the backend.

`reconcile-git-publication-staging` dispatches only the lower saga's phase action.
Before ref CAS, the lower saga acquires the exact integration/guardian/real-index
locks through its one durable lock owner, enumerates every touched/untouched
worktree scope member, freezes the real index owner inode/complete byte artifact,
writes and fsyncs all touched after-images into protected staging, and derives
the candidate real index from that frozen artifact while preserving unrelated
staged entries. It then recomputes scope/projection roots and before bytes and persists
`staged`/parent `publication-staged`; it has not yet changed the real ref,
worktree or index. Every recovery artifact is addressed by publication/saga ID,
never selected by scanning for a newest or apparently unique file.

For an established branch, `resume-git-ref-cas` has only three outcomes after
the exact locks are held: (1) frozen old ref plus an empty segment after the real
sealed anchor permits one exact update; (2) expected commit plus exactly one
result for every precomputed reflog intent is lost-ack recovery and performs no second
write; (3) every other ref, generation, anchor or segment is
conflict containment. Therefore A→X→A cannot enter branch one. For an unborn branch,
the frozen old/current/parent OIDs are canonical null and the helper uses exactly:

```text
git update-ref --create-reflog --stdin
start
create <full-ref> <expected-commit>
prepare
commit
```

Its precomputed first ref-log entry starts with the object-format-sized zero OID,
then expected commit, exact committer and exact message. Recovery accepts only
(1) ref/log still absent, with only exact-attempt-owned empty/orphan artifacts,
which resumes the same attempt; (2) ref equals the expected commit and the log
contains exactly that one first entry, which binds the observed storage identity
without another create; or (3) sticky conflict. Ref-without-log,
log-without-ref, extra entries, a wrong zero length or a changed symbolic HEAD
are never repaired heuristically. External create success writes only the lower
reflog/ref outcome results and candidate first real anchor
`H_D(genesisAnchor,firstEntryHash,observedStorageIdentity)`; the protected head
remains `unborn/generation=0/current_oid=null` through worktree/index/seal. Its
only `unborn -> established` CAS occurs later in kernel bind.

After ref observation the publication can only roll forward. It walks intents by
ordinal; each member accepts exact-before and records `applied`, or exact-after
and records `already-applied`. Any third state is conflict. Only after every
member and complete touched/untouched after root verify may it publish the exact
owned candidate index. Before rename, the preallocated witness action hardlinks
the owned candidate `index.lock` inode into the qualified same-device protected
recovery path and fsyncs that path. Rename/fsync lost acknowledgment is
classified only by that same-inode hardlink, absent consumed lock path, real-
index bytes and exact intent/receipt; it never overwrites later user staging.
The index-publish bind transaction records the consumed-lock receipt, advances
the owner to `index-lock-consumed`, binds the `published-held` witness and
atomically creates the unique post-commit trigger/CAS.
`reconcile-post-commit-and-seal-git-publication` then settles that exact program
and revalidates, while the integration/guardian locks and witness remain held,
the governed ref, the qualification-frozen complete reflog intent/result set,
`commit^{tree}`, symbolic HEAD, real worktree/untouched roots, real index path/
inode/bytes, absence of the consumed source lock and absence of an unexpected
foreign `index.lock`, plus exact pre-object/post-commit receipts into one
publication verification receipt. `resume-git-kernel-bind` repeats this stable
exclusion/witness/index check in the same protected critical section as the
kernel CAS. Any drift first moves publication, witness and owner to conflict
containment; recovery never renames the witness back onto the real index or
overwrites later staging.

The `publication-verified → kernel-bound` transaction atomically writes both the
Git bind and `GitBoundUntrusted`, CASes `git_ref_heads` from the frozen old
revision/state/OID/generation/anchor to the exact new established tuple—generation
one plus the first observed real anchor for unborn, or old generation plus one
for established—and
invalidates every open task/goal draft and current task/goal head bound to the
prior generation through the dependency index, eliminating a bind-before-task-
state or ref-generation window. The same transaction CASes the witness from
`published-held` to `release-pending` and its current lock owner from
`index-lock-consumed` to `release-pending`; the broker writer fence remains
`armed`. `kernel-bound` is not settled: that owner, or after its exact death the
sole post-bind zero-lock successor, must remove/fsync staging and recovery
markers, unlink/fsync only the owned witness, reap helpers, retire principals,
classify/release the remaining integration/guardian locks and seal the immutable
cleanup receipt. The zero-lock successor resumes only the frozen unfinished
prefix and never reacquires a Git lock. Still inside the broker fence, the
settlement transaction requires every admission head closed plus the current
gapless control-only continuity receipt, consumes/revokes every exact allow capability, rereads a
complete one-to-one touched and untouched worktree observation set plus the
other four external parts, and appends a fresh final-purpose `armed-observed`
fence receipt against its one-use challenge. It atomically creates the final-
revalidation and acyclic authority receipts, binds the unique
`GitSagaSettlementV1`, moves publication/saga to `settlement-committed`,
advances the exact manifest prefix and moves the writer fence to
`release-pending`. It cannot commit a fence or worktree observation made before
cleanup. The idempotent release suffix then drops that exact physical guard
using only the control-only broker. If that broker dies before the call or
after a lost acknowledgment, the sole budgeted successor starts control-only,
appends the continuity receipt proving predecessor reap/audit/handoff plus the same
guard/tombstone, and cannot reopen any writer slot. Its effect-bind appends the
release receipt and enters broker-retirement-pending. Only after exact current
broker exit/reap/audit/retirement does one closure
transaction bind the release-closure composite, move publication/saga to
`settled`, and unblock the next saga or final manifest.
A
history-rewrite bind still
creates no task proof: C1 must open a new exact-tip task completion draft and
run its terminal policy. Only that later transaction may create a provisional
attestation, and only a current `full-trusted` capability may create or promote
a current attestation and project `TaskDone`. Each transition is one kernel
transaction, so a crash leaves exactly the old or new state with no intermediate
record. DocStore keeps its own
WAL/recovery; backup/restore coordinates but does not claim cross-database
atomicity.

Git idempotency is exact: the prepared saga stores `sagaId`, mode,
history-rewrite authorization when required, expected old ref/parent/ref,
protected head revision/generation/reflog anchor and exact expected reflog entry,
approved tree OID and fixed author/committer/message/timestamp metadata. The
expected reflog bytes additionally freeze updater name/email, reflog message,
`GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, timezone/locale and qualified Git/config/format and are
byte-checked by the platform qualification corpus. Pre-object governed hooks run
only in that explicit read-only program. The index-publish bind—not a caller or
later scan—creates the unique `GitHookPostCommitTriggerV1` and advances the
program to `post-commit-pending`; lost acknowledgment returns that row. The
exact post-commit member similarly settles and binds its receipt atomically on
program/saga/publication before the composite
`reconcile-post-commit-and-seal-git-publication` action may form the combined
receipt. Missing program members, legacy/unqualified chains,
capability leakage or a frozen index/message/tree change is containment/conflict.
`git commit-tree` creates one
deterministic expected commit OID, and the branch-appropriate update-ref
transaction performs CAS/create. After a kill, retry accepts only the exact
expected branch-state/ref/parent/tree/commit/publication combination. An existing
commit object with an unmoved ref reserves or resumes the one publication; an
already moved expected ref rolls that publication forward through worktree,
index, combined verification, kernel bind and cleanup. Zero/multiple/divergent
matches enter owned-resource containment and then manual conflict. Prepared, each pre/post hook member/attempt,
post-commit-object, every publication lock/stage/worktree-member/index/seal boundary,
post-ref-update, post-guardian-arm,
post-ref-lock-create, post-`prepare: ok`, post-orphan-reap, post-kernel-bind and
post-cleanup acknowledgment are separate fault points;
“latest commit” is never an oracle.

The candidate sandbox exposes the Git common-dir and refs read-only; only the
external control bundle may mutate a governed ref during trusted execution. The
protected `git_ref_heads` row is a monotonic continuity witness, not just an OID.
Before any trusted task/goal read or new saga, the bundle verifies the exact ref
and the reflog segment from its sealed anchor with replace/graft mechanisms
disabled. A normal out-of-band Git transition creates an unadopted transition,
increments/fences the generation and invalidates dependent heads; it requires a
separate operator-approved adoption/re-proof before trusted work resumes.
Unexpected missing/truncated/rewritten established reflog, or unborn
ref/log presence inconsistent with its absence receipts, direct-ref ambiguity, an unexpected alternate
object store or a transition that moved away and back to the same OID is
`manual-conflict`. Thus ref ABA cannot resurrect an attestation merely because
the final bytes again name its commit. Qualification proves candidate
manager/orchestrator/worker/gate mutations of the common-dir are OS-denied; a
malicious trusted OS principal remains outside the local threat boundary and
causes diagnosis/rekey, not a remote-attestation claim.

Task state gains `ReadyToCommit`, `GitBoundUntrusted` and
`TaskDoneProvisional`. Gate success can reach the first; an exact Git bind
reaches the second only through the exact current commit-approval manifest/entry
and linked saga. A raw ReadyToCommit status, recomputed manifest or stale approval
cannot arm Git. C1's current task-contract/proof policy may reach only the
provisional state until the effective capability is `full-trusted`; C2 is the
first track that can make that predicate true in a scoped qualification fixture
and reach `TaskDone`; D2 supplies production grants. `--no-commit`,
dry-run, skipped review/gate, and waived approval produce explicit non-trusted,
non-terminal outcomes. A single terminal-transition policy is used by loop,
orchestrated, parallel, recovery, and compatibility CLIs; bypass flags cannot
mint trusted receipts or Done.
`TaskDoneProvisional` is likewise nonterminal for trusted dependency scheduling,
goal coverage, automatic feedback and unattended dispatch; only an explicit
human provisional-continuation policy may build on it before promotion.

Git recovery and task-terminal recovery are separate aggregates. A task in
`GitBoundUntrusted` maps to `terminal-evidence-pending` while its exact saga is
only `kernel-bound | settlement-committed`; the first resumes cleanup/settlement
and the second releases the broker writer fence. After that saga is `settled` it maps to the one task action
`evaluate-terminal-policy`, while the settled Git saga itself maps to `noop`.
That action re-observes the current contract, Git identity, approval/key state,
effective capability and proof dependencies: current C1 predicates with an
incomplete C2/default grant atomically produce `TaskDoneProvisional`, while all
current `full-trusted` predicates produce `TaskDone`;
stale/revoked predicates produce `TaskProofStale`; temporarily missing evidence
leaves `GitBoundUntrusted` with a typed `terminal-evidence-pending` reason and a
bounded retry. `TaskDoneProvisional` maps back to
`evaluate-terminal-policy`; a still-current TaskDone attestation maps to `noop`,
while `TaskProofStale` requires a new
approved re-proof/replan operation and cannot silently retry old evidence. Thus
a manager crash after kernel bind cannot strand the task or infer Done from the
finished Git saga.
After the retry budget, active polling stops but the nonterminal state remains;
only a causally relevant grant/calibration/receipt/repair event re-enqueues the
same policy action. Cockpit exposes the event dependency and repair command, so
the loop neither burns forever nor converts timeout into success.
The task contract predeclares its calibration/capability slots.
`TaskDoneProvisional` leaves the corresponding terminal-promotion fields null;
the promotion transaction fills an immutable domain-separated promotion hash,
execution-cell/environment-observation, scope-appropriate grant and ordered
calibration-set bindings while CASing to `TaskDone`. A divergent prefill is
`manual-conflict`, so a raw status promotion cannot omit the evidence that made
the effective capability full. When the first terminal transaction can create
`TaskDone` directly, it fills that identical promotion proof and binding set in
the same transaction; every `current` task attestation therefore has them.

Task and goal drafts share one completion-verification protocol. Draft creation
atomically freezes the ordered slot descriptors and approved attempt-policy set,
derives each stable `verification_semantic_scope_hash`, resolves or creates its
current obligation head, inserts or returns the global owner for every
`verificationSubjectHash`, and on first insertion atomically preallocates that
owner's sole semantic/gate-attempt IDs and attempt. Slot descriptors bind the
returned canonical owner and obligation IDs. The same transaction appends the
lineage event and installs an
exact-one draft owner for the same completion input/scope. A request with the
same input/head returns the existing open or consumed draft. The subject hash
and its global owner key exclude `completion_kind`; task and goal are usage
provenance, not semantic retry namespaces. It also excludes draft/slot/gate-
attempt/session/nonce/result identities and expected-head
revision when it is only CAS metadata. It includes only contract/constraint/trust
bytes that affect the verifier executable, inputs or semantic predicate; prose,
review and allocation-only changes cannot mint a subject. Thus a new allocation
cannot rerun the same verifier. A genuinely changed tree/commit or approved
verifier behavior creates a different subject; an identical old subject receives
an applicability binding over its complete history and a no-new-execution
receipt. The completion-lineage root still retains every prior subject/outcome.
An unresolved negative for the same stable criterion and overlapping semantic
verifier class blocks automatic completion even after a changed verifier,
contract row, task allocation or Git metadata-only identity; only an explicit
approved negative resolution/waiver over the exact old obligation root can
adjudicate it. Every contract/criterion revision declares predecessor and
superseded obligation heads; omission or a non-covering successor is invalid.
The obligation head has no independent recovery phase: only the transaction that
settles a canonical owner negative or consumes an approved exact-root resolution
may CAS its count/root/current owner and append its event. Draft creation is
read-only with respect to an existing head.

Completion-verification recovery is closed:

| Completion-verification slot phase | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `reserved` | `bind-or-return-completion-verification-owner` |
| `owner-bound` | `execute-or-observe-sole-completion-verifier-attempt` |
| `pass-settled` | `noop` |
| `negative-settled` | `noop` |
| `waiver-pending` | `reconcile-exact-completion-waiver` |
| `waived-settled` | `noop` |
| `stale` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

| Completion-verifier attempt phase | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `prepared` | `arm-qualified-completion-verifier` |
| `observer-armed` | `launch-blocked-completion-verifier` |
| `child-registered` | `deliver-exact-completion-verifier-go` |
| `go-committed` | `observe-exact-completion-verifier-result` |
| `cancelling-no-exec` | `observe-cancelled-completion-verifier-exit` |
| `result-fsynced` | `observe-completion-verifier-exit` |
| `exit-observed` | `reap-completion-verifier-whole-job` |
| `job-reaped` | `seal-completion-verifier-lifecycle-audit` |
| `audit-sealed` | `bind-completion-verifier-terminal-once` |
| `containment-pending` | `contain-and-reap-conflicted-completion-verifier` |
| `settled-pass` | `noop` |
| `settled-negative` | `noop` |
| `cancelled-no-exec` | `noop` |
| `ambiguous-terminal` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

V1 permits one semantic attempt and one launch generation. Any pre-GO launch/
observer failure first enters `cancelling-no-exec`; it reaches terminal
`cancelled-no-exec` only after canonical result absence, exact exit, whole-job
reap, principal/namespace retirement, audit seal and no-late-effect proof. It is
visible negative availability evidence and cannot be replaced inside the same
completion input. After GO, recovery observes the same job/result, then the same
exit/reap/audit suffix, or records sticky ambiguity and never starts another
verifier. A raw or fsynced PASS is nonauthorizing while the job or any descendant
remains live. Nonzero/disallowed exit, survivor, late effect or audit gap yields
the policy's negative outcome or `containment-pending`; it can never settle PASS.
`manual-conflict` is reachable only after the exact actor capability is fenced
and the known job/namespace is reaped; otherwise containment remains the sole
action. FAIL, post-GO error and ambiguous/lost output remain in
the global owner history and reject a later PASS insert. If the approved contract
predeclares a human waiver, that independently signed waiver must bind the exact
draft/input/slot/owner, complete negative attempt-history root, terminal outcome
and current contract/key/nonce. It creates an explicit waived-negative proof; it
does not relabel the verifier PASS or erase risk.

`isCompletionVerificationSlotSatisfied(slotId)` is the only slot predicate. It
recomputes exact ordered membership, global owner/subject, pre-result policy,
complete attempt/event history, terminal envelope, applicability, stable
semantic scope and the current obligation-head count/root. It accepts only a
terminal PASS whose result, allowed exit, whole-job reap, audit seal and no-late-
effect roots all recompute, with no unresolved negative/ambiguity, or the exact predeclared
waiver/resolution over the full negative root, and rejects a missing predecessor
inheritance edge or unresolved prior negative in the same stable criterion and
overlapping verifier semantic class. Every task/goal terminal transaction and
`canCountAsTrustedProof` uses it. Before attestation, one acyclic completion-
verification freeze computes
`verificationProofRoot = SHA-256("VA-COMPLETION-VERIFICATION-ROOT-V1\0" ||
completionKind || completionInputHash || canonical ordered complete slot
histories)`. The freeze never contains the later attestation ID.

Every terminal attempt first opens an immutable `task_completion_drafts` row.
`taskCompletionInputHash` is the domain-separated canonical hash of the exact
project/checkout/run/task, goal/task-contract revisions and criterion/support
edge, lineage mode/root/predecessor, expected lineage-head revision, settled
Git saga plus its exact `GitSagaSettlementV1` composite ID/hash (from which
publication cleanup, branch-authority consumption, fence release and broker-
retirement closure are dereferenced), protected ref-head revision/generation/reflog anchor, complete
task settlement-member count/root, exact ancestry-oracle receipt/derived proof
or settlement-equal history-rewrite authorization, final
ref/commit/tree, ordered cycle-free verification slot-descriptor/subject root, approved attempt-policy
set, preallocated semantic/gate-attempt IDs, waiver slots and required promotion
calibration/capability slots. It excludes result-envelope hashes. One unique
owner over the exact completion input/head scope returns the existing draft
instead of accepting another ID. Draft state is closed to
`open | consumed | stale | manual-conflict`; identity, head, ref
generation or contract drift makes an open draft stale and requires a new ID.

Every task verifier receipt and waiver names that exact draft/input hash and is
produced against its exact tip. The terminal transaction re-observes the ref,
tree, protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor and the exact settled saga/
`GitSagaSettlementV1` composite FK/hash, dereferences and recomputes that row's
publication cleanup, authority branch, released writer fence, exact release-
closure/broker-retirement composite and complete task transition root,
and rechecks the contract and unique
lineage head; requires every slot to satisfy the canonical predicate, freezes the
complete verification histories, validates every current envelope/capability
dependency; consumes unused waiver nonces; and computes
`proofSetHash = SHA-256("VA-TASK-PROOF-SET-V2\0" || taskCompletionInputHash ||
verificationProofRoot || canonical ordered remaining proof envelopes)`. It then
records every owner/policy/attempt/applicability/waiver dependency edge, CASes
the prior `task_completion_heads` revision to install exactly one new head,
marks the previous attestation `superseded` where present, creates the new
attestation and atomically moves the task to its policy-selected terminal or
provisional state while consuming the draft. A fresh root uses the same unique
insert/CAS path. Any mismatch or concurrent successor commits none of these
effects. Approval or history-rewrite authorization is permission to attempt
this transaction, never completion evidence.
Task-attestation status is closed to
`provisional | current | superseded | stale | revoked | manual-conflict`; a head
may select only provisional/current, and superseded is immutable audit history.
Task-draft recovery is `open -> evaluate-task-completion`, `consumed -> noop`,
and `stale | manual-conflict -> diagnose-only`. The task-level
`GitBoundUntrusted -> evaluate-terminal-policy` action is eligible only after
the origin task saga is `settled` with its released fence and exact broker-
retirement closure. It rereads the
current protected tip: origin still current creates `direct-current-task`, while
a later fully settled normal manifest suffix creates
`direct-descendant-current-task` with the exact origin-to-current member root
and positive ancestry receipt. A merely kernel-bound/settlement-committed final
saga waits; a rewrite, gap or unowned transition fails closed. Thus a successor
entry winning before this first draft cannot permanently strand the task. The
action then creates or returns the exact draft; once present it delegates verifier progress to the draft action
rather than rerunning a gate itself.

One canonical `canCountTaskCompletion(taskId, observedRef)` policy is the only
trusted current-task read. Dependency scheduling, cycle close, cockpit, MCP,
observe, feedback settlement, approval and every TaskDone projection call it;
architecture lint rejects raw task-status comparisons or selection from the
attestation table. It reads only the unique lineage-head pointer, re-observes the
exact ref/commit/tree and protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor recorded by that
head's attestation plus its exact `GitSagaSettlementV1` ID/hash and dereferenced
cleanup/authority/fence-release/broker-retirement payload plus its mode-
appropriate complete transition root,
and returns true only when that selected attestation is
`current`, its `promotionProofHash`, execution-cell/environment/grant and
calibration bindings are all non-null and exact, the task projection is
`TaskDone` naming that attestation, its verification freeze/root/lineage/slot/
policy fields recompute exactly and every frozen slot still satisfies
`isCompletionVerificationSlotSatisfied`, and the freshly recomputed
effective capability is `full-trusted` on the active SQLite backend. That
minimum includes the current backend/rollback ceiling, irreversible
finalization, sandbox/control-bundle generation, exact execution-cell
qualification/environment/default grant, every required calibration, task
contract, approval/key and receipt dependency, plus the final external bound
receipt for every bootstrap-backed factor. A provisional head is a typed
hard false even if missing predicates have since appeared; only its promotion
transaction can make it current. Ref-head revision/generation/anchor, backend
ceiling, ref,
commit or tree
drift—including an ABA return or same-tree different-commit/parent
replacement—first CASes the head/attestation to `stale`, projects
`TaskProofStale`, and only then returns false. Zero/multiple heads or a head row
that disagrees with the attestation is an integrity conflict, never a selection
heuristic.

A legitimate later branch commit does not silently preserve an earlier current
task proof. `direct-descendant-current-task` is only the race-free first proof
for a task with no predecessor attestation/head; after a current task proof
exists, the ordinary successor path is exclusively a
`descendant-refresh`: before that earlier task can satisfy another dependency on
the new tip, a trusted supervisor Git-ancestry oracle must prove that the old
attested commit is an ancestor of the exact new tip with replacement mechanisms
disabled, and that every intervening governed ref transition has an exact
approved `GitSagaSettlementV1`. A new task completion draft binds the old
head/attestation/commit, exact ancestry-oracle receipt, derived ancestry proof,
complete ordered settlement-member root, current ref-head
revision/generation/anchor, new
ref/commit/tree and fresh exact-tip verifier slots. Only the common terminal
transaction above may create the successor with `supersedes_id`,
`lineage_mode=descendant-refresh` and `ancestor_proof_hash` while CAS-replacing
the old head; the old Done event remains audit history. Missing objects, a
shallow boundary, replace refs, grafts, an ambiguous ancestry walk, ref ABA or an
unadopted intervening ref transition fails closed and cannot mint that draft or
successor.

A non-descendant tip—including rebase, force-update or a same-tree
different-parent/commit replacement—can never use `descendant-refresh` or an
ordinary `supersedes_id`. An intentional governed rewrite requires the dedicated
two-key authorization aggregate, which binds the old/new refs, parents, commits,
trees, reason, task/contract and affected lineage. Consuming it only invalidates
the old lineage and arms an exact `history-rewrite` Git saga; the authorization
cannot replace that saga or a verifier. After the saga is settled at the new ref
generation, a new task completion draft forces all verifier
receipts/waivers and capability dependencies to bind the exact new tip. The
common terminal transaction may then install a new lineage root with
`supersedes_id=null`, the mandatory `git_saga_id`,
`history_rewrite_authorization_id` exactly equal to the final settlement's
authority ID, and `replaced_lineage_id`.

If an out-of-band non-descendant update already happened, it cannot be
retrospectively described as the planned rewrite saga. The old task stays stale;
the operator may either restore and execute the approved rewrite CAS, or approve
a genuinely new task/contract and normal Git saga rooted after the observed
tip, followed by full exact-tip proof. Tree equality never weakens these rules.
Dependency dispatch binds both observed tip and protected ref generation in its
kernel transaction and rechecks them immediately before worker GO. This makes
branch advance explicit without accepting an unrecorded rewrite or stale
semantic proof.

### 4.5 Goal and acceptance contract

Every run selects a versioned `GoalAcceptanceContract` containing objective,
constraints, risks, stable criterion IDs, required proof policy, allowed human
waivers, source human-intent revision, and policy hash. Backlog items reference
one or more criteria or a causal support edge to a parent criterion. Each task
also has a local `TaskAcceptanceContract`. Candidate code may propose contracts,
criteria, verifier/gate/artifact predicates, and support edges; only the external
control plane plus the configured human/review policy may approve them before
plan approval. Orphan work cannot become trusted work.

Goal-contract approval preallocates its `GoalGitBaselineV1` and exact current
`GitRefHeadSnapshotV1` before signing. The signed approval subject includes both
contract content and baseline composite identity/hash. The consume transaction
re-observes a `current` qualified-anchor or fully settled-saga head, consumes the
nonce, inserts/binds baseline and contract revision and records their equal
approval ID/subject atomically. A moved, rewrite-pending, kernel-bound or
settlement-committed head rejects without consuming the approval; lost
acknowledgment returns the same approved contract/baseline pair.

The goal pipeline assigns stable criterion IDs, bumps candidate-backlog/plan
schemas, and migrates all readers from free-text acceptance notes. Contract
creation/invalidation is an explicit C1 deliverable, not an implicit parser
change.

Task plan, constraint selection, dispatch, worker episode, gate receipt, review,
commit approval, Git saga, and Done transition all bind the exact contract hash.
Any relevant goal/acceptance/constraint intent change increments the contract
revision and durably invalidates affected episodes. Invalidation is checked
before GO, before/after every gate, before approval, and immediately before
commit; it fences/cancels work when possible and otherwise makes its receipts
ineligible.

`TaskDoneProvisional` requires the task's approved local contract, declared goal
criterion subset/support edge, structurally valid current evidence and exact Git
binding in a task-completion attestation. `TaskDone` is only the current
attestation projection and additionally requires the effective capability to be
`full-trusted`, including every required non-expired C2 calibration and the exact
execution-cell default grant; `missing | not-current | expired |
calibration-unsupported` are hard false. `GoalComplete`
requires every goal criterion to have current trusted proof or an authenticated
human waiver scoped to that criterion/revision. The final reviewer receives the
goal/task contracts, criterion coverage map, candidate diff, and receipts.
Diff-only review cannot certify completion.

Coverage cannot be assembled across unrelated candidate trees. C1 creates a
two-phase immutable `goal_completion_drafts` row only after observing one exact
final ref/commit/tree, the approved contract's exact `GoalGitBaselineV1`, the
final fully settled/released-fence saga's exact `GitSagaSettlementV1` composite
ID/hash, and the complete
continuous settlement slice from baseline to final tip. Cleanup and branch-
authority consumption are accepted only by dereferencing that final/member
settlement payload, never as parallel caller fields.
`completionInputHash` is the domain-separated canonical hash of
the exact registry/project/checkout, stable goal-lineage/contract, goal/intent
revision, predecessor/current-head key/generation/
revision, protected ref-head revision/generation/reflog anchor, final
ref/commit/tree, approved baseline ID/hash, final saga/settlement ID/hash and the
complete approved-settled Git transition count/root from that baseline to final
tip, contract,
criterion/verifier requirements, ordered cycle-free verification slot descriptors/subjects,
approved attempt-policy set, preallocated semantic/gate-attempt IDs and waiver
slots plus required promotion calibration/capability slot descriptors. It deliberately
excludes origin run, result signatures and envelope hashes. `origin_run_id` is
audit provenance only. One unique exact input/head owner
returns an existing draft rather than minting a new verifier sample. Draft state is closed to
`open | consumed | stale | manual-conflict`; head, ref generation, ref, commit,
tree, baseline, final settlement/member slice or contract drift makes an
open draft stale and requires a new ID.

Every final-tree verifier receipt and human waiver names that
`completionDraftId` and `completionInputHash`. C1 re-evaluates every non-waived
goal criterion against the draft's exact tree; older task proofs are historical
inputs and a TaskDone/attestation label alone is not goal-completion proof.
However, every identical task verifier attempt and every overlapping unresolved
negative already belongs to the kind-neutral owner/obligation head: the goal
slot must reuse it through an exact no-new-execution applicability binding and
cannot run another GO. A changed goal verifier subject still reads the canonical
cross-kind unresolved-negative head for that stable criterion/class. Each goal
slot executes only when no prior kind has created that subject owner. One final
kernel transaction re-observes the exact
  ref/commit/tree, approved baseline, exact final `GitSagaSettlementV1` and
complete continuous settlement-member root, dereferences its cleanup/authority
payload, rechecks saga/publication `settled`, writer fence `released` and the
exact release-closure/broker-retirement composite,
validates every slot through the canonical predicate and freezes
the complete histories, verifies approval/key
currency, protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor and expected goal-head
revision, consumes all
unused waiver nonces, and computes
`proofSetHash = SHA-256("VA-GOAL-PROOF-SET-V2\0" || completionInputHash ||
verificationProofRoot || canonical ordered remaining proof/waiver envelopes)`.
It then records all owner/policy/attempt/applicability/waiver proof
dependencies, creates one `GoalCompletionAttestation`, and CASes the draft to
`consumed`. The same transaction CASes the prior `goal_completion_heads`
revision, marks a predecessor superseded when present and installs this
attestation as the sole head; a fresh head uses the same unique insert/CAS path.
The head key is stable goal-lineage/ref, never run: concurrent runs completing
the same goal revision contend on this CAS, and a later contract revision
supersedes the same row while retaining the prior attestation history.
If effective capability is already `full-trusted`, this transaction computes
the same domain-separated promotion proof and exact
execution-cell/environment/grant/calibration/bound-receipt bindings described
below, creates the attestation `current` and projects `GoalComplete` atomically.
Otherwise it creates `provisional` with those fields null for the sole promotion
action to fill.
Any failure or concurrent draft commits none of those effects. Thus neither result
signatures nor the proof-set hash are self-referential, and a T1 envelope cannot
be used to build a T2 attestation even when the trees are identical.

The attestation binds the draft/input hash, goal/intent revision, protected ref
head revision/generation/reflog anchor, approved baseline, final settlement
ID/hash and complete continuous settlement-member root, complete
proof/waiver set, exact verification freeze/root/lineage/slot/policy-set fields,
receipt head, policy/config, constraint snapshot,
trust-control closure and authority epoch. `GoalComplete` is a derived status
that exists only while this attestation is `current`.

Completion-draft recovery is a separate aggregate but Git-settlement-dependent:
`open →
evaluate-goal-completion`, `consumed → noop`, and `stale | manual-conflict →
diagnose-only`. The first action reruns all final observations and either commits
the all-or-nothing transaction above or leaves the draft open with a typed
pending/error reason and bounded retry; it cannot weaken a slot. A crash before
that transaction therefore re-enters evaluation, while a crash after commit
observes `consumed` plus the exact attestation and does nothing.
This evaluation retry only observes/drives the existing slot/attempt phases; it
never allocates another semantic verifier attempt after GO or a terminal result.

The produced attestation is a separate aggregate with status closed to
`provisional | current | superseded | stale | revoked | manual-conflict`. Its recovery map is
`provisional → evaluate-goal-promotion`, `current | superseded → noop`, and
`stale | revoked | manual-conflict → diagnose-only`. Promotion re-observes the
exact unique goal head, protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor,
ref/commit/tree, approved baseline, exact final settlement and continuous member
root, settled saga/publication, released writer fence, exact release closure/
broker retirement and every contract, approval, proof, calibration,
execution-cell and scope-appropriate capability dependency; one transaction
computes a domain-separated `promotionProofHash` over the completion input plus
the exact environment-observation, scope-appropriate grant and ordered current
calibration envelope hashes, fills those previously-null attestation bindings,
then CASes the still-selected head's `provisional → current` and records the
GoalComplete projection.
Those bindings are immutable after promotion; a prefilled/divergent field is
`manual-conflict`.
Missing predicates leave a typed provisional/pending reason with bounded retry;
drift records stale before returning false. A crash before promotion therefore
reruns the same policy, while a crash after commit sees `current` and cannot
mint a second attestation.
Exhausting the retry budget stops polling; only a matching dependency event
re-enqueues promotion, and the provisional result remains visibly noncurrent.

A protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor, ref/commit/tree,
baseline/final-settlement/member-root drift,
contract or intent revision, policy/config/trust-closure
change, receipt revocation, waiver revocation, or verifier invalidation
transactionally changes the attestation to `stale|revoked` when observed and
projects `GoalCompletionStale`; release/publish/read paths re-observe the ref and
commit/tree and fail closed before trusting completion. Affected task current status becomes
`TaskProofStale` where its own proof was invalidated, while the historical Done
event remains audit evidence. Tests cover T1 proof followed by a T2 regression,
post-completion ref drift, same-tree commit/parent replacement, receipt
revocation, and contract/config changes.

One `canCountGoalCompletion()` policy is the only trusted read. Cockpit, MCP,
observe, release, publish, approval and every `GoalComplete` projection call it
instead of inspecting `status`. It reads only the unique goal-head pointer;
zero/multiple heads or a head/attestation mismatch is integrity conflict. It
returns true only when the selected attestation is `current`, its immutable
`promotionProofHash`, execution-cell/environment/grant/calibration bindings are
all non-null and exact, its verification freeze/root/lineage/slot/policy fields
recompute exactly, every frozen slot still satisfies the canonical predicate,
and the GoalComplete projection names that attestation.
A provisional head is a typed hard false even if every missing dependency has
since become current; only `evaluate-goal-promotion` may CAS it to `current` and
fill those bindings. It
re-observes the protected ref-head revision/generation/anchor, exact
ref/commit/tree, approved baseline, exact final settlement and complete
continuous settlement-member root, settled saga/publication and released writer
fence, plus config
bytes, then transactionally compares current contract/intent, authority epoch,
constraint catalog/snapshot, policy, trust closure, receipt/waiver revocation
facts, approval/key revocation facts, archive anchors and per-gate calibration state through the dependency
index, including current irreversible finalization, backend qualification and
exact-cell default grant.
Any mismatch first records stale/revoked and only then returns false.
Approval/key/receipt/waiver/calibration/qualification/default-grant/environment-observation invalidation writes its fact and invalidates every
dependent proof/feedback/attestation in the same kernel transaction.
The same read requires effective capability `full-trusted` for the exact current
execution cell and active SQLite backend, including the final external bound
receipt for every bootstrap-backed factor; a reverse flip or cell/grant drift
therefore invalidates completion even when every historical receipt remains
cryptographically intact.

For an external release/publish effect, the outbox expected identity explicitly
contains exact ref, commit, tree and all other observations; its apply boundary re-observes them immediately and
its observer rejects any before-ack drift. Fault fixtures cover config write
before outbox ack, archived-receipt revocation, calibration revocation and
waiver revocation.

C1 can construct `TaskDoneProvisional` and `provisional` goal attestations only
on a finalized checkout (or disposable finalized fixture) while C2
trust-closure, exact-cell default grant and required-gate calibration
capabilities are not current. C2 is the first track allowed to promote those to
`TaskDone`/a `current` attestation and therefore the first that can project
trusted task or goal completion in an isolated qualification fixture. Its test
grant is externally signed, checkout-scoped and marked non-production; only D2
may issue a production per-cell default grant after the required soak. C1/C2
merge tests prove rejection of uncalibrated or non-production evidence rather
than opening an early trust window.

Repository bridge:

| Surface | A2 action | C1 action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `human-board.mjs`, goal/intent CLI | preserve IDs/revisions in JSON authority | externally approve goal/task contract proposals |
| `goal-backlog.mjs`, candidate backlog/plan | add versioned criterion/support-edge projection fields | create/bind contract hashes and reject orphan work |
| orchestration checkpoint/review | carry opaque contract revision/hash | invalidate plan/episode on contract drift; review coverage map |
| `schemas/evidence-bundle.schema.json`, `schemas/protocol-fixture.schema.json`, candidate-backlog schema/fixtures | dual-read optional `goalContractHash`, task-contract and criterion IDs | require vNext contract/criterion proof fields |
| templates, MCP, test flows and E2E scenarios | expose degraded/legacy projection safely | expose TaskDoneProvisional vs TaskDone vs GoalComplete and proof/waiver/capability status |

## 5. Constraint governance

Constraint versions contain origin/authority, lifecycle, immutable semantic ID,
supersession lineage, scope, subject, predicate, polarity, tags,
`conflictsWith`, base confidence, half-life policy, learned sequence/time,
policy version, and actor/reason for every transition.

Selection is deterministic:

1. match scope/exact tokens;
2. compute decay at a snapshot-fixed `asOf` (curated/human constraints do not
   decay by default; clock anomalies fail closed);
3. build explicit/structural conflict clusters;
4. resolve by authority, specificity, evidence threshold, then DB sequence;
5. suppress unresolved ties and emit evidence risk rather than inject both;
6. enforce domain/dispatch caps;
7. return selected/suppressed/decayed/conflicted/retired items and reason codes.

The pure B1 boundary freezes three closed values:
`ConstraintSelectionInputV1(project_id, catalog_revision, catalog_root_hash,
selector_policy_hash, candidate_version_count,
candidate_version_set_root_hash, normalized_scope_tokens_hash,
normalized_subject_hash, domain_cap_policy_hash, as_of_sequence,
as_of_unix_ms, trusted_clock_observation_hash)`,
`ConstraintSelectionMemberV1(input_hash, constraint_semantic_id,
constraint_version, disposition, reason_code, conflict_cluster_hash,
effective_confidence_micros, canonical_rank)`, and
`ConstraintSelectionSnapshotV1(input_hash, catalog_revision,
selector_policy_hash, as_of_sequence, as_of_unix_ms, member_count,
member_root_hash, selected_count, selected_root_hash, suppressed_count,
suppressed_root_hash, decayed_count, decayed_root_hash, conflicted_count,
conflicted_root_hash, retired_count, retired_root_hash,
reason_code_set_root_hash, snapshot_hash)`. `disposition` is closed to
`selected | suppressed | decayed | conflicted | retired`; the clock observation
references the existing monotonic `trusted_time_heads` authority rather than a
second time subsystem. Exactly one disposition is assigned in precedence order
`retired -> decayed -> conflicted -> suppressed -> selected` after each earlier
predicate has removed the member from later consideration.

Before ranking, the selector rejects duplicate version IDs, multiple current
versions for one semantic ID, divergent semantic/version aliases, negative or
non-integer caps, unsupported decay kinds, non-positive half-life, non-finite
confidence and learned time later than trusted `asOf`. Confidence/decay use the
policy's integer fixed-point scale, never implementation-dependent floating
point comparison. Candidate/conflict/reason-code/output sets are canonical-
sorted before hashing, so iteration order cannot change conflict resolution,
capacity membership, injection order or bytes. Caps apply only after head
validation, decay, conflict resolution and suppression; duplicates/conflicts do
not consume capacity.

The selector returns immutable version IDs through those members plus catalog
revision, policy hash, fixed `asOf` and snapshot hash. Dispatch commits that
exact snapshot and lease in one transaction while CASing the catalog revision
before worker GO. A concurrent human constraint invalidates the stale dispatch.

Feedback authority is append-only `constraint_feedback`, not mutable counters.
Plan approval creates an immutable `evaluationOpportunityId` bound to contract,
criterion, logical task, candidate lineage, causal root and preregistered
outcomes grouped by stable `exclusivityGroupId`. Retry, recovery, duplicate worker,
reopen, or an unchanged candidate inherits that ID. A new sample requires a new
approved opportunity with a materially distinct candidate/criterion lineage.
The first dispatch CAS-binds one immutable selection snapshot to the opportunity;
retry cannot rebind it. A relevant catalog change invalidates that opportunity,
and any newly approved replacement remains in the same cohort unless an
independence record proves otherwise.

Sampling independence is external-policy data, not candidate assertion. An
externally approved `independenceClassId` is stable across routine contract
revisions. The control plane assigns one stable `evaluationClusterId` to the
same candidate tree/logical change/causal root by default, even when criteria are
split, renamed or separately tasked.
`cohortKey = projectId + evaluationClusterId + independenceClassId`;
automatic statistics grant at most one current sample weight per
cohort/exclusivity group. Exact candidate tree duplicates always reuse the
cluster; criterion-specific opportunities inside it cannot add weight. A new
causal root requires an externally approved structured independence record
binding old/new tree hashes, logical change sets, criterion and rationale;
missing/near-duplicate/shared-root evidence is conservatively clustered rather
than counted. Candidate code may propose, never approve, opportunity/root IDs.
Cross-revision and trivial-variant adversarial fixtures must retain the same
cohort unless an approved independence record proves a new causal class.
Splitting one change across two criterion lineages also retains the same cluster
unless an explicit criterion-outcome independence record proves separability;
criterion-splitting is a mandatory adversarial fixture.
The unique current-settlement key is `(evaluationOpportunityId,
constraintVersion, exclusivityGroupId)`; the bound selection snapshot and
selected outcome are values, not parts that can mint another key. Settlement
CASes `pending` to exactly one
outcome. A later reopen/revert correction revokes and replaces the old fact in
one transaction without adding sample weight. Concurrent contradictory outcomes
enter `manual-conflict` and contribute zero until an externally approved
resolution. The same transaction CASes the unique cohort settlement slot;
multiple opportunities in one cohort merge evidence into that slot rather than
minting weight, and opposite outcomes put the cohort slot in conflict. Receipts
attach as an evidence set to that fact; multiple
gates/episodes cannot inflate sample count. Receipt lifecycle is `pending |
settled | revoked`; promotion records exact feedback fact IDs and statistical
inputs. Replay is idempotent and rebuilds derived counters/lifecycle. Tests cover
success→reopen→failure, concurrent opposite settlement, revocation and replay.
Retries, infra failures, calibration runs, and repeated gates do not become
independent success samples.

A catalog change relevant to an in-flight episode writes a durable invalidation
outbox operation. It fences/cancels the episode where possible and blocks later
receipt settlement, approval, and commit when cancellation is late. Reopen,
revert, retry, and multiple-receipt cases are part of the idempotency suite.

B2a manual lifecycle/feedback depends on canonical receipts. B2b automatic
promotion/demotion remains feature-disabled until mutation-calibrated evidence
exists. Hard-constraint promotion remains human-reviewable. Receipt revocation,
archive, or restored history deterministically recomputes affected decisions.

B2b uses a closed automatic-lifecycle decision aggregate; it never mutates a
constraint row in place. Immutable
`constraint_automatic_lifecycle_decisions(id, project_id,
constraint_semantic_id, source_constraint_version, action_kind,
decision_input_root_hash, decision_equivalence_hash, lifecycle_policy_hash,
selection_snapshot_count, selection_snapshot_root_hash,
feedback_fact_count, feedback_fact_root_hash, cohort_settlement_count,
cohort_settlement_root_hash, receipt_chain_head_hash,
calibration_set_root_hash, revocation_head_hash, archive_head_hash,
expected_catalog_revision, proposed_target_version,
proposed_target_content_hash, approval_requirement_kind,
approval_object_hash, human_approval_id, execution_cell_hash,
capability_requirement_hash, phase, evaluation_result_hash,
application_input_root_hash, capability_skip_receipt_id,
capability_skip_receipt_hash, result_version, result_content_hash,
result_catalog_revision, decision_receipt_hash, conflict_fact_id,
revision, created_sequence, settled_sequence, invalidated_by)` is globally
unique on `(project_id,constraint_semantic_id,source_constraint_version,
action_kind,decision_equivalence_hash)`. `decision_input_root_hash` is recomputed
from lifecycle policy, every listed count/root, receipt/calibration/revocation/
archive heads and expected catalog revision. `decision_equivalence_hash` binds
project, semantic/source identity, action, that input root, proposed target,
approval requirement/object, execution cell and capability requirement.
`action_kind` is closed to `promote | demote | retire | human-override`;
automatic policy may produce the first three only. `approval_requirement_kind`
is `none | hard-promotion | human-override`; the latter two require the exact
current purpose/audience/object/signing-operation approval before preparation
and bind. `human-override` is never silently automatic.

Phase checks forbid placeholder success. `prepared` forbids evaluation,
application, skip, result and conflict fields; `evaluated` requires only the
immutable evaluation result; `approval-pending` additionally requires a non-
`none` approval requirement/object; `apply-prepared` requires
`application_input_root_hash = decision_input_root_hash` after re-observation;
`bound` requires `result_version = proposed_target_version`,
`result_content_hash = proposed_target_content_hash`, and
`result_catalog_revision` to be the unique CAS successor of
`expected_catalog_revision`, plus the exact decision receipt;
`capability-skipped` requires the signed skip receipt bound to policy,
requirement, execution cell and platform and forbids all result/decision-receipt
fields; `invalidated` requires `invalidated_by`; `manual-conflict` requires
`conflict_fact_id`.

| Constraint automatic-lifecycle phase | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `prepared` | `evaluate-constraint-lifecycle-decision` |
| `evaluated` | `classify-constraint-lifecycle-application` |
| `approval-pending` | `reconcile-constraint-lifecycle-approval` |
| `apply-prepared` | `bind-constraint-lifecycle-version` |
| `bound` | `noop` |
| `capability-skipped` | `noop` |
| `invalidated` | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

Evaluation, classification and binding each re-observe normalized input members,
catalog/source head, revocation/archive heads, execution-cell capability and any
required approval. Drift invalidates the old decision before a changed input can
create a new equivalence owner. Binding atomically appends exactly one immutable
constraint version, supersession edge, decision receipt and catalog revision;
its CAS revalidates approval and input roots, so lost acknowledgment or a
competing binder returns the same result.

An unsupported execution cell can close only as `capability-skipped` with its
signed capability receipt; it does not count as a lifecycle decision or success
sample. Restore/replay recomputes the same equivalence/input roots. Exact input
returns the existing aggregate/version; changed input creates a new lineage,
while the same equivalence key with divergent target/result bytes is integrity
conflict—never a rewritten result for one owner.

## 6. Evidence and gate calibration

### 6.1 Canonical receipts

Gate configuration v2 is structured:
`{stableGateId, executable, args, cwd, envAllowlist, required, profiles}` and is
executed with spawn/execFile. Legacy shell strings remain compatible but are
`configured/legacy-shell` and cannot count as calibrated proof.

Receipt outcomes are closed:
`passed | failed | skipped | not-run | infra-error | timed-out | signaled`.
Only `passed` for every policy-required gate can count as proof.

Each receipt binds:

- canonical candidate/Merkle snapshot and approval manifest;
- gate/profile/config/validator/supervisor and trust-control-closure hashes;
- resolved executable identity, argv, cwd and environment hash (Node, OS/arch,
  lockfile, relevant tool/dependency versions);
- authority epoch, task/track/dispatch/gate-attempt IDs and task revision;
- constraint snapshot/catalog/policy hashes;
- start/end, exit/signal/timeout/truncation;
- redacted output and artifact hashes;
- chain scope, sequence and previous hash.

Receipt head allocation is linearized in StateKernel by sequence/CAS; a fork is
an integrity failure. Approval binds the exact chain range/head. Archive uses an
immutable catalog, segment root, preceding/following anchors and verifiable
tombstones. A receipt referenced by feedback/transition is never simply deleted.

One canonical `canCountAsTrustedProof()` policy is the only route used by
approval, commit, cockpit, progress and CLI. Architecture lint forbids direct
status comparisons. `gates audit --strict` returns nonzero/`ok:false` for any
required gate below policy. `configured` is never equivalent to proof.
The policy resolves the dependency index and rejects any revoked approval/key,
receipt, waiver, calibration, backend qualification, default grant or trust
closure, or an invalid/expired environment observation before returning true. It also
requires effective capability `full-trusted`; missing, expired, not-current,
wrong-execution-cell or `calibration-unsupported` qualification/default/calibration
facts are hard false, not absence of a revocation.
For task/goal proof it additionally requires the exact completion-verification
freeze, complete owner/attempt/outcome histories and every canonical slot
predicate; receipt-chain presence cannot make a caller-selected PASS sufficient.

C1 carries a checked callsite inventory covering loop terminal transitions,
parallel runner, orchestrate await-workers automatic-policy/approve-commit/commit,
approval-policy,
observe/cockpit, progress iteration, gates audit, recovery, MCP/read resources,
and bypass flags. Its denylist gate fails while any surface compares raw trust
status or reaches Done outside the terminal policy.

Cockpit is a derived trust view, not another success oracle. C1 freezes
`schemas/vnext/cockpit-output.schema.json` around exactly three top-level
questions: goal (contract revision and criterion coverage), risk (open conflicts,
dead letters, stale dependencies and capability downgrades), and evidence
(current trusted-proof verdict plus reason codes). One response is built from a
single kernel snapshot sequence and then re-observes external ref/commit/tree
identities before return. Each summary fact carries its source record ID,
content hash, observation sequence/time and a content-addressed raw-artifact
drill-down; collapsed prose alone can never authorize approval. Missing,
divergent, truncated or stale input renders the affected question
`unknown|blocked`, never green. The JSON and human views use the same canonical
`canCountAsTrustedProof()`/`canCountGoalCompletion()` results and repair command
IDs, so operators do not need forensic file parsing to distinguish an evidence
risk from a product failure.

The inventory explicitly names `sprint-board.mjs` and sprint-board core,
`validate-distribution.mjs` duplicate state enums, `va-parallel-runner.mjs`,
`auto-pilot-loop.mjs` `transitionToDone/finalizeDoneTaskCommit`, and
`auto-pilot-orchestrate.mjs` finalize/approval paths. A0 generates
`state-lint/terminal-callsites.json`; after A2, `sprint-board update --state Done`
is rejected unless invoked through the terminal policy with a Git saga binding.

### 6.2 Dual-plane calibration

Calibration has two planes:

- the candidate snapshot being tested is exactly the commit-approval candidate;
- the supervisor/profile validator comes from a content-addressed previously
  approved installation outside the candidate tree.

A0 freezes `schemas/vnext/trust-control-closure.schema.json`. The previously
trusted supervisor resolves each gate from its top-level executable through
package-manager script expansion, shebang/interpreter, child-process argv,
static and observed dynamic imports, test configuration/harness, criterion
verifier, reason encoder, terminal/coverage policy, lockfile resolution,
filesystem-read golden/fixture/snapshot/schema/policy data, relevant environment
inputs and non-SUT dependency bytes. Sandbox tracing must account for every
control-file open as well as imports/children. The manifest contains content hashes and an externally
approved boundary between candidate system-under-test files and control files.
Changing any control byte/resolution path enters bootstrap even when
`{executable,args}` is unchanged. Unclassified dynamic delegation, an observed
child/import absent from the closure, or a candidate-provided reason encoder is
`noncalibratable/manual`, not trusted proof.

The closure also freezes semantic edge direction. Control may choose fixtures
and send inputs to the SUT; SUT-to-control data is limited to a declared
observation schema (exit, stdout/stderr, protocol response and artifact bytes).
Expected values, selected fixture/path, oracle, verdict, reason and policy may
not originate from the SUT or be chosen from SUT output. A calibratable
criterion verifier runs in the pinned supervisor process and invokes candidate
SUT code in a separate sandboxed process; no SUT module loads into the verifier.
Legacy in-process/candidate-owned tests may be receipted but are
`noncalibratable` unless a pinned external verifier independently establishes
the criterion.

Changes to gate config, profile, supervisor, receipt validator, approval policy,
trust-control closure, criterion verifier, package script, or trust code enter
bootstrap mode and require validation by the previous trusted
supervisor plus explicit external CI/human approval. A candidate cannot certify
its own replacement trust controller.

The gate executes in a platform adapter that enforces: original repository
read-only/inaccessible, disposable root as the only writable project area,
controlled HOME/TMP/Git config, disabled external hooks, explicit network policy,
no control-root/database/socket/approval access, and no writable
symlink/hardlink escape. Workers use the same mandatory containment class, not
only calibration gates. Linux/macOS/Windows mechanisms and
limitations are qualification evidence. Without a proven adapter, calibration
is unsupported and cannot be required for unattended approval on that platform.

Each profile is declarative and curated: fixture source, allowed candidate paths,
deterministic mutation, expected stable gate ID, machine-readable rejecting
reason, time/resource limits, and cleanup proof. Model-suggested shell text is
never executed as a mutation.

Calibration is a differential experiment on the same environment:

1. clean candidate PASS;
2. exactly one mutation FAILS at the expected gate for the expected reason;
3. clean replay PASS.

This experiment is a protected saga, not three receipts selected by query.
`calibration_runs.phase` is closed to `prepared | clean-passed |
mutation-rejected | replay-passed | current | failed | manual-conflict`. The
creation transaction freezes candidate/tree, gate/profile/mutation/closure,
execution-cell and environment-observation hashes plus three preallocated step
attempt IDs before the first process starts. Its unique action map is:

| Persisted calibration phase | Unique action |
| --- | --- |
| `prepared` | `resume-calibration-clean-before` |
| `clean-passed` | `resume-calibration-known-bad` |
| `mutation-rejected` | `resume-calibration-clean-replay` |
| `replay-passed` | `finalize-calibration-current` |
| `current` | `noop` |
| `failed` or `manual-conflict` | `diagnose-only` |

Each step action first reconciles its preallocated attempt ID through the
control inbox: an exact already captured receipt advances the phase without a
second selection; a proven absent attempt runs the one frozen step; divergent
identity is `manual-conflict`. All three receipts must bind the same run,
candidate/tree, gate/profile/closure, execution cell and environment
observation, and only the known-bad step may use the frozen mutation. Wrong
outcome/reason, infra error or environment drift records `failed` and requires a
new approved run ID. One final kernel transaction revalidates the ordered three
receipts, writes their dependencies and the sole current calibration fact, and
CASes `replay-passed → current`; no partial phase can satisfy `canCount*`.
Therefore a kill after an external step but before its phase CAS resumes by
exact attempt identity and cannot combine receipts from different runs.

Always-fail gates, wrong reasons, missing dependencies, timeouts, signals, or
infra errors fail calibration. Profiles exist per required gate; project trust
is the minimum of required gate states. Non-deterministic review may be
`receipted-noncalibratable`, never promoted by another gate's profile.

Negative fixtures include candidate self-modification (`true` gates, weakened
profiles/validator), writes to original repo/parent/HOME/index, symlink/hardlink
escape, direct DB/WAL/outbox/receipt/supervisor access, approval forgery, PATH
replacement, shell expansion, missing dependency, wrong-reason,
timeout, skipped/not-run gates, receipt fork/tamper, and environment drift.
They also keep the top-level gate config constant while replacing a package
script, indirect child/import, test harness, criterion verifier or reason
encoder, and separately replace a golden/snapshot/schema/policy input; every such
change must enter bootstrap or fail closure validation.
Another fixture keeps the harness bytes unchanged while the SUT supplies an
expected value, expected-data path, verdict or reason; closure validation or the
external verifier must reject it.

The full `await-workers → internal automatic policy or approve-commit → commit`
flow must reject missing,
stale, tampered, wrong-source/config/environment, incomplete, or uncalibrated
required evidence.
