`TrustControlStateMachineInventoryV1` is generated from those schemas and the
normative phase tables. For every aggregate it records the exact phase/state
enum, one RecoveryAction per nonterminal phase, terminal disposition and fault-
manifest scenario IDs. The architecture gate checks four-way exact equality:
every prose/table phase exists in schema, every schema enum has exactly one
action, every action has declared recovery/denial faults, and no fault names an
undeclared phase. “Phases above” or a free recovery string cannot pass.

Review authority is split: the operator-admitted, out-of-repository
`BootstrapReviewRootV1` may service only the three bootstrap ceremony kinds and
is permanently sealed after A0 final bind; the installed review control plane
may service successor ceremonies only after its exact generation is active. A
bootstrap ceremony cannot cite the installed generation, a successor cannot cite
the bootstrap materialization, and the governance candidate's broker/parser
bytes are inert subject data during their own round-ten review.
Round-ten provider qualifications and transport/raw facts are root-signed rows in
the immutable offline archive using preallocated registry/audience IDs; G2
imports and revalidates them byte-for-byte. TCB/A0 facts are preallocated in the
live registry and submitted through the root's closed evidence ingress.
The manifest requires:

- exact snapshot commit/tree, original-byte input manifest and before/after
  clean/read-only hashes;
- closed ceremony kind, exact requested authorization scope, subject kind/hash,
  predecessor authorization/manifest hashes and the stage-specific exact-path
  input manifest with a role on every entry;
- the exact scope-binding object and, for round ten, signed candidate-policy
  hash/max/variant/termination fields copied into decision/admission/authorization;
- exactly one entry for each closed perspective
  `crash-authority | backend-operator | repository-feasibility |
  false-success-adversary`;
- per entry: random nonce, externally allocated review-session and launcher-
  request IDs, canonical request-envelope/input-manifest/content-access-log
  roots, complete transport-turn root, local wire-send and provider acceptance/
  response receipts, provider qualification/trust domain, mandatory provider-
  returned request, response and resolved-model identities (provider session when exposed),
  supplemental provider-configuration hash, exact root/proxy/broker/launcher
  path/hash/version/argv, prompt and tool-schema hashes, exit/signal, raw
  transport/stdout/stderr paths and byte counts/hashes, normalized reviewer-
  output bytes/hash, findings and strict verdict;
- four distinct perspectives, nonces and review-session IDs, at least two
  independent provider/credential/transport trust domains, and four unique model
  classes keyed by `(providerTrustDomain, resolvedUnderlyingModelId)`.
  Session ID is not part of model-class uniqueness. A configuration hash is
  supplemental provenance and can never substitute for an unresolved underlying
  model ID. Local argv/config/model labels, assistant echo and client-minted IDs
  are expectations only: raw provider response metadata must return the request
  response and resolved model identities and match them. Request/response IDs are
  unique only within their provider trust domain through the normalized claim
  index, and every semantic turn in one slot keeps the same domain/model. Provider session is required
  only for a protocol that claims to supply it. Reusing a frontend is permitted only when the provider trust domain and
  resolved model class still differ; duplicate or undisclosed classes fail
  closed;
- `authorizing=true` only when all four entries exit cleanly, all identities and
  raw hashes verify, two independently implemented wrapper/schema auditors agree
  on every normalized object, every findings array contains zero CRITICAL/P1
  while its closed verdict is PASS, and an independent human/operator decision
  signs the four raw/normalized hashes plus verbatim canonical findings arrays.

Reviewer assistant content is exactly one closed `ReviewerOutputV1` JSON object,
not Markdown plus a magic last line. It echoes perspective, nonce, plan/input
bundle hashes, snapshot commit/tree, clean/read-only observations, provider
and resolved model plus the externally allocated review-session ID, and contains
a typed findings array with severity
`CRITICAL | P1 | P2 | NOTE` plus a closed verdict. Counts are derived from that
array; reviewers cannot supply trusted counts. The frozen adapter specification
extracts exactly one assistant object from each named CLI JSON/plain wrapper and
rejects extra unparsed assistant text, duplicate result objects, unexpected
stderr, malformed/truncated wrappers, a conflict between any marker and JSON,
or a PASS object containing a blocking finding. Raw output remains evidence but
is never searched by an ad-hoc candidate regex.

Each review starts in an empty external directory with CLI project-rule,
`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, skills, plugins, MCP, memory/resume, implicit context and
all general assistant tools disabled. Repository instruction files are ordinary
length-delimited subject entries, never system/developer control. One reviewed
read-only primitive, `read_review_input(entryId, offset, length)`, may return
only original bytes from the exact input manifest; it accepts no path, URL or
command, and every range/read hash appends to the exchange access-log root. The
OS sandbox denies subject execution, shell/subprocess launch, mutation and all
network except the recorder/proxy's provider transport.

`ReviewRequestEnvelopeV1` freezes ordered system/developer/user content blocks,
the untrusted-data delimiter rules, perspective, nonce, required full-read entry
set/ranges, exact broker tool schema, output schema, provider/model expectation,
context/output limits and no-truncation policy. Before send, the broker proves
the required plan/governance bytes fit or are fully addressable through the
content primitive. An authorizing result requires the access log to cover every
required byte. Each initial request and every later broker-tool result is a new
append-only `ReviewTransportTurnV1`: the admitted review root freezes/fsyncs the
exact canonical request bytes and included delivery IDs/ranges/hashes, records a
local wire-send receipt at the TLS adapter boundary, then preserves provider-
origin request/model/response metadata and raw bytes. The provider is not
fictionally required to echo a client hash it does not support: exact byte
delivery is an explicit trust claim of the operator-admitted local root, while
provider-origin metadata proves which remote request/response/model resulted.
The final slot/decision binds the full turn chain. A missing range, turn, local
send receipt, provider request/model identity, implicit truncation or
candidate instruction treated as control is rejection. Repository feasibility
may inspect any exact base-tree entry through the broker, while every perspective
must fully read the plan and governance core selected by the frozen routing
profile. A call to any other tool, candidate execution or undeclared entry is
structurally non-authorizing regardless of verdict.

The minimum implementable formal provider contract is
`http-json-response-id-model-v1`: the exact admitted adapter owns canonical HTTP
request serialization and TLS endpoint verification; locally seals bytes before
send; preserves response headers/body; requires a provider-origin unique request/
response ID and actual model ID in the response; and optionally uses provider
idempotency/query only when the endpoint's qualified API really supports it. If
the process dies after possible send and cannot recover the same response, the
turn/ceremony is ambiguous and terminal—never resent. A provider/CLI that hides
raw response identity or bypasses this adapter remains diagnostic. Endpoint
qualification uses live conformance vectors before the ceremony; if fewer than
four eligible model classes across two trust domains exist, formal review is
unavailable rather than locally attested as provider-origin.

The operator decision is a separate closed, signed object containing
domain/version, registry/project/checkout, the scope-specific authority/root/
activation binding, operator key ID
and generation, ceremony/run/full-history/equivalence root,
plan/bundle/snapshot identity, all raw artifacts and normalized-object hashes,
the full canonical findings arrays, derived severities, the two auditor-output
hashes, an explicit approve/reject value and one closed authorization scope
`a0-implementation-dispatch | bootstrap-tcb-staging-execution |
a0-merge-install | successor-control-bundle-update`. Round ten permits only the
first, the exact bootstrap-TCB ceremony only the second, the later A0 artifact
ceremony only the third and an installed-control ceremony only the fourth. The operator views the archived raw
objects outside either validator and signs with a key never exposed to the
governance bundle. A machine PASS, bootstrap key or signed empty summary cannot
stand in for this decision. This human key is the explicit irreducible bootstrap
trust root; later automated control remains bounded by what it signed.

Scope shape is one canonical `SignedReviewScopeBindingV1` closed `oneOf` shared
by ceremony, decision and authorization:

- `round10` requires the review-root admission/materialization, preallocated
  registry/project/checkout audience, `proposed_authority_epoch`, proposed
  program/lineage IDs and candidate policy. Current `authority_epoch`, BTS or
  installed-control activation/generation, lineage/program/run/current subject
  and successor IDs are mandatory null. Its consumption creates only the signed
  IDs; G2 activation is a separate typed evidence edge and never mutates scope.
- `bootstrap-tcb` requires the root admission/materialization, current authority
  epoch/BTS activation, lineage/program/run and exact pre-execution subject/
  context/history; source staging receipt and applicability binding are mandatory
  null because this authorization creates them.
- `bootstrap-a0` requires the same current bootstrap/program/run identities plus
  the non-null source staging receipt and mandatory applicability binding (first
  execution or reuse) with full exact subject/context/history roots.
  Installed-control and all proposed bootstrap IDs are mandatory null in both.
- `installed-successor` requires current authority, installed control generation
  and activation, successor update/current/target generation and its exact
  subject/evidence, plus dual-signed successor candidate policy, predecessor-
  global program, selected candidate, stable equivalence owner and acyclic
  complete-history freeze. Bootstrap root/BTS, bootstrap candidate policy/program
  and bootstrap proposed IDs are mandatory null.

Generic prose that “all decisions repeat run identity” never overrides this
scope-specific shape, and callers cannot add missing audience/generation fields
after signature.

The verifier converts an approved signed decision into one durable external
`review_authorizations` row only when scope, ceremony kind, exact subject hash,
parent-authorization set, operator key/nonce/expiry and signed-object hash all
match the closed schema. Scope equality is mandatory: an overbroad or narrower
decision is rejected as a whole and is never rewritten or downgraded into a
different authorization. A rejected decision creates no authorization.
Authorization state is orthogonal: `consume_state` is `available | consumed`
and `validity_state` is `current | expired | revoked | invalidated`;
`consumed` records exactly-once use and is not synonymous with currentness.
The registry uniquely indexes decision ID, decision signed-object hash,
operator-key/generation/nonce and exact consumed-by kind/ID, and permits at most
one `current` authorization for `(scope, subject kind/hash, canonical parent
set)`. Domain tags, schema versions and canonical object bytes are part of every
hash; caller-supplied aggregate hashes are always recomputed.

`isReviewAuthorizationCurrent(id, expectedScope, expectedSubject,
expectedConsumer)` is the only authorization predicate. On creation it checks
the approved decision signature, current operator key, unused nonce, unexpired
decision, exact audience/root materialization or control generation, exact
scope/subject/equivalence owner, a complete ceremony history in which every
predecessor is proven no-execution infrastructure-only, current provider
qualification dependencies, and the canonical complete parent set, then writes
the authorization plus the operator-key and every reverse-indexed dependency
edge in one registry transaction. The parent-role set and each edge's
lineage terminal are recomputed from this closed policy, never accepted from a
request:

| Scope | Authorization parents | Typed evidence dependencies | Consumer / required-until |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `a0-implementation-dispatch` | none | bound exact `bootstrap-trust-service-activation` and round-ten review manifest | one implementation program / that program's review-lineage terminal |
| `bootstrap-tcb-staging-execution` | exact implementation authorization | prior behavior-outcome root, exact TCB/A0/build/runtime/context manifest | exact run/staging context / `control-bundle-install-final-seal` |
| `a0-merge-install` | exact implementation + TCB authorizations | sealed staging receipt, complete context-execution + behavior-outcome + program roots, build/runtime/conformance and no-install evidence | exact materialization/installation / atomic final-seal transaction |
| `successor-control-bundle-update` | none in v1 | current installed-control activation, predecessor final seal, dual-signed successor candidate policy, predecessor-global program/equivalence owner/complete-history freeze, fresh successor review inputs, source-build, conformance, complete exact-cell fixture execution/outcome/applicability/receipt roots and distinct final update approvals | exact successor update/materialization/installation / its generic final-seal transaction |

The successor activation dependency is phase-typed rather than a permissive
OR. Its closed stages are `review-current-unconsumed | pre-fence-current |
handoff-owned | final-sealed | cancelled | invalidated`.
`review-current-unconsumed` is created with the review authorization and binds
the exact current activation ID/revision/fence, handoff-history count/root and
preallocated handoff ID, while proving that handoff does not yet exist.
Consumption revalidates those anchors, creates exactly that pending handoff and
CASes the dependency to `pre-fence-current` in one transaction; an intervening
handoff/history/activation change invalidates it rather than widening the
predicate. `pre-fence-current` requires the exact activation to
remain `current` with the one pending `current-bound` handoff. The atomic fence
transaction alone advances it to `handoff-owned`, which requires the exact
installation/handoff/fence and monotonic fenced/draining/closure chain;
`final-sealed` accepts only that successor seal. Cancel and invalidation are
terminal negative outcomes. A generic `current OR handoff` predicate, an
unrelated activation or an ordinary exit can never satisfy the edge.

`required_until` is a closed enum, not a caller timestamp: v1 permits only
`program-lineage-terminal` for the plan authorization and
`control-bundle-install-final-seal` for TCB/A0/successor parent, evidence,
provider, review-authority, operator, signer and root-admission edges. The former
resolves only to the exact program's `installed+final_seal_id` or explicit
invalidation; before program consumption it is the signed pending
`proposed_review_lineage_id`, and the consume transaction creates that exact row
rather than choosing one. The latter resolves only inside that exact generic
final-seal transaction.
Early receipt seal, authorization consumption, pointer update, executor exit or
wall-clock expiry cannot shorten either requirement.

The TCB staging attempt/receipt is an `execution` consumer, never its terminal
child. Once A0 materialization binds the exact installation, the lineage terminal
resolves to that installation's `control-bundle-install-final-seal`; every
intermediate phase revalidates the still-open TCB edge, and final bind alone
atomically writes its terminal consumer/seal (or explicit lineage invalidation).

Authorization parents occupy only `review_authorization_dependencies`; receipt,
history and report objects occupy `review_evidence_dependencies` with their
typed object IDs/hashes and reverse invalidation edges. Every edge points to the
same `review_lineage_id`; none may terminate at child authorization consumption
or receipt seal. On
consumption it repeats those checks for the leaf, requires the leaf
`consume_state=available`, every parent `consume_state=consumed` by the exact
predecessor object in this lineage, and rejects any non-`current` ancestor or
non-null invalidation fact. It CASes the leaf `available -> consumed`, records the trusted clock observation,
and creates the one
exact consumer in the same transaction. Lost acknowledgments observe that same
consumer ID; another subject or consumer writes nothing.

Provider qualification, review authority, root admission, operator key and every
receipt signer/key operation are not short-lived ceremony conveniences: each has
a typed edge with the same policy-computed terminal. Final bind enumerates the
complete required role set, revalidates every family, rejects orphaned/missing/
unbound signing operations, writes per-family counts/roots plus their aggregate
closure into the seal, and terminal-seals all edges/operations in the same
transaction. Any explicit pre-seal revocation/compromise invalidates the lineage,
advances its fence and persists reap intents. After seal, facts cannot rewrite
history, though a later compromise quarantines the current generation.

The dependency-family manifest has exactly seven ordered entries:
authorization, evidence, provider, review-authority, operator-key, signer-key and
root-admission. First install requires a nonempty root-admission edge root;
successor scope requires the canonical empty root/count zero. Direct admission
IDs never substitute for enumerating and terminal-sealing those edges.

Expiry is a deadline for creating the exact consumer, not a wall-clock recovery
selector. The bootstrap service accepts only a signed/pinned time source and
maintains `trusted_time_heads`; an observation below its persisted wall/monotonic
floor, beyond the qualified skew, or from another key/boot generation fails
closed. Once an available leaf is observed past expiry, that same transaction
monotonically records `expired`; clock rollback cannot revive it. Once a consumer
transaction proved the leaf unexpired, later elapsed time cannot split its
durable saga, and a consumed authorization does not age into expiry. Explicit
operator-key or authorization
revocation remains monotonic. Before the lineage's final installation bind, the
revocation transaction walks the operator→authorization,
authorization→authorization and authorization→consumer reverse indexes in the
same external registry transaction, marks every nonterminal descendant
`invalidated`, records the typed invalidation fact, fences any active
staging/install launch by incrementing its registry capability fence, persists
the exact reap intent, and moves its
attempt, receipt, later authorization or installation to `manual-conflict` (or
prevents creation when absent). Thus a consumed parent can remain a valid
historical predecessor only while it and its key were valid at consumption and
no explicit invalidation has occurred. After the exact installation is `bound`,
the lineage is sealed and grants no future operation. Routine key rotation or a
routine revocation recorded after that seal does not rewrite history. Revocation
facts have registry write sequence only—no caller backdating. A `compromise`
recorded before terminal bind invalidates it; one recorded after bind immediately
quarantines the current generation, denies all new capability/trusted reads and
requires offline authority without pretending the historical write order was
different. Audit records remain immutable.

Logical fencing is committed before the external reap effect: every privileged
registry/install operation rechecks that fence and is denied immediately, while
the launch guardian durably reaps the now-nonauthorizing process set. A crash
between fence and reap resumes only `reap-invalidated-review-consumer`; it cannot
restore validity or issue a receipt.

Round-ten authorization consumption and program creation are one transaction:
it consumes the plan authorization, creates one `a0_implementation_programs`
whose ID equals the signed `proposed_program_id`, plus the review lineage whose
ID equals `proposed_review_lineage_id`, and
appends the first program-history event. Ack loss returns
that same program by the authorization unique key. The signed candidate policy
sets a finite `max_candidate_runs`; a program admits at most one nonterminal run
and its signed max/variant/equivalence/termination fields are copied rather than
accepted from the caller. Reserving an ordinal consumes budget, including an
eventually `aborted-pre-go` run; the distinct-equivalence maximum equals the run
maximum and duplicate equivalence returns the existing verdict. A program cannot
extend its budget without a distinct operator-signed budget-chain object. The
extension may be consumed only with no active run, exact program revision/history
and positive old+delta=new arithmetic; it cannot change equivalence/variant/
termination policy, lower an ordinal, erase history or revive installed,
invalidated or manual-conflict state. Consumption also creates its operator-key
dependency edge through the final first-install seal.
Review FAIL, staging failure, abort and conflict remain append-only program
events. The final A0 review and installation bind the complete frozen program
history, never only the selected candidate.

Identity has three orthogonal canonical objects. `BehaviorSubjectV1` describes
only bytes and policy that can affect execution: exact target entrypoint, source/
artifact/runtime/loader/import closure, runtime input manifest, argv/environment
allowlist, readable mount manifest and behavior configuration. Its
`candidate_behavior_hash` excludes plan prose, reviews, sessions,
authorizations, run IDs, nonce and time. If governance/plan bytes become readable
runtime inputs they must enter the behavior closure. `QualificationContextV1`
binds the exact TCB/adapter/instrumentation/sealer, sandbox/principal/mount-release
policy, fixtures/evaluator/fault/sample policy and platform cell. `ReviewContextV1`
binds plan/governance/base/program/run, all three subject hashes, complete prior
program/behavior histories, parent/evidence sets and exact review input. Thus a
whitespace-only plan change requires a fresh review context but neither changes
behavior identity nor clears execution outcomes.

Each run begins `reserved` with a unique ordinal and null subject columns. One
all-or-nothing CAS changes it to `subjects-frozen`, writes exact TCB/A0 subjects,
behavior/context/review hashes and canonical subject set, and appends the program
event; partial/second freeze is rejected. An identical formal subject already
reviewed in this program cannot obtain a new ceremony/run to resample model
verdicts: `candidate_equivalence_hash` covers plan/governance/base and exact
TCB/A0/behavior/qualification while excluding run/history/session/nonce
allocation identities, and is unique within the program. Separately, the scope-
specific `formal_review_equivalence_hash` adds the exact frozen histories and
review inputs, excludes ceremony/session/nonce IDs, and is unique in the ceremony
registry. A used behavior/context pair returns its existing sticky execution
history and never starts another process. A genuinely changed trusted harness
may create a new context only with a fresh exact TCB authorization that binds the
prior behavior outcome root. Its result appends to the same behavior ledger: a
later PASS never overwrites an earlier FAIL/conflict, and final reviewers must
explicitly adjudicate the complete sequence.

Program states are `open | candidate-active | installing | installed |
budget-exhausted | invalidated | manual-conflict`, with recovery actions
`reserve-next-implementation-run | resume-current-implementation-run |
resume-program-installation | noop | noop | noop | diagnose-only` in that order.
Run states and recovery are:

| Implementation-run phase | Required state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | program owns the sole active run/ordinal; all subject fields null | `freeze-a0-implementation-subjects` |
| `subjects-frozen` | exact subjects/contexts/set and program event atomically frozen | `create-or-recover-tcb-review-ceremony` |
| `tcb-review` | one immutable ceremony/history owns this subject | `settle-exact-tcb-review-ceremony` |
| `staging` | one exact qualification execution history is bound or an old one reused | `drive-or-bind-exact-staging-history` |
| `artifact-review` | passing receipt plus complete execution/outcome/program roots frozen | `settle-a0-artifact-review-and-materialization` |
| `installing` | exact materialization/installation owns the selected run | `resume-exact-install-final-seal-saga` |
| `bound` | final seal atomically closed run, program and lineage | `noop` |
| `rejected` | immutable review/staging negative evidence appended | `settle-rejected-run-and-consider-next-ordinal` |
| `aborted-pre-go` | complete no-exec/reap evidence appended | `settle-pre-go-abort-and-consider-next-ordinal` |
| `manual-conflict` | freeze, lineage, evidence, launch or installation identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

Every post-round-ten ceremony, decision, authorization, staging execution/
outcome history, applicability binding, receipt, materialization, installation,
qualification, executor launch and final seal repeats the scope-required
program/run/subject/behavior/qualification/review identities and complete roots;
round ten instead binds its proposed program ID and null sentinels. Cross-run splice fails. `manual-conflict` never
opens a new candidate. A new plan authorization is required if plan/base/
governance, BTS admission or bootstrap activation drifts.

Bootstrap-TCB authorization consumption creates or reuses exactly one execution
history for the behavior/context pair. Every passing source receipt is paired
with a fresh `staging_history_applicability_binding` for the current
program/run/review context and TCB authorization, binds the immutable source
receipt's historical execution/behavior roots, proves that behavior root is an
exact prefix of the same scoped ledger, freezes the current full behavior and
program roots and binds a no-new-execution receipt for only the source behavior/
context. On first execution the source/current counts and roots are equal and
the prefix proof is the canonical identity proof; on reuse they may differ and
the old receipt is never relabeled. It then exposes both historical and current roots as typed evidence; a
later context suffix can never be hidden behind the old PASS and stales the
binding/formal equivalence.
A0 merge/install authorization can create only the materialization bound to both
parent authorizations, source staging receipt plus applicability binding, frozen
execution-history root, complete behavior-outcome root and full program root.
Every creation and pre-bind phase rechecks the revocation closure.

Before any provider call, one ceremony transaction freezes its run/subject/
parents/evidence/input/request profile and atomically creates all four
perspective exchanges with random review-session, launcher-request, reviewer
nonce and transport correlation keys. TCB/A0 creation requires its implementation
run already `subjects-frozen`. The transaction also creates a scope-specific
`formal_review_equivalence_hash` excluding allocation/run/session/nonce labels;
an existing verdict owner for that hash is returned instead of arming a resample.
Canonical request objects are immutable/fsynced before send.

A selective retry can never replace one perspective. V1 permits at most one new
complete generation and only when all four prior slots are terminal
`closed-no-provider-execution` and every turn has the typed, externally
verifiable no-send/no-provider-acceptance/no-model-execution/whole-job-reap/no-
late-send proof defined below. A signed
`ReviewRetryDecisionV1` binds the predecessor/root, closed infrastructure reason,
all four proofs, object domain/schema, registry/project/checkout and authority
audience, scope binding/review authority, formal equivalence, exact predecessor
and next four-slot sets, next run ID/generation/nonce, retry ordinal/maximum,
operator key/nonce, trusted issue observation and expiry. It has orthogonal
available/consumed and current/expired/revoked/invalidated states. One transaction
revalidates every field/proof/expiry and creates exactly the signed next whole
run; acknowledgment loss returns it.
Any possible send permanently consumes that semantic slot and makes it
ineligible for infrastructure retry. Exact same-request query/idempotency may
still finish the original turn; if it cannot recover that exact response, the
slot/ceremony is terminal nonauthorizing. An accepted request, provider response,
ambiguity or semantic finding can never be replaced by a new send; full history
must contain no substantive old output before authorization. Reclassifying
FAIL/P1 as “infrastructure” is structurally impossible.

The admitted transport proxy uses only a current provider qualification matching
audience, materialization, adapter/runtime/platform/API/credential trust domain,
expiry and revocation head. Every turn revalidates it. Exact request/delivery
bytes are sealed by the local wire-boundary receipt; provider-origin raw metadata
must independently supply a unique request/response ID and actual resolved model.
Uniqueness is normalized within provider trust domain across request and response
columns/turns, so two domains may legally emit the same raw string but one domain
cannot reuse it. The first semantic turn fixes the slot's trust domain, resolved
model and four-review model class; every later broker-tool semantic turn must
match. Provider query/idempotency recovery is recorded as recovery rather than a
new semantic turn. A routed/composite model requires a future explicit schema;
v1 rejects drift.
The local requested selector, stdout/stderr, resume hints, session stores,
assistant echo, aliases and wrapper-minted fields are diagnostic only.

Provider qualification freezes `pre_send_remote_visibility_kind` to
`none-before-release | provider-visible-precreation`. The first branch proves the
adapter cannot create any provider-visible request/session/idempotency state
before semantic release and supplies a current no-precreation observation for a
nonexecution proof. In the second branch, the transaction moves the turn to
`send-released` before the first remote precreation call; that call is already a
possible semantic send and permanently consumes the slot even if no later wire-
body receipt exists. A caller/recovery path cannot decide after a crash whether
provider query was “needed.” The kind and conformance receipt are copied into
the turn; mismatch or an unobservable provider precreation policy is terminal
nonauthorizing and never retry-eligible.

Slot, exchange and turn are independent closed recovery aggregates:

| Review-slot phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | exact ceremony/run/perspective/provider/model/content/nonce and exchange ID frozen | `activate-review-slot-exchange` |
| `exchange-active` | one exact current exchange owns all transport work | `reconcile-review-slot-exchange` |
| `response-bound` | final raw response/exchange identity bound; normalization/verdict pending | `normalize-and-settle-review-slot` |
| `settled` | exact semantic PASS or FAIL and complete exchange root terminal | `noop` |
| `closed-no-provider-execution` | complete externally verified no-send/no-acceptance/no-model-execution proof terminal | `noop` |
| `terminal-nonauthorizing` | send/acceptance/response/semantic ambiguity or rejection terminal | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | slot/provider/model/exchange/raw identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

| Review-transport-exchange phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | exact envelope/input/broker/proxy/provider/correlation and first-turn identity frozen | `materialize-first-review-transport-turn` |
| `turn-active` | one exact current turn/ordinal owns send or broker-tool continuation | `reconcile-current-review-transport-turn` |
| `final-response-bound` | final settled turn/raw response and complete input-access/turn roots frozen | `bind-review-transport-exchange-result` |
| `settled` | exact result bound to parent slot | `noop` |
| `closed-no-provider-execution` | every turn proves no send/acceptance/model execution | `noop` |
| `terminal-nonauthorizing` | semantic/transport ambiguity or rejected exchange terminal | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | turn chain/provider/raw/root identity diverged | `diagnose-only` |

| Review-transport-turn phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | canonical request/deliveries/correlation and blocked send-attempt IDs fsynced; no send capability | `reconcile-or-arm-review-turn-send-attempt` |
| `send-armed` | exact adapter child/job/GO nonce registered and blocked; no wire send | `reconcile-or-release-review-turn-send-attempt` |
| `send-released` | GO may be consumed; a second send attempt is permanently forbidden | `reconcile-possible-review-turn-send` |
| `wire-send-committed` | local TLS-boundary exact-byte send receipt durable | `reconcile-review-provider-acceptance` |
| `provider-accepted` | provider-origin request/session/resolved-model acceptance bound | `recover-exact-review-provider-response` |
| `response-captured` | preallocated raw object and fsync receipt bound; actor cleanup pending | `observe-review-turn-actor-exit` |
| `terminalizing-nonauthorizing` | possible-send/semantic/transport failure is sticky; actor capability fenced and cleanup pending | `fence-and-observe-review-turn-actor-exit` |
| `actor-exit-observed` | exact adapter/descendant exit set observed | `reap-review-turn-whole-job` |
| `actor-job-reaped` | whole job empty and principal retired; audit/no-late-send seal pending | `seal-review-turn-actor-audit` |
| `actor-audit-sealed` | complete actor/process/send audit and no-late-send receipt durable | `bind-review-transport-turn` |
| `containment-pending` | actor/provider/raw identity diverged while an actor may remain live | `contain-and-reap-review-turn-actor` |
| `settled` | exact turn/resulting chain hash terminal | `noop` |
| `closed-no-provider-execution` | no-send/no-acceptance/no-execution plus reap proof terminal | `noop` |
| `terminal-nonauthorizing` | failure is terminal only after actor exit/reap/audit/no-late-send seal | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | contained/reaped actor plus send/process/provider/raw/chain identity divergence | `diagnose-only` |

`reconcile-current-review-transport-turn` appends exactly the next ordinal only
after the current settled turn is a valid broker tool call; a final assistant
response enters `final-response-bound`, while an illegal tool or identity/model
drift is sticky terminal. If a qualified provider exposes real idempotency/query,
the same key may recover only the same request; otherwise any kill after possible
send and before durable response enters `terminalizing-nonauthorizing`, never
replay. Raw
response fsync followed by DB/ack loss queries only the preallocated object and
provider identity; it never scans for a convenient response. Tool calls create
another chained turn carrying the exact broker delivery results. Raw headers,
body, stdout/stderr and normalized object are immutable content objects with
size/media/storage receipt and lineage retention. Every exit, timeout,
malformed/rejected result and verdict settles preallocated identities; nothing
is deleted/reused. Missing/duplicate provider request/response/model identity,
per-slot domain/model drift, revoked provider qualification or request/nonce
reuse rejects the ceremony.
No turn becomes `settled`, `terminal-nonauthorizing` or `manual-conflict` until
its exact adapter job and descendants exit, the whole job/namespace is reaped,
the principal is retired and a complete actor/send audit plus no-late-send
receipt is sealed. Slot/exchange terminalization requires that terminal turn
closure. If identity diverges while cleanup is incomplete, only
`containment-pending` may run; diagnostic terminal state cannot abandon an actor.

These receipts prove which exact bytes the trusted local root sent, which ranges
it returned, and which provider-origin response/model came back. They do not
claim remote proof that the model semantically attended to or understood every
byte. That irreducible limitation remains explicit.

The bootstrap-verifier output names its own externally pinned artifact hash,
schema hashes, input manifest hash and every rejection reason. Unknown fields,
missing raw bytes, output normalization without both source/archive hashes,
unresolved model identity, reviewer/session reuse, majority-vote recovery, or a
legacy `dryRun:true`/`passed:true` object is structurally non-authorizing.
`check:state-architecture` validates these schemas and independently recomputes
all bytes; candidate plan-review code cannot supply the verdict parser or turn
diagnostic PASS text into authorization.
Before A0 exists, the offline bootstrap root freezes an immutable out-of-
repository review-governance subject containing all of those schemas, the parser
specification/schema, two independently implemented validator/raw-auditor
sources and executable artifacts with disjoint runtime/toolchain closures,
bundle manifest, the exact operator-admitted bootstrap review-root admission/
materialization manifest and courier/broker/transport/runtime closure, provider
protocol/qualification vectors, the complete candidate `BootstrapTrustServiceV1` source/
artifact/runtime closure enumerated above, credentialless adapter, external
instrumentation and closed receipt-sealer artifacts plus signing-operation
implementation/schema, normative
unprivileged control-coordinator, disposable install-executor and staging
sandbox/runner/oracle contracts
and threat profiles, and an adversarial review-
parser conformance corpus with expected authorize/reject results. It contains no
future control coordinator, install executor, runner, oracle or A0 executable
and therefore cannot authorize one. The service candidate is inert subject data during round
ten; only the exact admitted review-root materialization handles those four
provider exchanges and its authority is the explicit irreducible host choice,
not a model verdict about itself.
The round-ten operator decision schema fixes
`authorizationScope=a0-implementation-dispatch` and rejects any broader scope.
The generic qualification adapter is review infrastructure, not a control
coordinator or install executor: it can create only a disposable sandbox namespace, attach external
OS/filesystem/process instrumentation and emit unsigned diagnostics into the
bootstrap-service-owned write-once observation sink. A separate reviewed external
receipt sealer re-observes that sink and the protected attempt/job identities,
then signs only the closed observation object named by one pre-registered
signer operation. The adapter/staging principal has no signing key or generic
sign endpoint and no project/control-registry/install-root/pointer access,
no network and no method that can reserve, install or activate an artifact; the
external registry ACL rejects it independently of any candidate mode flag.

Signing is a durable registry saga, not a hash mentioned only inside a seal. The
registry derives the canonical unsigned object from protected dependencies and
creates one `receipt_signing_operations.phase=prepared`; callers cannot submit
arbitrary bytes. Its closed recovery is:

| Signing phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | exact purpose/object/schema/dependencies/key generation/fence and idempotency key are frozen; no signature | `submit-exact-signing-operation` |
| `signature-observed` | the exact HSM/signer response is durably verified against that object and key; bind may be unacknowledged | `bind-signed-object-once` |
| `bound` | exactly one seal/receipt references this operation and signed object | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | object/key/fence/dependency/signature or consumer diverged | `diagnose-only` |

The signer endpoint accepts only operation ID plus a single-operation capability
and reads the frozen object itself. Lost acknowledgment queries/replays the same
idempotency key and object; even if a randomized algorithm returns another valid
signature, registry CAS binds only one envelope. `signature-observed -> bound`
and creation of the observation seal/launch receipt are one registry
transaction. Key revocation, dependency invalidation or fence drift before bind
makes the operation nonauthorizing and schedules exact reap; adapter, TCB and
target never see the key or a generic signing method.
The
corpus covers a hidden P1 with PASS, conflicting markers, extra text, duplicate
JSON, malformed wrappers, unknown fields, raw/hash drift, dry-run fake PASS,
duplicate nonce/session/model/perspective, unresolved model identity, config-hash
fallback, missing local wire/request-model identity/input ranges, implicit project rules,
truncated request bodies, signer replay and missing stderr/input bytes. Round ten pins every raw hash and the
aggregate bundle hash. Both auditors must pass and agree on the corpus before
and after the four reviews. After bundle freeze, the admitted review root reveals a
previously committed random seed that generates metamorphic plan/bundle-hash
variants and wrapper mutations not knowable to a special-cased artifact at
build time. Their expected invariants come only from the declarative
schema/parser spec; disagreement is non-authorizing. Each closed output names
every schema/vector/artifact hash and rejection reason.

No opaque source/artifact pairing is accepted. Round-ten validators/auditors
and the generic qualification adapter/instrumentation must either execute the
exact reviewed source bytes under an interpreter/loader,
dependency and environment closure fully enumerated and hashed by the bundle,
or have at least two isolated builds from those source bytes produce a
bit-for-bit identical artifact. The latter binds build recipe, compiler/linker,
flags, container/base image, SBOM and runtime loader/dynamic-library/import
closure. The aggregate hash covers that provenance plus exact launch argv,
minimal environment and PATH-independent resolution, and the bootstrap verifier
revalidates the runtime closure before every execution. Conformance adds
source/artifact mismatch, corpus-special-case, PATH/loader/import substitution
and runtime-dependency drift fixtures.

After round ten authorizes and activates the exact bootstrap service, it creates a
separate immutable `bootstrap-tcb-authorization` bundle containing the exact
unprivileged control coordinator, disposable install executor and staging
runner/oracle sources, executable artifacts,
sandbox profiles, build provenance, SBOMs, runtime closures and qualification
vector definitions plus the exact candidate A0 tree/artifact/runtime identity;
it contains no live TCB-produced observation. Those executable components satisfy the same
source-as-executable or two-isolated-build rule and frozen mismatch/loader/
runtime-drift corpus. Four new model sessions review that exact bundle, both
auditors agree, and the operator signs its raw findings under
`authorizationScope=bootstrap-tcb-staging-execution`.

Only that exact staging scope can create staging state, and identity is split so
nonbehavioral review drift cannot reset evidence:

- `candidate_behavior_hash` is `SHA256("VA-BEHAVIOR-SUBJECT-V1\0" ||
  RFC8785(BehaviorSubjectV1))` over only the target entrypoint/source/artifact/
  runtime/loader/import closure, runtime inputs, argv/environment, readable
  mounts and behavior configuration. Platform and harness semantics are not
  smuggled into this key. Plan/governance prose, reviews, sessions,
  authorizations, nonces, time, run IDs and labels are excluded unless their
  bytes are actually readable by the target, in which case they enter runtime
  inputs.
- `qualification_context_hash` binds the exact reviewed TCB set plus adapter,
  instrumentation, observer/sealer, principal/environment, inert/coordinator
  fixtures, evaluator, fault and sample policy. It likewise excludes raw
  plan/governance/review identities.
- `review_context_hash` binds exact plan/governance/base/program/run/subject,
  parent/evidence/input and complete prior history identities, but never keys or
  clears execution history; ceremony run/session/nonce remain separate facts.

Consumption revalidates all three hashes, the exact behavior/context execution-
history root and the scoped behavior outcome root. Each behavior/context pair
has one attempt and sticky post-GO outcome; the same harness context may qualify
different behavior subjects without collision or evidence reuse. A materially
changed reviewed harness may produce a new context and one attempt for that
behavior only under fresh TCB authorization; before
launch it appends the prior scoped outcome root to its dependencies. The old
FAIL/conflict remains visible forever, a new PASS cannot replace it, and the
artifact reviewer must decide against the entire ordered behavior ledger. Plan,
governance, review, run or authorization churn alone returns the existing
context/history and creates no process. V1 has exactly one sample per stage per
context; unreviewed multi-sample/result-shopping policies are unsupported.

The creation transaction consumes the TCB authorization, creates or binds the
scoped behavior ledger/context execution history, creates the pair's sole attempt,
appends `attempt-reserved`, and CASes program/run to staging. The registry
allocates every execution ordinal and chains phase/attempt/process/raw payload
into that context root. At terminal context outcome it atomically appends an
event referencing that exact execution root to the behavior ledger. Both roots
cover aborts, reservation/arm/registration/mount/release/GO, observation,
pass/fail/conflict, receipt and freeze; candidate-computed roots are never used.

The attempt has three independently reaped stages:

| Attempt phase | Protected state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepared` | exact program/run/authorizations/behavior/context/review root frozen; no child | `arm-staging-inert-launch` |
| `inert-launch-armed` | current inert child is pre-GO under the nested machine | `dispatch-exact-inert-child` |
| `inert-running` | exact inert child is executing under the nested machine | `settle-exact-inert-child` |
| `inert-observed` | PASS seal, complete reap and namespace destruction bound | `arm-coordinator-fixture-launch` |
| `coordinator-launch-armed` | exact coordinator child is pre-GO against disposable fake registry/install roots | `dispatch-exact-coordinator-child` |
| `coordinator-running` | exact coordinator runs only against disposable fake registry/install roots under qualification-install principal | `settle-exact-coordinator-child` |
| `coordinator-observed` | full install/recovery method/fault fixture PASS, continuous effect audit, reap and namespace seal bound; production registry/root untouched | `arm-staging-target-launch` |
| `target-launch-armed` | fresh exact target child is pre-GO | `dispatch-exact-target-child` |
| `target-running` | fresh exact target child is executing | `settle-exact-target-child` |
| `target-observed` | target PASS seal, complete observation/reap/namespace seal bound | `seal-staging-launch-receipt` |
| `bound` | one signed receipt freezes this context execution root and appends its outcome to the registry/project/checkout behavior ledger | `noop` |
| `failed` | complete negative evidence freezes this context and appends sticky FAIL; it can never be rerun or hidden | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | identity, coverage, process/effect/history or revocation state incomplete/divergent | `diagnose-only` |

Every stage uses append-only child generations:

| Child phase | Protected/external state | Unique action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reserved` | namespace/job/observer/release identities allocated; namespace absent | `ensure-empty-staging-namespace` |
| `armed-empty` | observer coverage, empty pre-GO root/descriptor manifest and kernel process limit 1 durable; no subject bytes/handles | `start-blocked-staging-adapter` |
| `child-registered` | exactly one blocked adapter PID is owned; no descendant/fork/exec, subject mount absent | `authorize-exact-subject-mount` |
| `mount-authorized` | exact grant durable; same PID remains blocked | `attach-exact-subject-inputs` |
| `inputs-attached` | exact read-only closure mounted and verified; same sole PID remains blocked | `commit-execution-release` |
| `executing` | one release result durable; same PID execs exact first subject artifact and only then may frozen descendant policy open | `resume-staging-observation` |
| `observation-sealed` | complete externally signed raw stream/outcome/effect/reap/namespace seal exists | `bind-staging-stage-observation` |
| `pre-execution-aborted` | no subject mount/GO/under-review exec and exact whole-job reap proof bound | `noop` |
| `settled` | passing stage seal bound into context and behavior histories | `noop` |
| `failed` | negative stage seal bound into context and behavior histories | `noop` |
| `manual-conflict` | child/job/mount/coverage/GO/process/effect/reap not uniquely provable | `diagnose-only` |

Before release, the namespace contains only the reviewed adapter and an empty
root. Its argv/env contain opaque content IDs only—no target bytes, host paths,
memfd/inherited handle, loader/package cache, host `node_modules`, IPC or subject
descriptor. The external observer/mount broker/sealer remain outside the job.
The kernel process limit is one and the adapter cannot launch a shell/helper.
After registration, the mount broker persists the exact grant, attaches and
verifies only the approved read-only closure, then BTS-0 commits the child-bound
release result before unblocking. The same PID `execve`s the exact subject; it
does not spawn a second pre-GO process. Any early subject byte/access/process or
unexpected first exec is sticky conflict. Lost acknowledgment returns the same
grant/release result to the same child.

Only a generation with no subject mount, no GO, complete no-exec stream and
whole-job reap may advance to a new generation inside the same attempt. After
mount or GO, death is resolved from that generation's complete observation;
ambiguity is conflict and a negative result is failure, never a rerun. Observer
coverage begins before namespace creation and continues gap-free through every
process/effect, spawn-gate closure, whole-job reap and namespace destruction.
Continuous registry/filesystem/process/ACL auditing catches write-then-restore;
final snapshots are supplemental only. Each next stage requires the prior fresh
namespace fully reaped/destroyed and shares only content-addressed read-only
inputs.

The credentialless adapter forwards unsigned bytes to the bootstrap-service
write-once sink. The external sealer verifies protected identities, mount/
coverage/event/evaluator/effect/reap manifests and consumes the durable signing
operation above; TCB/target verdicts remain diagnostic. Lost acknowledgment
returns the already bound signed object.

The immutable A0 artifact-review subject contains the exact A0/TCB bytes, all
three observation seals, every raw/pre-GO abort record, this context's complete
frozen execution root, the complete scoped behavior-outcome root across contexts
and the full program history. Auditors enumerate each `1..N` and recompute it.
Receipt signing, operation bind and history freeze are one
registry transaction: freeze-first rejects another event; append-first stales
the review. A newly executed receipt repeats its producer program/run; a reused
receipt remains immutable and is paired with the current-run applicability
binding. Decision/authorization/materialization/installation repeat the current
program/run/subject set, behavior/qualification/review contexts, source receipt
identity, mandatory applicability binding, and all roots. Four fresh formal
exchanges, both auditors and operator scope
`a0-merge-install` must pass; a suffix, selected PASS or earlier/narrower scope
cannot substitute.

The same governance bundle is an input to all four reviewers, not an unreviewed
authorizer beside them. The separately signed operator decision prevents that
bundle from interpreting reviews of its own source into authority. A0's first review-governance change must install
byte-identical schema/parser/vector bytes at the named paths and reproduce the
external conformance result. Its exact implementation tree/control bundle and
bootstrap TCB must first receive their separate exact-scope authorizations; A0
is then activated only through the predeclared
`a0-trust-control-install` slot. Any hash or semantic drift leaves A0
unmergeable, avoiding a candidate-authored bootstrap parser.

A0 implementation dispatch consumes the round-ten plan manifest/operator
decision bound to the exact original plan-byte SHA-256 and review-governance-
bundle hash and exact implementation-only scope. A0 merge/install additionally
consumes the bootstrap-TCB staging authorization plus the fresh artifact
manifest/operator decision bound to the exact A0, unprivileged coordinator,
disposable executor and runner/oracle bytes and `a0-merge-install` scope. Each records
four unique model classes,
non-interactive command, mandatory resolved provider/model identity, executable
version, external review-session/launcher-request and provider request identity
(provider session when the qualified API exposes one) with trusted sources,
raw/normalized output hashes, verdict and
findings. The
required perspectives are crash consistency, backend portability/operator UX,
repository feasibility, and false-success adversary.

Any plan byte change makes all prior reviews stale. Missing/duplicate reviewers,
ambiguous output, CRITICAL, or P1 blocks dispatch. Review outputs and the merged
resolution ledger are committed under `docs/reviews/`. Disagreement is resolved
by an explicit decision record and re-review, never majority vote.

Rounds one through nine found blocking issues. Their ledgers are retained only
as non-authorizing diagnostic history; where raw transcripts or complete
manifests were not preserved, no identity/verdict claim from those rounds may
be reused as trusted evidence. Revision-ten through twenty preflight additionally
rejected task/goal lineage and trusted-read/ref-continuity predicates,
review-authorizer source/runtime/self-certification closure, purpose-specific
bootstrap/install/update recovery, staging sandbox/oracle and control-bundle TCB
gaps, including global target eligibility, repair fencing and orphaned Git ref
locks. Governance-bundle inventory then found that revision fifteen required
the future permanent TCB executable before plan approval, violating the
pre-implementation gate. Revision sixteen splits implementation-only plan
authorization from exact-artifact merge/install authorization, but preflight
found a remaining pre-authorization inert-fixture execution loop, narrative-only
scope persistence and substitutable raw staging evidence. Revision seventeen
adds the credentialless reviewed qualification adapter, durable exact-scope
authorization lineage, globally fresh sessions, one fenced staging attempt and
a signed exact-target launch receipt. Its exact-hash preflight nevertheless
found stale-parent/revocation gaps, spawn/GO-before-observation orphan windows in
staging and the privileged first-install coordinator, non-atomic implementation
subject freeze, and an ability to reset exact-subject failure history with a
fresh run/authorization. Revision eighteen adds orthogonal authorization
validity/consumption and reverse invalidation edges, all-or-nothing run binding,
a global content-derived staging history with sticky post-GO outcomes, durable
blocked-child/GO/observer/reap state machines for both staging stages, and a
durable fresh privileged launch aggregate. Its frozen exact-hash preflight still
failed: the round-ten TCB omitted the actual bootstrap registry/review/launch/
signing services; registry writer and final bind were not transactionally closed;
review transport could forge delivery/provider identity or selectively combine
runs; raw plan bytes contaminated the execution-history key; the privileged
installer could become permanent; and WorkspaceRoute did not cover the real
orchestration/write surface. One Grok `--check` response also emitted mutually
contradictory verdict/count objects; it is retained only as a negative strict-
parser conformance vector, never as a verdict.

Revision nineteen responded by explicitly admitting BTS-0 through the external
bootstrap host root, mechanically fencing its unique writer, separating
`Round10ReviewDecisionV1` from `BootstrapProgramAdmissionV1`, freezing complete
four-slot ceremony generations and provider-origin delivery, splitting behavior/
qualification/review identity plus execution/outcome/program histories,
enforcing empty-root delayed-mount same-PID release, replacing permanent
privileged installation with qualified disposable executors under continuous
external audit, sealing first install in one registry transaction, and upgrading
WorkspaceRoute to per-command effect capabilities. Its frozen bytes
`cf06502b31ae544b85a763980153834378a0d6e5d28e5de8955c8794b661fcd0`
nevertheless failed every independent exact-hash preflight. Findings included an
unmaterialized bootstrap review root, G1 activation/authorization recursion,
whole-ceremony result shopping and missing multi-turn wire proofs, incomplete
provider/signing currentness, writer recovery authority gaps, qualification and
per-action install crash gaps, incomplete multi-generation audit/final seal,
behavior/context key collisions and old-receipt applicability contradiction,
missing real command profiles/route target facts, and pre-seal target execution.
The structured Grok diagnostic also reported FAIL, but its raw wrapper emitted
multiple contradictory intermediate JSON objects and is therefore itself only a
strict-parser negative vector.

Revision twenty materializes the exact operator-admitted bootstrap review root;
uses locally sealed wire turns plus real provider-origin response/model identity;
allows only signed no-execution whole-ceremony retry; makes operator/provider/
signing audience and currentness explicit; splits activation G1 from review/
authorization G2; closes recovery-writer authority; adds qualification, action,
audit, principal, target-launch and full install-history machines; scopes
behavior/context composite histories with fresh applicability bindings and a
formal-review equivalence key; and makes route profiles/targets exhaustive and
recoverable. All earlier results remain diagnostic only. Revision twenty must
pass fresh exact-byte preflight before it can become the formal round-ten
bootstrap candidate. Its frozen bytes
`e4827bc99a9369b5bd8fa6aabfd2241d06c20c1fa0166348b68d6770b9c0bd17`
instead failed three independent stable-hash preflights with an aggregate
`CRITICAL 0 / P1 12 / P2 7`. The blockers were unsigned caller-selectable
candidate budget, impossible round-ten post-activation fields, provider-turn
identity/model drift and dependency lifetimes, missing executor-generation/
principal/history/repair closure, an incomplete post-seal target launcher,
first-install-only sealing of successor updates, non-recomputable target-denial
evidence and RouteSpawn path routing without syscall confinement.

Revision twenty-one responds with a signed `CandidatePolicyV1` and extension
chain; scope-timed review `oneOf`; domain-normalized per-turn provider identity;
final-sealed provider/review/operator/signer/root dependency families; a
non-recursive core→descriptor→admission→materialization→decision/archive DAG;
orthogonal executor/action generations with sticky qualification and anti-fork
histories; explicit principal/repair/target-launch closure; qualified target-
execution guard events/checkpoints; a generic first/successor final seal; and
OS-enforced route-spawn sandboxes plus pre-route/argv authority. All prior
verdicts remain diagnostic. Its frozen bytes
`4122625b4ff8e2ba0b4d33fce575e824eca3394940f9fc393389fa0b614de1de`
failed three independent stable-hash preflights with aggregate `CRITICAL 0 / P1
13 / P2 3`: crash-authority `0/3/2`, false-success `0/2/1`, and repository-
feasibility `0/8/0`. The remaining blockers were qualification PASS replacement
versus stable negative scope, incomplete post-seal launch/audit/revocation and
repair/quarantine closure, missing first-run applicability/root-admission/TCB
terminal evidence, RouteKernel/non-Git/DocStore/RouteSpawn/guard gaps, successor
handoff currentness, a cyclic first-install historical anchor and inconsistent
intent/generation/repair inventories.

Revision twenty-two responds by moving the minimum same-registry RouteKernel to
A0; adding opaque non-Git identity, trusted pre-route launch/RPC and full
DocStore/RouteSpawn member/audit machines; separating generation-local PASS from
stable cross-authorization negative qualification; keeping the target guard
continuous through a one-use launch-one handoff; closing every post-seal
serving/early-exit/restart/invalidation cleanup boundary; sealing complete repair
and writer-quarantine histories; requiring first-run identity applicability,
seven-family dependency roots and TCB edges through generic final seal; freezing
pre-wire retry authority; adding transitional successor handoff/service closure;
and making final-seal→historical-anchor signing acyclic. The generated state-
machine inventory and fault annex now require exact phase/action/schema equality.
Its frozen bytes
`e20f2be7bb2b165b480a36d0ebfd5c61d1b5e9e6e69a3ba8c1e6f7f927590285`
failed fresh exact-hash preflight with aggregate valid findings `CRITICAL 0 /
P1 7 / P2 2`: crash perspectives found pre-fence handoff/activation conflict,
dead-serving writer action ambiguity, repair-owned guard/generation leaks and
unclosed resume/dead-letter repair; repository feasibility found missing
existing-repository init, normalized pre-route authority rows and complete
DocStore public-writer disposition. Both independent false-success reviews were
`0/0/0`. One external repository report merely listed the intentionally
unimplemented A0 artifacts as defects; it preserved useful baseline facts but
was rejected as an out-of-scope architecture verdict.

Revision twenty-three responds by keeping activation current until the atomic
handoff fence; arming and later cancelling/reaping its closure audit explicitly;
making dead-serving recovery use disposable observation generations before
`exit-observed -> reaped -> claim`; deriving mutually exclusive resume phases
from a closed registry classifier; terminalizing target guards/streams in
abort/supersede; adding repair-owned predecessor generation restoration;
closing typed dead-letter repair with sticky histories, exact successor
authority and one positive predicate; preserving existing Git/non-Git `init .`
plus zero-write dry-run; normalizing every pre-route parameter/target/spawn
member; exact-matching the packed DocStore writer graph; and separating its
pre-effect transaction intents from append-only results. Intermediate targeted
draft `d3bfae237398cc2679d1f8aae1ec4b9559441399d1158df379d48de76be20738`
failed `CRITICAL 0 / P1 6 / P2 3`; those findings also produced the explicit
unconsumed successor-dependency phase and mode-specific repair disposition now
present there. Its frozen bytes
`0dac08d380e388d8c35afffe7229707ca18958e624a0f60c582dd0048f9aae60`
failed fresh exact-hash preflight across five valid read-only reports with raw
aggregate `CRITICAL 1 / P1 9 / P2 4`. The blockers were dead `claimed`/`draining`
registry writers and competing exit-CAS ownership; unclosed review transport and
umbrella recovery faults; real DocStore migrate argv and published SDK/package-
resolution compatibility; successor static-review and task/goal verifier result
shopping; and the missing canonical commit-approval aggregate/public-command
profile bridge. A Composer output was not retained and one stalled Kimi run
returned only an identity preamble; neither was counted as a verdict.

Revision twenty-four responds by giving all three active registry phases one
outcome-discriminated reconcile action and one recovery-owned exit CAS; closing
review slot/exchange/turn send/acceptance/fsync recovery; splitting every mixed
bootstrap/DocStore/dead-letter/settled fault row; exact-mapping public argv to
internal profiles while preserving DocStore 0.2.1 migrate spellings; replacing
silent SDK export removal with an inventoried capability-gated deprecation
window; introducing a predecessor-global signed successor candidate program;
making completion verification one-owner/one-attempt with full-history freezes;
and inserting a canonical stale-aware commit-approval manifest/head and ordered

also makes successor verdict ownership independent of caller change-class and
qualification allocations; separates through-review prefixes from terminal
successor history roots; gives review retry typed per-turn no-send/nonexecution
proofs; adds stable completion obligation heads; separates ref-level commit
batch identity from run/cycle with immutable members, first-seen execution order
and shared-tree snapshots; routes SDK/hook/automatic invocations explicitly;
protects the package-wide 0.2.1 resolution surface; and assigns history-rewrite
authorization to A2 with C1 exact-tip re-proof. Revision twenty-four
frozen at exact original-byte SHA-256
`686da289f0e0624f22d8b4629b45f4bf519af877db9e69de128e0b183b32bf42`
(8,531 lines; 666,534 bytes) and failed fresh exact-hash preflight across five

`0/5/3`, false-success `1/0/0`, repository feasibility `0/4/1`, Kimi `0/2/0`
and Composer `0/6/2`. The blockers were cross-kind task/goal verifier and
negative-obligation bypass, run-scoped goal heads, pre-registration child crash
windows, response/effect actors terminalized before exit/reap/audit, Git ref-only
binding without real worktree/index publication or unborn genesis, provider
pre-send visibility, package/DocStore baseline drift and missing B1/B2b fault
contracts. The Grok diagnostic corroborated several package/export gaps but
emitted multiple contradictory objects and could not independently recompute the

Revision twenty-five responds with stable cross-run goal heads and cross-kind
completion owner/obligation namespaces; result→exit→whole-job-reap→audit→terminal
verifier and review lifecycles; late-registration barriers for RouteSpawn and
pre-route children; provider-specific pre-send visibility; closed successful
outbox actor cleanup; preallocated successor final-seal intents; corrected clean
detached package/DocStore baselines; deterministic B1 and transactional B2b
contracts; real human/automatic approval source, policy, decision and signing
bindings; exact hook-chain isolation; and a five-part Git ref/reflog/tree/
worktree/index publication saga with SHA-1/SHA-256 unborn genesis. Its later
draft closures add structured RouteFS link/rename receipts, complete publication-
owner histories, a broker writer fence through final external revalidation,
acyclic authority/verification/cleanup settlement receipts, a post-commit
trigger, snapshot-backed signed goal baselines and complete task/goal settlement
slices. Its latest draft replaces an impossible SQLite/backend issuance CAS
with per-capability monotonic backend-slot sagas, inert prepare and bind-gated
activation, exact GO/mailbox delivery, intent-before-effect terminalization,
post-tombstone actor barriers and complete lost-ack query histories. Intermediate
exact bytes `d637abfe13ff2aa9fd3e1af81292eba241d47b827b1fc46c4ca6edb6f5a726a1`
(11,679 lines; 916,877 bytes) failed three internal exact-hash perspectives with
three independent P1s: selected-before-prepare was unreachable, late-admission
authority was only a naked hash, and a pre-final control-only successor could
not satisfy the current-broker barrier. Grok's exact-byte `0/0/3` diagnostic was
overturned by those executable counterexamples and is nonauthorizing. The
post-review draft closes selected-but-unissued actor stages with an explicit pre-prepare
phase and authenticated superseded-action dispositions; binds terminal before-
state/predecessor/outcome selection into every direct/query result; makes every
writer allocation/binding/prepare/activation/authorization/delivery contend
with one CAS-closed actor-slot admission head; and carries the origin drain
barrier through a gapless control-only broker continuity chain across pre-final
or release-lost-ack successors. The resulting exact bytes
`12bd351b86498d346d18c796a90d19ea7d102ed9c3aa3d27f463d0f775b4f8b9`
(11,994 lines; 939,622 bytes) still failed exact-hash review with `CRITICAL 0 /
P1 6`: channel/mailbox drain authority remained naked; an in-place demoted
writer had no legal allocation branch; control-reservation semantics were
undefined/cyclic; final revalidation ignored historical control allocations;
a successor could die before continuity and consume an unaccounted generation;
and future writer-generation heads could close before global drain. Grok's
exact-byte `0/0/0` response missed those executable counterexamples and is
retained only as a nonauthorizing diagnostic.

Revision twenty-five's post-review draft separates generation continuity from attempt
outcomes: one non-reopening broker-generation head and contiguous claim chain

rather than mutable saga phase. Final revalidation binds the exact current

Round nine preserved all four raw outputs but failed. Before A0
exists, round ten uses the exact operator-admitted immutable
`BootstrapReviewRootMaterializationV1`, not candidate code. It assigns a random
nonce to each reviewer, verifies plan and repository-tree hashes, rejects
dry-run/echo/custom fake reviewers, preserves raw output, and recomputes the
merged ledger through both reviewed auditors. The independent operator then
directly inspects and signs the canonical raw findings decision; without that
signature the manifest is non-authorizing. The bootstrap exception,
governance-bundle hash and human/bootstrap trust-root hashes are explicit. After A0, the
schema/verdict logic moves into the external control plane and is itself
trust-controlled.

The bootstrap review replaces the dirty-worktree input with a detached snapshot. The
external verifier materializes the declared Git tree read-only, injects only the
plan/ledger files and external governance-bundle files enumerated by
original-byte SHA-256 into a declared review-only namespace, and rejects every
other undeclared untracked/modified file. It hashes all inputs before and after
review. Each reviewer must validate both plan and governance bundle and emit the
closed JSON identity/verdict. The manifest records reviewer perspective,
command, executable/model identity, independent session, exit status,
stdout/stderr/normalized hashes and parser result. A0 consumes this external
plan manifest only as permission to begin implementation; it cannot produce its
own prerequisite, and the plan manifest cannot authorize merge/install. The
later artifact manifest uses a fresh detached implementation snapshot and the
same raw-preservation rules.
Original-byte SHA-256 is bootstrap identity; semantic canonical hashes are only
diagnostics.

Snapshot inputs are exact path sets, not broad role grants. Every ceremony uses
a canonical `ReviewInputEntryV1` array whose entry contains normalized relative
path, closed role, source namespace, original-byte SHA-256, byte size, file mode,
Git blob/object identity when applicable, and explicit symlink/hardlink metadata.
The base Git tree is expanded to every entry; injected files are individually
listed. Globs, directory-only entries, implicit descendants and “all files of
this role” are forbidden.

Roles are still closed per ceremony. Round ten permits only individually named
base-repository, plan/ledger and governance-bundle entries. Bootstrap-TCB review
additionally permits individually named exact TCB source/artifact/provenance,
sandbox/vector and A0-target entries. A0 artifact review additionally permits
individually named parent authorizations, sealed staging receipt/history and raw
observations, derived report/build/SBOM/runtime entries and exact A0/TCB bytes.
The materializer verifies normalized-path and case-fold uniqueness, rejects
Unicode/case aliases, device/FIFO entries, undeclared links and any symlink or
hardlink escape, then proves exact set equality, role, mode, object and bytes
before launch. After review it repeats the same set/byte check. An extra,
missing, replaced or merely category-compatible path makes the ceremony
non-authorizing.

D1 wires deterministic PR-safe commands into `check:all`; multi-hour and full
platform profiles remain required nightly/release evidence rather than silently
running inside every local PR gate.

The raw-byte hash of `state-fault-manifest.json` is pinned in the external A0
bootstrap/control registry. Changing or deleting a scenario is a trust-control
change requiring previous-supervisor plus human approval. Nightly/release fault
and soak manifests bind the same hash or an approved strict superset.
Fault IDs are never generated at runtime. Any source-level parameterized family
is deterministically and finitely expanded during A0 schema freeze into one
literal manifest row per phase/boundary, with expansion count/root and generator
artifact hash in `check:state-architecture`; the pinned raw manifest contains
each resulting literal ID (including every `A0-INSTALL-GEN-PHASE-*` row).
Runtime runners may select only those literal IDs and reject an unknown,
unexpanded or duplicate ID, so a favorable subset cannot satisfy a template.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `A0-WORKSPACE-01` | any sprint-board/init/plan/recover command receives an isolated `--state-file` while sibling output-path flags are omitted | every derived artifact stays under that workspace or the command rejects before writing; integration worktree/hash set is unchanged |
| `A0-WORKSPACE-02` | state, board, journal, pitfall, meta or history arguments, including `--meta-file`, resolve to mixed workspace/integration roots | path-coherence validator rejects the command before its first write; `fail-closed`, including isolated `--state-file` plus integration-root `--meta-file` so crash/retry can never create dual meta writers |

| `C1-TASK-00` | open task completion draft before terminal transaction | exact settled saga/settlement composite, released writer fence plus broker-retirement closure, mode-specific complete transition root, head/ref and slots are re-evaluated without another semantic verifier; `evaluate-task-completion` |
